failures.title: Lesson buttons required a long precisely-placed press
failures.symptom: Nick reported every button in the lesson flow needed a long held press and only registered a tap in one specific spot rather than anywhere on the button.
failures.root_cause: mobile/src/components/ui.tsx built every pressable as an outer Animated.View carrying a native-driven press-scale transform wrapping an inner Pressable carrying the touch handler. On RN 0.86 with Fabric (New Architecture), the transform visually repositions the button while Fabric hit-tests against the pre-transform layout, so only the sliver where the stale and current bounds overlap ever registers a tap -- a known regression class, facebook/react-native#57502.
failures.fix_summary: Collapsed each Animated.View+Pressable pair into a single AnimatedPressable (Animated.createAnimatedComponent(Pressable)) so the transform and the touch handler live on the same node.
failures.no_test_reason: No automated UI/gesture test harness exists in this repo (no test runner is configured); confirmed via TypeScript compilation and by reasoning against the documented Fabric bug, not on a physical device by the agent.
failures.prevention_notes: Never split an Animated transform from the Pressable it visually wraps onto two separate nodes on this RN version; apply the transform directly to the Pressable/AnimatedPressable itself.

failures.title: Lesson generation blocked the whole request on one large completion
failures.symptom: Nick reported test/lesson generation and regeneration felt slow, especially over a network connection.
failures.root_cause: The per-objective guess/teach/fade/solo lesson content was produced by one Anthropic completion of up to 6000 tokens, run synchronously in the GET/POST request path with no streaming and no early return -- measured at ~31 seconds on a real objective.
failures.fix_summary: Split generation into two prompts (guess+teach, fade+solo) run concurrently with Promise.all, and return guess+teach as soon as ready instead of waiting on both; the fade/solo half keeps generating in the background via next/server after() and lands in the cache once done.
failures.no_test_reason: No automated integration test harness exists for this route (no test runner is configured); verified live end to end against a throwaway seeded test account and the real Anthropic API instead.
failures.prevention_notes: For any single-request AI generation whose fields aren't all needed at once, prefer returning the part the UI needs first and completing the rest in the background over one large blocking completion.

failures.title: Regenerating a lesson reliably returned near-identical material
failures.symptom: Nick reported that hitting Regenerate lesson did not produce different material from what was already there.
failures.root_cause: lessonGenerationPrompt built its prompt only from the track/unit/objective titles -- identical on every call -- and callClaudeJSON was never given a temperature override, so asking again with an unchanged prompt reliably came back close to word-for-word the same content.
failures.fix_summary: Regenerate now looks up the objective's current cached teach/fadeProblem/soloCheck and feeds it back into the prompt as an explicit do-not-reuse-this instruction, and both generation calls now request temperature 1 instead of the API default.
failures.no_test_reason: No automated test harness exists for this route; verified live end to end against a throwaway seeded test account, comparing the regenerated teach/fadeProblem/soloCheck text against the pre-regenerate row in Postgres and confirming all three changed.
failures.prevention_notes: A regenerate/retry action against an LLM needs an explicit anti-repeat instruction (and ideally a higher temperature) fed from the previous result -- an unchanged prompt is not enough to guarantee different output.

failures.title: Split lesson-generation token budgets were too tight for verbose objectives
failures.symptom: GET/POST on a real hardware-procedure objective (laptop battery/keyboard/wireless-card replacement) returned a 500 with 'Claude did not return valid JSON, stop_reason=max_tokens' on every retry.
failures.root_cause: When REQ-062's single ~6000-token completion was split into two smaller calls, the per-half maxTokens values (1500 for guess+teach, 4000 for fade+solo) were set by proportionally shrinking the old combined budget rather than re-checking headroom per half. A multi-step safety-procedure objective's teach field alone exceeded 1500 tokens, truncating the JSON mid-string; because the prompt and inputs are deterministic, every retry failed identically rather than flaking.
failures.fix_summary: Raised maxTokens to 4000 for the guess+teach call and 6000 for the fade+solo call -- real margin above the old combined 6000-token ceiling for the full ten-field response, not a proportional split of it -- and confirmed the same objective generates cleanly on both GET and POST.
failures.no_test_reason: No automated test harness exists for this route; caught and confirmed fixed via live testing against a throwaway seeded test account and the real Anthropic API, deliberately including a known-verbose objective rather than only simple ones.
failures.prevention_notes: When splitting one generously-budgeted AI completion into several smaller ones, budget each half with real margin above what it alone might need -- do not divide the original ceiling proportionally between them. Test against a worst-case-verbose real input, not just a typical one, before trusting a new token ceiling.

failures.title: Regenerate could serve stale pre-regenerate content while the new version was still generating
failures.symptom: In a live test, a GET fired immediately after a POST regenerate (before the background fade/solo generation had finished) returned the old, pre-regenerate lesson content instead of the new one or a pending state.
failures.root_cause: The route checked whether a cached row already existed before checking whether a generation was already in flight for that objective. On first-time generation that ordering is correct (no row exists yet), but on regenerate an old row already exists on disk until the background job's upsert overwrites it, so the existing-row check short-circuited and returned the stale version.
failures.fix_summary: Reordered both GET and POST to check the in-flight-generation map first and await it if present, falling back to the cached-row check only when nothing is in flight.
failures.no_test_reason: No automated test harness exists for this route; caught and confirmed fixed via live testing: POST regenerate followed immediately by GET, with the database row inspected directly to confirm the fresh content (not the old row) was what came back both times.
failures.prevention_notes: When a cache can be invalidated by a background job rather than synchronously, check for an in-flight replacement before checking the cache itself -- checking the cache first assumes it can never be stale, which is only true for a first-time write, not a regenerate/overwrite.

failures.title: Biometric unlock toggle never appeared in Settings on Android
failures.symptom: The Face/fingerprint unlock toggle in the Settings screen never rendered, with no error shown anywhere in the app; reported unresolved across multiple sessions since at least 2026-09-26.
failures.root_cause: expo-local-authentication ships a config plugin (plugin/withLocalAuthentication.js) whose entire job is injecting android.permission.USE_BIOMETRIC and USE_FINGERPRINT into AndroidManifest.xml during expo prebuild/EAS build. It was never listed in app.json's plugins array, so it never ran and no native build ever carried those permissions. Without them, hasHardwareAsync/isEnrolledAsync fail on a real Android device, so isBiometricAvailable() resolves false (or its promise rejects), biometricAvailable in AuthContext.tsx stays at its false default, and the toggle -- gated on that flag in settings.tsx -- never renders. A second bug compounded the silence: the mount-time isBiometricAvailable().then(setBiometricAvailable) call in AuthContext.tsx had no .catch(), so any thrown error vanished with nothing logged.
failures.fix_summary: Added expo-local-authentication to app.json's plugins array so the next native build injects the Android permissions. Added .catch() logging to both mount-time biometric calls in AuthContext.tsx so a future failure of this kind is visible instead of silent.
failures.no_test_reason: No automated test harness exists in this repo, and this is a native-manifest-level behavior that can only be observed on a real device with a fresh native build -- not reproducible against the dev server or a simulator without biometric hardware enrolled.
failures.prevention_notes: Installing an Expo SDK package that ships its own config plugin (an app.plugin.js / plugin/ directory) is not enough -- it must also be listed in app.json's plugins array, or its native-side mods (permissions, Info.plist keys, manifest entries) never run. Check for a plugin/ directory whenever adding a new native-capable Expo package. Also: never leave a mount-time async call with no .catch() when its failure would otherwise be invisible -- silent failures here look identical to 'the feature was never built.'

failures.title: In-flight generation dedup only covered the practice half, not the intro half
failures.symptom: Immediately re-calling prefetch-next for the same objective returned status started twice in a row instead of in-flight the second time -- caught on literally the second call in live testing, not a rare race. A real GET for the same objective landing during that window ran its own independent intro generation, producing different guessPrompt/teach text than what the original prefetch's intro produced, with whichever call's practice phase happened to run first silently determining what actually got cached.
failures.root_cause: The prior pendingPractice map was only set once the intro half had already resolved (inside startPractice), so the entire intro-generation window -- often 10+ seconds, close to half the total generation time -- had no dedup at all. Any second caller in that window saw nothing in the map and started its own competing generation.
failures.fix_summary: Replaced the practice-only pendingPractice map with pendingGeneration, claimed synchronously in a new ensureGeneration() the moment a caller decides to generate -- before either the intro or practice promise is awaited anywhere. Any caller checking the map after that point, even on the very next microtask, sees the claim.
failures.no_test_reason: No automated test harness exists in this repo; caught and confirmed fixed via live testing -- immediately re-calling prefetch-next now correctly returns in-flight, and a real GET racing an in-flight generation now returns the single shared result instead of a second independently-generated one.
failures.prevention_notes: Any in-flight-dedup map must be claimed synchronously at the point of the decision to start work, not lazily once some later sub-step completes -- claiming late leaves every step before that sub-step completely unguarded, and that window can be most of the total duration, not a rare edge case.

failures.title: Sonnet 5's default adaptive thinking consumed max_tokens with no visible output
failures.symptom: A GET on a real, verbose objective (a multi-step hardware safety procedure) returned a 500: Anthropic response had no text content block, stop_reason=max_tokens, blocks=[thinking]. The model was still thinking when its token budget ran out and never produced any answer text at all.
failures.root_cause: Claude Sonnet 5 runs adaptive thinking by default even when the thinking parameter is never set -- confirmed against the claude-api skill's model reference, not assumed. Thinking tokens count against the same max_tokens ceiling as the actual answer, and how much a given prompt makes the model think is not predictable or capped by this code. For deterministic JSON content generation, that budget is pure downside.
failures.fix_summary: Added a disableThinking option to callClaude/callClaudeJSON/callClaudeStructured that sends thinking: {type: disabled} -- explicitly accepted by Sonnet 5 per the model reference -- and set it on both lesson-generation calls, since this is content generation, not a reasoning task.
failures.no_test_reason: No automated test harness exists in this repo; caught and confirmed fixed by regenerating the exact same objective that failed and getting a clean 200 with no error in the server log.
failures.prevention_notes: Never assume omitting an API parameter means a feature is off -- check the current model reference before relying on a default, especially for a model newer than this assistant's training cutoff. For a deterministic structured-generation task, explicitly disable thinking rather than trusting whatever the model's default happens to be.

failures.title: Prompted free-text JSON was occasionally syntactically invalid despite a clean stop_reason
failures.symptom: A GET on the same verbose objective later failed again with stop_reason=end_turn (not truncated) but Claude did not return valid JSON -- the visible text looked complete and well-formed, but JSON.parse still rejected it. This was the third distinct raw-JSON failure mode hit in this same code path across the session (after mid-string truncation and the pure-thinking-no-text case), each with a different cause.
failures.root_cause: The lesson-generation prompts asked Claude to write JSON as free text ("Produce ONLY a JSON object...") and callClaudeJSON parsed whatever text came back. The model occasionally wrote a literal, unescaped newline inside a string value (e.g. a paragraph break in the teach field) instead of the escaped two-character sequence JSON requires, which is syntactically invalid JSON even though the model considered its own response complete.
failures.fix_summary: Replaced prompted free-text JSON with the Anthropic API's structured outputs feature (output_config.format via the SDK's zodOutputFormat helper and client.messages.parse()), which constrains the API's own generation to schema-conforming JSON rather than parsing free-hand text after the fact. Defined lessonIntroSchema/lessonPracticeSchema as Zod schemas in lib/prompts.ts (the LessonIntroContent/LessonPracticeContent types are now derived from them via z.infer, removing a previous hand-maintained duplication) and added callClaudeStructured in lib/anthropic.ts. Added zod as an explicit dependency (was only present transitively via the SDK's optional peer dependency).
failures.no_test_reason: No automated test harness exists in this repo; caught and confirmed fixed by regenerating the exact same objective and getting a clean 200, and again on a second full round of testing across both the plain GET/POST path and the prefetch path with zero errors.
failures.prevention_notes: Prompting a model to write JSON as free text and parsing it afterward is inherently fragile -- three different failure shapes came out of the same prompted-JSON pattern in one session. Prefer the API's native structured-outputs / schema-constrained generation for any new JSON-shaped call instead of prompting-and-parsing; callClaudeStructured in lib/anthropic.ts is the reusable path for this. callClaudeJSON's other two callers (app/api/grade/route.ts, app/api/pbq/route.ts) were not touched by this fix and remain exposed to the same class of failure -- worth migrating them the same way if it comes up there.

failures.title: Course dashboard Overall progress bar always showed 0%
failures.symptom: The Overall progress bar and percentage on the course dashboard (mobile/app/(app)/course/[trackId]/index.tsx) always read 0%, no matter how many objectives a user had mastered, while the same track's card on the Explore/Home list correctly showed the real percentage. The per-unit progress bars further down the same dashboard were also correct.
failures.root_cause: GET /api/courses/[id] selected only subject_tracks.* and never joined view_track_progress, so the API response had no percent_complete field at all. The mobile client reads track.percent_complete ?? 0, which silently rendered a plausible-looking 0% instead of surfacing the missing field. GET /api/courses (the list endpoint) joins view_track_progress correctly, which is why only the dashboard was wrong.
failures.fix_summary: Joined view_track_progress into the GET /api/courses/[id] query (same total_units/total_objectives/mastered_objectives/percent_complete columns the list endpoint already selects), so the dashboard now gets the real value instead of falling back to 0.
failures.no_test_reason: No backend test harness exists yet in this repo (.ai/test-suites.json is empty); verified by comparing the updated query's output against view_track_progress directly via the Supabase MCP connection.
failures.prevention_notes: Any endpoint returning a subject_tracks row for display should join view_track_progress the same way GET /api/courses does, rather than re-deriving progress ad hoc or letting a fallback default mask a missing column.

failures.title: Overall progress and mastery were the same metric everywhere
failures.symptom: Every 'progress' indicator in the app (course dashboard's Overall progress bar, Explore/Home course cards, the Home continue card) actually showed the mastery rate -- percent of objectives at Independent/Transfer-ready -- not how far a learner had gotten. An objective sitting at Introduced or Guided, clearly worked on, still read as 0% progress.
failures.root_cause: view_track_progress only ever computed one number, percent_complete, filtered to Independent/Transfer-ready mastery statuses. Every screen that wanted to show 'how far along is this course' had nothing else to read, so it read that mastery number and labeled it progress -- there was no separate concept of started-but-not-mastered in the data model at all.
failures.fix_summary: Added started_objectives/percent_progress to view_track_progress, counting any objective with a mastery row at all (mastery rows are only ever inserted once an objective is attempted, per backend/app/api/objectives/[id]/mastery/route.ts, so a row's existence means 'touched' regardless of status). Repointed every headline progress bar/percentage at percent_progress; left everything explicitly labeled mastery (Mastery matrix screen, per-unit 'at Independent+' captions) on the original percent_complete/mastered_objectives. Renamed the dashboard's 'Progress' quick action and the progress.tsx screen's header to 'Mastery' so the two no longer collide under the same word on one screen.
failures.no_test_reason: No backend test harness exists yet in this repo (.ai/test-suites.json is empty); verified against live data via the Supabase MCP connection, where percent_progress and percent_complete now visibly diverge (e.g. Security+: 5.6% vs 0.0%), plus a clean tsc --noEmit in both backend and mobile.
failures.prevention_notes: Progress (has this been touched) and mastery (has this been learned well) are now separate columns in view_track_progress; any new UI element needs to pick the one it actually means rather than reaching for whichever percent field happens to be on the object.

failures.title: Lesson-generation prompt claimed the app auto-picks answer format
failures.symptom: lessonPracticePrompt's system message (backend/lib/prompts.ts) told Claude 'the app decides per visit which one to show based on track record' when generating fadeProblem/soloCheck, describing a proficiency-gated auto-selection feature that doesn't exist. A comment directly above CheckStep in the mobile lesson screen made the identical false claim.
failures.root_cause: Both were written against an early design intent (auto-pick format by track record) that was never implemented; the actual shipped behavior -- the learner freely toggles MC/free-response themselves, every time, via CheckStep's mode buttons -- was built later without updating either the generation prompt or the comment to match.
failures.fix_summary: Rewrote both to state plainly that the learner picks the format every time, so fadeProblem/soloCheck and their MC counterparts must each stand as complete, independent questions rather than one being treated as primary.
failures.no_test_reason: Prompt wording change with no schema/behavior change; verified by re-reading the full prompt file for any other instance of the same claim (none found) and confirming lessonIntroPrompt/pbqGenerationPrompt never made it in the first place.
failures.prevention_notes: When a described-but-unbuilt feature (auto-selection by track record) is dropped in favor of a simpler shipped one (user choice), grep for its description in both code comments and generation prompts, not just the code path itself.

failures.title: Chat history sent the oldest 40 turns, not the newest
failures.symptom: Once an Ask-the-coach thread passed 40 messages, the model stopped seeing anything recent: replies ignored the last few turns and answered as if the conversation were still at its start.
failures.how_detected: code review during the 2026-10-08 app-wide sweep
failures.root_cause: POST /api/chat built history with 'order by created_at asc limit 40', which keeps the first 40 rows ever written, not the most recent 40. The comment next to it said 'capped to the most recent 40' so the intent was clear and the query simply did the opposite; nothing exercised a thread long enough to notice.
failures.fix_summary: Subselect the newest 40 by created_at desc, then re-order ascending for the model.
failures.no_test_reason: Query-level fix against a live Postgres table; no DB test harness exists yet (REQ-080 only covers pure modules).
failures.prevention_notes: When a comment says 'most recent N', the query needs desc+limit then a re-sort; asc+limit is the oldest N.

failures.title: Errors PATCH and sessions PATCH had no authentication; mastery PUT had no ownership check
failures.symptom: PATCH /api/errors/:id and PATCH /api/sessions accepted unauthenticated requests and matched rows by id alone, so anyone with an id could resolve another user's spaced-review entries or end their study session. PUT /api/objectives/:id/mastery authenticated but wrote a mastery row for any objective id, owned or not.
failures.how_detected: code review during the 2026-10-08 app-wide sweep; confirmed with curl (unauthenticated PATCH now returns 401)
failures.root_cause: The three handlers predate requireUser (REQ-era single-user app) and were never swept when auth was added; the GET handlers in the same files were updated and the PATCH/PUT ones below them were missed.
failures.fix_summary: requireUser on all three; every update scoped by user_id; mastery PUT verifies the objective belongs to one of the caller's tracks.
failures.no_test_reason: Route-level auth against a live DB; verified by curl, no HTTP test harness exists yet.
failures.prevention_notes: When adding auth to a route file, grep every exported handler in it, not just the one being worked on.

failures.title: Catalog was copied per user; new accounts saw zero courses
failures.symptom: Any account other than the one the seed ran under had an empty Home and Explore. The seed also overwrote that account's display_name to 'Pak' on every run.
failures.how_detected: found during the 2026-10-08 sweep; confirmed by creating a throwaway account via the API and seeing zero tracks
failures.root_cause: subject_tracks rows were created with the seeding user's id (single-user-era design), and GET /api/courses filtered on st.user_id = caller. Favorites were a boolean on the track and the progress views joined mastery with no user filter -- all three assumed one user per track copy. The seed's upsert of app_users set display_name unconditionally.
failures.fix_summary: Catalog tracks have user_id null and are visible to everyone (ownedOrCatalog predicate); course_favorites per-user table; per-user LATERAL rollups in lib/progress-sql.ts replace the views in routes; seed adopts the legacy owner's copies in place (same ids) and no longer touches app_users.
failures.no_test_reason: Verified live over HTTP with a throwaway account against the dev server (see REQ-082 changelog); no HTTP test harness exists yet.
failures.prevention_notes: Any new query touching subject_tracks must use ownedOrCatalog(), never st.user_id = caller alone; any rollup must bind m.user_id.

failures.title: Seed failed on fitness tracks: examRevision over varchar(100)
failures.symptom: npm run seed exited 1 after the PT tracks with 'value too long for type character varying(100)' and no indication of which row or column.
failures.root_cause: credential_exams.exam_revision is varchar(100) (migration 007); two fitness tracks carried 109- and 123-character revision strings. The seed prints progress per track but not the failing field.
failures.fix_summary: Shortened both strings under 100 chars.
failures.no_test_reason: Seed-only data; the type system can't see Postgres column widths.
failures.prevention_notes: exam_revision / standard_revision / objectives_revision are varchar(100): keep revision strings to a short label, put the long provenance note in the file comment instead.

failures.title: Aortic dissection objective overgeneralized definitive repair
failures.symptom: The first mitigation wording implied that every acute aortic dissection proceeds to definitive repair.
failures.root_cause: The objective carried the type A surgical pathway into all dissections instead of preserving the ACC/AHA distinction: uncomplicated acute type B starts with medical therapy, while type A needs immediate repair and complicated type B needs intervention.
failures.fix_summary: Kept the anti-impulse objective neutral about definitive management and appended a separate objective distinguishing type A, uncomplicated type B and complicated type B pathways.
failures.no_test_reason: This is sourced clinical curriculum content rather than executable behavior; validation is source-to-objective review against the 2022 ACC/AHA aortic disease guideline plus the append-only objective-position check.
failures.prevention_notes: For clinical treatment objectives, check management branches and exceptions in the Tier 1 guideline before compressing them into one objective.

failures.title: Full catalog seed interrupted by Supabase pooler drop
failures.symptom: The idempotent full-catalog seed terminated partway through with 'Connection terminated unexpectedly' before reaching the CCRN and MSHI tracks.
failures.how_detected: npm run seed during release validation
failures.root_cause: The long-running seed relies on one external pooled PostgreSQL connection across the 94-course catalog; the remote pooler dropped that connection during the run.
failures.fix_summary: Stopped retrying the broad live mutation and used a one-time append-only helper restricted to the four exact missing objective positions; it refused updates or mismatched existing rows. A read-only live count then confirmed all four course totals.
failures.no_test_reason: The drop is an external transient connection failure; the requirement-level regression evidence is the append-only snapshot comparison and live objective-count query.
failures.prevention_notes: For small live catalog additions, use an append-only operation scoped to exact missing positions and verify counts; do not use a broad updater as a workaround.

failures.title: Production build initially blocked by restricted Bash execution
failures.symptom: npm run build failed before compilation with Bash/E_ACCESSDENIED.
failures.root_cause: The build starts a Bash-based Expo web export, and the restricted execution environment could not launch that shell.
failures.fix_summary: Reran the unchanged production build with approved execution access; Expo export, Next.js compilation, TypeScript and static generation completed successfully.
failures.no_test_reason: This was an execution-environment permission failure, not application behavior; the successful full production build is the regression evidence.
failures.prevention_notes: Run the production build in an environment permitted to launch the repository's Bash export step.

failures.title: Progress counts compared as strings
failures.symptom: Continue/sidebar could treat a 9-of-10 unit as complete and skip it
failures.root_cause: pg returns bigint count() and numeric as strings; API passed them through; app compared with < as text
failures.fix_summary: Global INT8/NUMERIC type parsers in backend/lib/db.ts
failures.prevention_notes: Integration test asserts every rollup column is a JSON number

failures.title: No CI check that migrations apply or that production schema matches code
failures.symptom: Code depending on migrations 023/027a could deploy to a database without them and fail with 500s; CI stayed green
failures.root_cause: CI ran typecheck/unit tests/build only, with a placeholder DATABASE_URL; migrations are applied manually and separately from deploys
failures.fix_summary: Database CI job; schema probes in /api/health and npm run migrate -- --status
failures.prevention_notes: New migrations that code depends on get a probe in lib/schema-status.ts; CI requires all probes to pass on a fresh schema

failures.title: Single-use auth secrets could be used twice concurrently
failures.symptom: Concurrent refresh with one token minted several live tokens; one backup code, challenge, reset link or email link could create several sessions or changes
failures.root_cause: Select-then-update consumption with no guard on the update
failures.fix_summary: Guarded update ... where unused returning, inside transactions
failures.prevention_notes: Race tests fire 5 concurrent consumes and require exactly one success; they failed against the old code

failures.title: Routes skipped visibility checks on shared catalog
failures.symptom: Lesson-adjacent, grade, PBQ, chat and sessions routes accepted ids from other users' private tracks; catalog agent could write private tracks
failures.root_cause: Acknowledgement gate silently returned for invisible tracks and was treated as an access check
failures.fix_summary: lib/visibility.ts checks before work, 404 when not visible
failures.prevention_notes: One shared visibility helper; tests cover another user's private track

failures.title: One learner's regenerate replaced the shared lesson for everyone
failures.symptom: Regenerate on a catalog track changed every learner's lesson and reset their saved place; no rate limit
failures.root_cause: lesson_content keyed only by objective and overwritten by POST after the catalog became shared (REQ-082)
failures.fix_summary: Per-learner overrides, rate limit, cross-instance claims
failures.prevention_notes: Tests assert another learner's lesson and saved place are untouched

failures.title: PBQ simulator lost scenario and answer on navigation
failures.symptom: Leaving the PBQ screen and returning showed the unit picker; a long answer was gone
failures.root_cause: Scenario/answer/result held only in component state; API cannot re-fetch a scenario by id
failures.fix_summary: Per-user, per-unit snapshot in AsyncStorage storing the full scenario
failures.prevention_notes: Same save/restore pattern as lesson progress; parse rules unit tested

failures.title: MFA backup codes lost if the screen was left any way but Done
failures.symptom: Header back, swipe or hardware back discarded codes shown only once
failures.root_cause: Codes held only in state; no leave guard and no copy/share
failures.fix_summary: beforeRemove confirmation, Copy and Share buttons
failures.prevention_notes: Leave-guard decision logic unit tested

failures.title: Lesson marked complete after a wrong Solo answer
failures.symptom: A wrong Solo answer landed on Objective complete with a green check; the correct option was never shown after a miss
failures.root_cause: Done screen ignored the solo verdict; graded view hid the choices
failures.fix_summary: Outcome derived from the stored solo result; graded choices stay visible
failures.prevention_notes: Done-state and choice-marking logic are pure and unit tested

failures.title: Lesson routes skipped the access check
failures.symptom: GET/POST lesson and prefetch-next served or generated lessons for objectives in another user's private course
failures.root_cause: Batch B split the routes between two engineers; the lesson routes belonged to the regeneration pass, which wasn't asked to add visibility, and the access pass was told not to touch them
failures.fix_summary: visibleObjective check before any read or generation, 404 otherwise
failures.prevention_notes: Route-level regression test; when work is split across engineers, the lead re-checks the seams (blast-radius item in pre-completion)

failures.title: Guided step earned Independent and Transfer-ready in one sitting
failures.symptom: A correct free-response Guided (fade) answer gave Independent; Guided plus Solo minutes apart gave Transfer-ready
failures.root_cause: suggestStatus looked only at format and verdict, never at stage or time, and status came from the latest answer alone
failures.fix_summary: mastery_from_attempts (migration 029): only unassisted Solo free-response successes lift status above Guided; Transfer-ready needs two at least 24 hours apart
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-integrity.dbtest.ts::1. Guided work does not earn Independent or Transfer-ready
failures.prevention_notes: Mastery is decided in one SQL function from the whole attempt history, covered by DB tests that fail on the old code; the teaching-quality audit reviewer re-checks mastery rules

failures.title: Reopened lesson allowed full-credit resubmission
failures.symptom: After the answer was shown, reopening the objective and typing the same answer gave Independent
failures.root_cause: Nothing tracked that an item had been answered (and its answer revealed); every attempt counted as unassisted
failures.fix_summary: A second answer to the same item (same stage and server-held question) is recorded assisted=repeat and can't lift mastery above Guided
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-integrity.dbtest.ts::2. A reopened lesson can't be resubmitted for full credit
