failures.title: MFA leave guard blocked sign-out and lock
failures.symptom: On the backup-codes or setup view, logout, session expiry, background sign-out, biometric lock or web idle sign-out were cancelled by the beforeRemove guard; choosing 'Keep this screen' left the codes visible on a signed-out or locked device.
failures.root_cause: The guard only looked at the MFA view, not at why the screen was being removed. Auth-driven removals go through the same beforeRemove event as a back tap.
failures.fix_summary: Guard takes the auth status and never blocks when not signed in.
failures.prevention_notes: Any beforeRemove guard must let auth-driven navigation through.

failures.title: API client had no request timeout
failures.symptom: A hung request (weak signal, captive portal) left screens spinning forever with no way to retry; a hung progress fetch blocked lesson resume.
failures.root_cause: rawRequest called fetch with no AbortSignal and nothing else bounded the wait, so a stalled connect or body read never settled.
failures.fix_summary: AbortController per request; 15 s default, 180 s for model-backed routes (chat, pbq, grade, objectives/:id/lesson*, guess-feedback), per-call timeoutMs override; timeout throws RequestTimeoutError (plain Error, not ApiError, never retried by the 401 path). Avatar upload and data export use 60 s.
failures.prevention_notes: Every request now goes through one bounded path; new long-running routes must be added to MODEL_ROUTES or pass timeoutMs, which the route-default test documents.

failures.title: Native background sign-out fired while a share sheet or picker was open
failures.symptom: On Android without biometrics, sharing backup codes to another app (or picking a photo, exporting data) took longer than the 1.5 s grace period and the learner came back signed out.
failures.root_cause: Android reports background for any activity Ascendra itself launches; the grace period only absorbed brief permission dialogs, and nothing told AuthContext an outbound flow was open.
failures.fix_summary: withBackgroundHold opens a bounded (2 min) hold around Share and ImagePicker calls; the background timer waits for the hold; returning to active or settling without ever backgrounding ends it.
failures.prevention_notes: Any new flow that opens another app must wrap it in withBackgroundHold (documented in AuthContext and backgroundHold.ts).

failures.title: Web back, refresh and tab close skipped the backup-code leave guard
failures.symptom: On web, the browser back button, refresh or closing the tab discarded backup codes shown once, with no prompt.
failures.root_cause: expo-router answers browser back with navigation.resetRoot, which never fires beforeRemove, and unload never reaches React Navigation; the guard only listened to beforeRemove.
failures.fix_summary: While backup codes are shown and signed in: beforeunload asks the browser to confirm; a capture-phase popstate listener stops the router's listener, steps forward again, and asks; I've saved them goes back for real.
failures.prevention_notes: Leave guards on web must cover browser history and unload, not only beforeRemove (comment in webLeaveGuard.ts).

failures.title: Support form kind read from the URL only once
failures.symptom: A later kind param change on a mounted Support screen (popping back with another kind, a deep link, web back/forward) left the other form showing; Submit a ticket carried no params so it could count as the same screen.
failures.root_cause: kind was initialised from useLocalSearchParams in useState and never synced; the sidebar's ticket entry had no explicit kind.
failures.fix_summary: An effect switches the form when the kind param changes; chips write the param with setParams so the URL always names the form; the sidebar passes kind=ticket.
failures.prevention_notes: Screens that take a mode from params must follow param changes, not only the first value.

failures.title: dismissTo could land on another course's dashboard
failures.symptom: With Course B, ..., Course A, Lesson B in the stack, popping to /course/B landed on Course A's screen with its params swapped to B, dropping the history in between.
failures.root_cause: POP_TO matches the nearest route by name only and every course dashboard shares one route name; planNavigation's in-stack check compared exact paths, so it found Course B deeper down and chose dismissTo.
failures.fix_summary: dismissTo only when the nearest stack entry with the target's route is the target itself; otherwise push. planCourseReturn added for the lesson screen's Back to course (wiring deferred to the lesson rewrite).
failures.prevention_notes: Planner compares against the nearest same-route entry, matching how the router resolves POP_TO.

failures.title: Sent support ticket restored as a draft
failures.symptom: Leaving Support while a ticket was sending left its draft stored; the next visit offered the already-sent ticket again, inviting a duplicate.
failures.root_cause: The form was cleared only after the request succeeded; if the screen had unmounted by then the clear never reached storage.
failures.fix_summary: Fields are emptied before the send (the draft hook then removes the stored entry); on failure they come back unless new text was typed, and if the learner left or switched form the sent text is written back to that form's stored draft.
failures.prevention_notes: Same clear-then-restore shape as chat; documented at the call site.

failures.title: Failed Try another scenario wiped the graded PBQ
failures.symptom: If fetching a new PBQ scenario failed, the graded result was gone and the old scenario came back blank; answering again recorded a second attempt under a new id.
failures.root_cause: generate() cleared answer, result and the attempt id before the request instead of after a scenario arrived.
failures.fix_summary: pbqAfterGenerate replaces the state only on success; the Try another button shows loading and Change unit is disabled while busy.
failures.prevention_notes: State that a request replaces is replaced on its success, not before it.

failures.title: History filter showed a stale response
failures.symptom: Switching answer-history filters quickly could fill the list with another filter's attempts.
failures.root_cause: Each filter change started a request and every response was applied, so whichever answered last won.
failures.fix_summary: createLatestRequest tickets; only the newest request applies its response or error.
failures.prevention_notes: Reusable latestRequest helper for any filter-driven fetch.

failures.title: Web share cancel showed an error; copySecret rejection unhandled
failures.symptom: Cancelling the browser share dialog showed Couldn't open sharing; a denied clipboard in copySecret produced an unhandled rejection.
failures.root_cause: navigator.share rejects with AbortError on cancel and every rejection was treated as failure; copySecret had no try/catch.
failures.fix_summary: isShareDismissal ignores AbortError (backup codes and data export); copySecret shows Couldn't copy on failure.
failures.prevention_notes: Share call sites use isShareDismissal.

failures.title: Drafts and progress left on the device after logout
failures.symptom: Chat, support and PBQ drafts and lesson positions stayed in AsyncStorage/localStorage after Log out and Log out of all devices.
failures.root_cause: Logout only cleared tokens; nothing enumerated the per-user ascendra.draft/pbqProgress/lessonProgress keys.
failures.fix_summary: logout (also used by the web idle sign-out and account deletion) and logoutAll remove that user's keys, block draft writes for that user until they sign in again, and sweep once more after 2 s for the lesson screen's direct writes. The native background sign-out and token expiry keep drafts.
failures.prevention_notes: New per-user storage keys must use one of the three prefixes or be added to localDataOwner.

failures.title: 029 recompute test committed the old mastery rule into the shared test database
failures.symptom: After migration 031, mastery tests saw 029 levels (Independent where 031 gives Transfer-ready) and pg_proc showed 029's mastery_from_attempts installed
failures.root_cause: mastery-recompute.dbtest re-runs the 029 file, which CREATE OR REPLACEs mastery_from_attempts with the 029 rule and commits it for every parallel test file; wrapping it in a transaction was not enough because the documented restore block it executes contains its own begin/commit, which committed the outer transaction early
failures.fix_summary: The 029 test runs on one dedicated connection inside one transaction rolled back in after(); the restore block is executed without its begin/commit lines (asserted present); a schema probe fails if mastery_from_attempts is not the 031 version
failures.prevention_notes: Any test that re-runs an older migration must run it in a rolled-back transaction and strip embedded transaction control; the 031 probe makes a reverted rule fail migrate --status and /api/health

failures.title: Mastery depth came from one question type only
failures.symptom: PBQs and multiple choice never influenced mastery, and two spaced Solo free responses made Transfer-ready: depth was measured on words only
failures.root_cause: The 029 rule counted only unassisted Solo free-response successes; PBQ attempts have no objective so they were excluded entirely, and there was no notion of accuracy, assistance credit, spacing weight or decay
failures.fix_summary: Migration 031: weighted-accuracy model over every assessment type with tunable weights; graded PBQs recompute the unit's studied objectives live
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-integrity.dbtest.ts::1. Guided work does not earn Independent or Transfer-ready
failures.prevention_notes: Every weight and threshold lives in mastery_model_params / assessment_types; DB tests pin one-format, one-sitting, assisted, spacing and decay behaviour

failures.title: Exam readiness could not tell unpracticed from weak and showed a score on thin evidence
failures.symptom: Readiness was the blueprint-weighted share of objectives at Independent or above; a learner with a few perfect answers and the rest unpracticed got the same kind of number as a learner who had tried everything
failures.root_cause: examReadiness (mobile) used only mastered counts per unit; no coverage, no accuracy, no evidence gate
failures.fix_summary: Server-side readiness (lib/readiness.ts) from per-objective weighted evidence, blueprint-weighted, with coverage and accuracy separate and a coverage gate; plain-language display on the dashboard and mastery matrix
failures.prevention_notes: Status is not_enough_evidence below readiness_min_coverage and the app shows no percentage then

failures.title: Coach could give away answers to unanswered items and took learner text as instructions
failures.symptom: Ask the coach would answer the open Solo or PBQ question outright if asked, and the learner message went to the model unfenced
failures.root_cause: The chat route knew nothing about the learner's open items and sent the message as a bare user turn; the prompt had no rule against solving ungraded work
failures.fix_summary: lib/coach-guard.ts finds open lesson, PBQ and review items server-side, names them to the model by question only, fences learner turns, adds on-topic and encouraging-tone rules, and checks the reply against open answer keys with one retry then a server-written hint
failures.prevention_notes: Answer keys never enter the chat prompt; tests use a mocked model client so they run without an API key

failures.title: Lesson screen copy still describes the 029 Transfer-ready rule
failures.symptom: Lesson screen (line ~582) tells an Independent learner to come back tomorrow and answer a fresh question to reach Transfer-ready; under 031 that needs a second format (e.g. a PBQ) on a separate day
failures.root_cause: The hint text was written for the 029 rule; the lesson screen is owned by a parallel batch (REQ-101) and was deliberately not edited here
failures.no_test_reason: Copy change belongs to the lesson-screen batch; handed off to the lead
failures.prevention_notes: When a mastery rule changes, grep the app for user-facing text that restates it

failures.title: One unidentified DB test failure in one full run, not reproduced
failures.symptom: npm run test:db reported 116/117 once (first run after a fresh migrate and double seed); the failing test name was not captured, and 13 later full runs (including one from a fresh database) passed 117/117
failures.root_cause: Most likely FAIL-088: the only failure seen in 24 further full runs was lesson-regen's lease test, a timing race that fails only under load and is the kind of one-off that went unnamed here. The move to --test-concurrency=1 does not explain it on its own: run 4 of 12 failed with files serial. It does remove the other candidate (the 029 and 031 re-run tests holding row locks from a global recompute while other files grade), since no other file runs while those transactions are open. The failing test was never named, so this attribution is inferred, not proven.
failures.fix_summary: FAIL-088 fixed the lease race; test:db runs one file at a time (FAIL-112). Merged suite before the fix: 11 of 12 runs passed (one FAIL-088). After it: see the b4-align commit message for the 12-run count.
regression_tests: backend/lib/lesson-regen.dbtest.ts::cross-instance generation claims::a GET waits for the learner's own regenerate running elsewhere
failures.no_test_reason: Not reproduced; capture the TAP log on the next occurrence
failures.prevention_notes: Keep TAP output from test:db runs so a one-off failure is named (all 24 b4-align runs were kept).

failures.title: Weighted mastery (031) trusted a stored assisted = false
failures.symptom: On the merged branch, attempts written with assisted = false by pre-029 code (repeats of the same item, hints revealed before the answer, Solo multiple choice) earned full credit and counted as format evidence under 031; integrity tests 'a repeat stored with assisted = false is still a repeat' and 'a hint recorded before the answer counts' failed once 031 replaced the 029 rule.
failures.root_cause: 031 was written against the first version of 029, whose rule read attempts.assisted. PR #22's review moved 029 to deriving repeats and hint reveals from history (FAIL-110); 031 replaced mastery_from_attempts wholesale and so dropped that guarantee.
failures.fix_summary: mastery_detail derives each direct answer's assist from history with the same precedence as assistReasonFor(): stored flag, Solo multiple choice (hint), lesson_hint_reveals at or before the answer (hint), an earlier answer to the same stage and question (repeat). Unit PBQs keep their stored flag.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-model.dbtest.ts::031 keeps 029's guarantees::a repeat or a Solo multiple choice written with assisted = false scores as if flagged (FAIL-082)
backend/lib/mastery-model.dbtest.ts::031 keeps 029's guarantees::a hint revealed before the answer counts even when the attempt says unassisted; one revealed after does not (FAIL-082)
failures.prevention_notes: A rule that replaces mastery_from_attempts must re-run the 029 guarantee tests (mastery-integrity.dbtest.ts section 10) against itself; the merge surfaced this because those tests run against whatever rule is installed.

failures.title: Weighted mastery (031) returned no row for no evidence, so self-set levels survived
failures.symptom: mastery_from_attempts returned nothing for a pair with no direct evidence; recompute_mastery()'s lateral join then skipped existing rows (old self-set overrides, PBQ-only levels), which kept their levels. The 029 schema probe ('current version', expects Not started) failed on a fully migrated database.
failures.root_cause: mastery_detail filters out pairs with no direct evidence (correct for readiness), and 031's mastery_from_attempts passed that through instead of returning Not started as 029's revised rule does (FAIL-111).
failures.fix_summary: mastery_from_attempts left-joins mastery_detail and returns Not started, score 0, when it returns nothing; mastery_detail still returns no row so readiness treats the objective as unpracticed. The PBQ grade path only writes Not started to objectives that already have a row, so a PBQ never creates rows for unstudied objectives.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-model.dbtest.ts::031 keeps 029's guarantees::no direct evidence is Not started; mastery_detail still returns nothing (FAIL-083)
backend/lib/mastery-model.dbtest.ts::031 keeps 029's guarantees::031b: self-set and PBQ-only levels reset
the restore leaves later progress alone
failures.prevention_notes: Same as FAIL-082: the 029 guarantee tests run against the installed rule.

failures.title: 031 held ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on attempts through the backup and recompute
failures.symptom: On the 1.9M-attempt / 320k-mastery review fixture, the first version of 031 ran 88.8 s in one transaction after ALTER TABLE attempts; 155 of 183 probe reads of attempts and 155 of 183 attempts inserts hit a 10 s statement timeout.
failures.root_cause: Schema change (attempts.assessment_type with an inline foreign key) and the backup plus global recompute were in one file; the runner applies a file as one transaction, so the ALTER's lock lasted until the recompute committed. The same defect FAIL-112 fixed for 029.
failures.fix_summary: 031 is schema and functions only, with set local lock_timeout = '5s'; the foreign key is added NOT VALID (no scan under the lock). 031b (sorts after 031) takes the backup, runs recompute_mastery(), records created rows and validates the foreign key under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE. Measured over three runs on the fixture: 031 0.33-0.68 s including runner start-up, 031b 90.8-92.9 s; probe reads of attempts, mastery and error_log and attempts inserts every 0.5 s answered within 0.33 s with no failures (before: 88.8 s, 155 of 183 reads and inserts timed out at 10 s).
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-model.dbtest.ts::031 keeps 029's guarantees::031 is schema only
under a lock timeout; the assessment_type key is added NOT VALID and 031b validates it (FAIL-084)
failures.prevention_notes: FAIL-112's prevention note applies: migrations that ALTER a large table keep data work in a separate b file; measure against the production-sized fixture with a concurrent read probe.

failures.title: 031's restore rewound progress made after the backup
failures.symptom: The documented 031 restore put every backed-up row back, including rows a learner had since earned by grading, and left rows the recompute created.
failures.root_cause: 031 copied 029's first restore, which FAIL-114 later fixed for 029.
failures.fix_summary: mastery_backup_031 has created_by_031; the restore in the 031b header updates only rows with updated_at <= backed_up_at and deletes created rows untouched since. On the fixture the restore returned all 320,003 rows to their pre-031 values exactly (in a rolled-back transaction).
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-model.dbtest.ts::031 keeps 029's guarantees::031b: self-set and PBQ-only levels reset
the restore leaves later progress alone
failures.prevention_notes: Restore SQL is executed by the test straight from the migration header.

failures.title: mastery_backup_031 kept a deleted account's mastery history
failures.symptom: mastery_backup_031.user_id had no reference to app_users, so DELETE /api/account left the learner's backed-up mastery behind.
failures.root_cause: Same omission FAIL-115 fixed for the 029 backups; 031 predated that fix.
failures.fix_summary: mastery_backup_031.user_id references app_users(id) on delete cascade (created in 031, before any rows exist).
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-model.dbtest.ts::031 keeps 029's guarantees::031b: self-set and PBQ-only levels reset
the restore leaves later progress alone
failures.prevention_notes: Any new per-user backup table needs ON DELETE CASCADE to app_users.

failures.title: Merged 029 test could not tell 'after the backup' from 'during it'
failures.symptom: Resolving mastery-recompute.dbtest.ts by running PR #22's new restore test inside REQ-100's single rolled-back transaction (FAIL-076) would make every write carry the backup's own timestamp: now() never moves inside one transaction, so the restore's updated_at <= backed_up_at test reverted rows changed 'after' the backup.
failures.root_cause: The two branches fixed the file in incompatible ways: one isolated it in one transaction (FAIL-076), the other added a test that depends on transaction boundaries (FAIL-114).
failures.fix_summary: Kept the single rolled-back transaction; migrate() runs 029 and 029b in it and then moves the learner's mastery and backup timestamps back a minute, modelling the migration's commit. The 031b test does the same.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-model.dbtest.ts::031 keeps 029's guarantees::031b: self-set and PBQ-only levels reset
the restore leaves later progress alone
failures.prevention_notes: Tests that run a migration inside a rolled-back transaction must not rely on now() differing between statements.

failures.title: Lesson-regen lease test raced the regenerate it was checking
failures.symptom: test:db failed 1 of 12 full runs (fresh database, seeded twice, --test-concurrency=1): lesson-regen.dbtest.ts 'a GET waits for the learner's own regenerate running elsewhere, then serves it' -- isClaimLive(...) was false right after the intro resolved. 0 of 40 runs of the file alone; a 50 ms pause before the check failed it 3 of 3.
failures.how_detected: repeated full DB suite runs (b4-align, FAIL-081 investigation)
failures.root_cause: The test's fake generator had no practice delay, so once the 100 ms intro resolved the regenerate could write the lesson and release its lease before the test's isClaimLive query ran; the test assumed 'practice still running' without making it so. Which query won depended on scheduling, so it failed only under load.
failures.fix_summary: The fake generator's practice now takes 500 ms, so the lease is held when the test checks it; with a 150 ms pause injected before the check the file passed 3 of 3, and 12 more full runs are recorded in FAIL-081.
regression_tests: backend/lib/lesson-regen.dbtest.ts::cross-instance generation claims::a GET waits for the learner's own regenerate running elsewhere
failures.prevention_notes: A test that asserts an in-flight state must hold that state open itself (a fake that waits), never rely on the code under test being slower than the assertion; check flaky candidates by injecting a delay before the assertion.

failures.title: Schema probe could not tell the first 031 from the current one
failures.symptom: With the first version of 031 installed, migrate --status reported only the 029 probe and advised re-applying 029, which would install the old rule over 031.
failures.root_cause: The 031 probe only checked that mastery_from_attempts calls mastery_detail; the 029 'current version' probe judged the function even when 031 owns it.
failures.fix_summary: New 031 probe: mastery_from_attempts returns Not started for no evidence and mastery_detail reads lesson_hint_reveals. The 029 probe passes once the 031 rule is installed, leaving the verdict to the 031 probes. Checked against the real first-version 031: status lists only 031.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-model.dbtest.ts::031 keeps 029's guarantees::the schema probe tells the first version of 031 from the current one
failures.prevention_notes: A probe for a function names its current version, and an older migration's probe defers once a later one replaces the function.

failures.title: Weighted mastery counted every attempt kind as evidence
failures.symptom: mastery_detail took every graded non-PBQ attempt on an objective (quiz, unitcheck, lab as well as lesson) as direct evidence and any earlier miss of any kind as a review retest, so an attempt kind nobody had weighted could set or lower a level.
failures.how_detected: second review of PR #22, applied to 031 at the lead's request
failures.root_cause: The evidence filter keyed on format (<> 'pbq') rather than kind; the second review of PR #22 found the same gap in 029 (lead, 2026-11-07).
failures.fix_summary: Direct evidence is kind = 'lesson' or an attempt that names an assessment_types row; unit evidence is kind = 'pbq'; review retests look at the same kinds.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-model.dbtest.ts::031 keeps 029's guarantees::only lesson answers and PBQs are evidence; another kind counts only when its assessment type is named
failures.prevention_notes: New attempt kinds reach mastery only through an explicit assessment_types row.

failures.title: Lesson resume hung on a bad connection
failures.symptom: Opening a lesson on a slow or dropped connection stayed on 'Picking up where you left off...' until the progress GET gave up, even with a valid device copy.
failures.root_cause: The restore awaited Promise.all of the account read and the device read, and the API client has no timeout, so the slowest source gated the screen.
failures.fix_summary: The account read is waited on for 4 s (settleWithin); after that the device copy is used, and a late account copy is adopted only if newer and the learner has not moved (shouldAdoptLateServer). Saving is skipped while the position is still the restored one, so a restore no longer re-stamps an old place with a new savedAt.
failures.prevention_notes: Network reads that gate a screen get an explicit wait budget and a fallback; the rule lives beside the code in lessonProgress.ts.

failures.title: A save in flight could resurrect a finished lesson
failures.symptom: After finishing a lesson, reopening it could resume at Solo: a progress PUT sent just before 'done' reached the server after the DELETE and its upsert recreated the row.
failures.root_cause: PUT and DELETE carried no ordering, so the server applied whichever arrived last.
failures.fix_summary: PUT carries the client's savedAt and DELETE its clearedAt; DELETE records a tombstone (migration 032) and a save not after it is ignored, under a per-user+objective advisory lock.
failures.prevention_notes: Last-writer-wins upserts that race a delete carry a client timestamp and are checked against a tombstone; a schema probe makes a missing 032 fail /api/health.

failures.title: Logout wrote anon lesson progress and a 401 save
failures.symptom: On logout the lesson screen re-rendered with no user, wrote ascendra.lessonProgress.anon.<id> and sent a progress PUT that 401'd.
failures.root_cause: userId fell back to the string 'anon', so the save effect treated a signed-out render as a user.
failures.fix_summary: No fallback: with no user nothing is read or saved and the pending save is dropped; the send also checks the user is unchanged; existing anon keys are removed once per app run.
failures.prevention_notes: Per-user storage keys never get a placeholder identity; code waits for a real user instead.

failures.title: Lesson progress fetched twice on resume
failures.symptom: Resuming at Guided or Solo while practice content was still generating fetched the saved position twice.
failures.root_cause: The restore effect depended on the lesson object; ensurePracticeReady replaced it with the same content, cancelling and re-running the restore.
failures.fix_summary: The restore effect keys on lessonFingerprint(lesson), which does not change when practice content fills in.
regression_tests: mobile/src/lib/lessonProgress.test.ts::REQ-101 restore runs once per lesson content (FAIL-094)
failures.prevention_notes: Effects that must run once per content key depend on a stable key, not an object that is replaced.

failures.title: No retry after a missed Solo check
failures.symptom: After 'Not yet', Re-read led back to Solo showing the old graded answer with only Continue; there was no way to answer again.
failures.root_cause: The graded Solo state is kept on purpose for resume, and nothing offered to clear it.
failures.fix_summary: 'Try again' on the Not yet screen and on a missed Solo result starts a fresh Solo check (new attempt id), with copy saying a repeat won't raise mastery (repeats are assisted by design, REQ-134).
failures.prevention_notes: Every graded miss offers a next action; UI copy states whether it can raise mastery.

failures.title: Back to course could land on another course
failures.symptom: With Course B, Course A, Lesson B in the stack, 'Back to course' popped to Course A's dashboard with B's params.
failures.root_cause: router.dismissTo pops to the nearest route with the same name, and every course dashboard shares one route name.
failures.fix_summary: planCourseReturn: dismissTo only when the nearest dashboard in the stack is this course, else push (same rule as FAIL-065 on fix/mobile-flows-2).
failures.prevention_notes: dismissTo is only used after checking the nearest same-named route is the target.

failures.title: Security+ and four other CompTIA tracks had no credential block
failures.symptom: SECPLUS, LINUXPLUS, CYSAPLUS, PENTESTPLUS and SECURITYX had no credential_exam_id: no exam code, duration, question format or passing score for the coach or any readiness feature, and no exam_domains rows.
failures.root_cause: The five tracks were hand-authored in data.ts before the credential block existed; later strands added credential blocks to new files only, and no test required one on every certification track.
failures.fix_summary: Credential blocks added from comptia.org pages (read 2026-11-07); catalog test requires a credential on every certification track.
failures.prevention_notes: catalog-blueprints.test.ts walks CATALOG_TRACKS (the same list the seed uses) and fails on any certification track without a credential block.

failures.title: AWSSAP taught SAP-C02 past its last test day
failures.symptom: The AWS Solutions Architect Professional track taught SAP-C02, whose last test day is 2026-11-16; SAP-C03 (5 restructured domains, pass mark 720) is GA 2026-11-17.
failures.root_cause: Vendor version changes are only caught when someone re-reads the guide; contentReviewDueAt (2026-10-27) had passed without a rebase, and the seed had no safe way to replace a version's units without rewriting learner-linked rows.
failures.fix_summary: AWSSAP now carries SAP-C03 (credential, five new units/objectives from the SAP-C03 guide); the four C02 units are retired, not rewritten; the SAP-C02 exam row is marked superseded.
failures.prevention_notes: contentReviewDueAt on transitioning tracks is the trigger; the seed's retiredAt/supersedes mechanism now makes the rebase safe to do as soon as a successor guide publishes. Remaining due rebases (DVA-C03, CySA+ CS0-004, Security+ SY0-801) are listed in REQ-102 risks.

failures.title: DVA-C02 last test day recorded as 2026-12-01
failures.symptom: credential_exams.retirement_date for DVA-C02 was 2026-12-01; AWS's exam-guide index and T&C post say the last day is 2026-11-30 (2026-12-01 is DVA-C03's first GA day).
failures.root_cause: The GA date of the successor was recorded as the predecessor's last day.
failures.fix_summary: retirementDate set to 2026-11-30 with source URLs; SeedCredential.supersedes now records lastExamDate explicitly as the last day to sit.
failures.no_test_reason: A vendor date; the test cannot know the right value. The supersedes field's comment and the ExamBlueprint.retirementDate doc fix the meaning (last day the exam can be sat).
failures.prevention_notes: SeedCredential.supersedes.lastExamDate and ExamBlueprint.retirementDate are documented as the last day the exam can be sat; source URLs sit beside each date.

failures.title: Eight Azure tracks' domain weights did not total 100
failures.symptom: AZ-900 99, AZ-104 94, AZ-305 102, AI-901 101, DP-900 97, AZ-140 97, DP-300 105, AZ-120 99: weighted readiness and exam_domains did not describe a whole exam.
failures.root_cause: Microsoft publishes ranges; each unit took the rounded midpoint, and nothing checked the total.
failures.fix_summary: Weights are points inside each published range that total 100 (midpoints when they already do; otherwise scaled and rounded by largest remainder). Ranges re-read on learn.microsoft.com 2026-11-07.
failures.prevention_notes: The blueprint test fails any certification track whose active weights do not total 100 unless publishedWeightsNote explains a vendor-printed total.

failures.title: Seed could only rewrite units/objectives in place on an exam-version change
failures.symptom: Units and objectives are matched by sort_order and updated in place, so replacing a version's units would re-point every learner's mastery and attempts at different objectives; rows past the end of the seed stayed listed; exam_domains rows past a shrunken blueprint stayed, inflating weight totals; the outgoing exam row kept looking current.
failures.root_cause: The seed had no notion of retirement or supersession -- only insert-or-update by position -- and the schema had no way to hide a row without deleting it (which cascades mastery).
failures.fix_summary: Migration 033 adds retired_at to course_units/objectives; every listing/rollup filters with isActive(); the seed writes retired_at from SeedUnit.retiredAt, retires surplus rows, deletes surplus exam_domains, and marks the superseded exam; schema probe added.
failures.prevention_notes: exam-blueprints.dbtest.ts drives a version change through seedTrack and asserts objective id/title/mastery survive and the course hides retired rows. New readers of course_units/objectives must use isActive() from lib/progress-sql.ts.

failures.title: credential_exams duration/format data was not readable by app code
failures.symptom: duration_minutes, question_format, passing_score_policy and exam_domains were written by the seed but no API or lib function returned them, so mock-exam or readiness work would have re-joined the taxonomy ad hoc.
failures.root_cause: coach-context joined only the exam code; nothing exposed the rest of the blueprint.
failures.fix_summary: lib/exam-blueprint.ts examBlueprintForTrack(); GET /api/courses/:id returns it as exam.
failures.prevention_notes: examBlueprintForTrack is the one reader for exam mechanics; exam-blueprints.dbtest.ts asserts it returns duration, format, passing policy and domains.

failures.title: Deploy gap: repeats written by old code counted as unassisted
failures.symptom: Between running 029 and deploying the code, old code inserts attempts with assisted = false and overwrites mastery with its latest-answer rule; mastery_from_attempts trusted the stored flag, so a resubmitted Solo item counted as a fresh success.
failures.how_detected: PR #22 independent review (reproduced with fixture scripts)
failures.root_cause: The rule depended on a column only the new code fills, so its correctness depended on deploy timing.
failures.fix_summary: mastery_from_attempts derives a repeat from history (same user, objective, stage, question earlier) and a hint from lesson_hint_reveals (revealed before the answer), trusting assisted only when it is true. Every grade recomputes the pair; 029 header says to run select recompute_mastery() once after deploying the code.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-integrity.dbtest.ts::10. Attempts written by pre-029 code during the deploy gap (FAIL-110)
failures.prevention_notes: A rule in SQL must be computable from data every live code version writes; a flag set only by new code may narrow, never widen, credit.

failures.title: Self-set mastery levels survived the 029 recompute
failures.symptom: recompute_mastery() only visited pairs with attempts, so a Transfer-ready row set through the removed PUT override, with no attempts, kept its level.
failures.how_detected: PR #22 independent review (reproduced with fixture scripts)
failures.root_cause: The recompute was driven from attempts, not from the rows it was meant to correct, and mastery_from_attempts returned no row for zero evidence.
failures.fix_summary: mastery_from_attempts returns Not started for no evidence; recompute_mastery() visits every existing mastery row as well as every pair with graded attempts. Rows whose only evidence was a PBQ also become Not started (PBQ is not objective evidence).
regression_tests: then recomputes under the new rules
failures.prevention_notes: A recompute must iterate the table it rewrites, not only the evidence table.

failures.title: 029 held ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on attempts through the whole backfill
failures.symptom: On a 1.9M-attempt fixture 029 ran 44 s in one transaction after ALTER TABLE attempts; reads of attempts and error_log timed out for the whole run.
failures.how_detected: PR #22 independent review (reproduced with fixture scripts)
failures.root_cause: Schema changes and data backfill were in one file; the runner applies a file as one transaction, so the ALTER's lock lasted until the backfill committed.
failures.fix_summary: 029 keeps only schema (index built first under SHARE, then the ALTERs, lock_timeout 5s): 0.76-1.06 s. Backup, backfill and first recompute moved to 029b (runner sorts it after 029 and before 030 and records it in schema_migrations): 52-61 s holding only row locks; probe reads of attempts, error_log and mastery and attempts inserts stayed under 0.5 s throughout (before: 44 s, reads timed out). test:db now runs files one at a time because 029b rewrites every learner's mastery.
failures.prevention_notes: Migrations that ALTER a large table keep data work in a separate file; measure against a production-sized fixture with a concurrent read probe.

failures.title: Learner answer could break out of the grading prompt fence
failures.symptom: gradeFreeResponsePrompt stripped <learner_answer> tags in one pass, so </learner_</learner_answer>answer> left a working closing tag; PBQ answers and guesses were not fenced at all.
failures.how_detected: PR #22 independent review (reproduced with fixture scripts)
failures.root_cause: Removing a known token is not escaping: removal can reassemble the token from its pieces.
failures.fix_summary: All learner text placed in a prompt (free response, PBQ, guess) is HTML-escaped and fenced (fenceLearnerText), so it contains no < or >. Chat sends the learner message as its own user turn and needs no fence.
regression_tests: backend/lib/prompts.test.ts::learner text can't break out of its fence
failures.prevention_notes: Learner text in prompts goes through fenceLearnerText; never strip tags.

failures.title: Documented 029 restore rewound progress made after the backup
failures.symptom: The restore put every backed-up mastery and review row back, overwriting grades and Got it taps made after 029, and left rows the recompute had created.
failures.how_detected: PR #22 independent review (reproduced with fixture scripts)
failures.root_cause: The restore keyed only on row id, not on whether the row had changed since the backup.
failures.fix_summary: Restore only rows with updated_at <= backed_up_at; rows the recompute created are recorded with created_by_029 and deleted if untouched; review state is no longer restored (029 never changes it).
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-recompute.dbtest.ts::the documented restore puts untouched levels back and leaves later progress alone
failures.prevention_notes: A documented restore must say which rows it touches and is run by a test.

failures.title: 029 backups outlived account deletion
failures.symptom: mastery_backup_029 and error_log_backup_029 had no foreign key to app_users, so DELETE /api/account left the learner's history behind.
failures.how_detected: PR #22 independent review (reproduced with fixture scripts)
failures.root_cause: Account deletion relies on ON DELETE CASCADE; new per-user tables must join it.
failures.fix_summary: user_id references app_users(id) on delete cascade in both backup tables.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-recompute.dbtest.ts::deleting the account removes its backup rows
failures.prevention_notes: Every new table holding per-user data references app_users ON DELETE CASCADE.

failures.title: Choice shuffle seed was computable by the learner
failures.symptom: presentationSeed was the user id, objective id, stage and question, all visible to the app, so the shuffle (and the right answer's position) could be recomputed.
failures.how_detected: PR #22 independent review (reproduced with fixture scripts)
failures.root_cause: Determinism was taken for unpredictability; the seed had no secret.
failures.fix_summary: Seed is an HMAC-SHA256 under CHOICE_ORDER_SECRET, or a key derived from AUTH_JWT_SECRET when unset; stable per learner, objective, stage and question.
failures.prevention_notes: Anything that hides an answer must depend on a server secret.

failures.title: Hint route had no cross-user access test
failures.symptom: No test showed that a second user calling POST /api/objectives/:id/hint on someone else's private objective gets 404 and records nothing.
failures.how_detected: PR #22 independent review (reproduced with fixture scripts)
failures.root_cause: The route's access check was added with the route but only the happy path was tested.
failures.fix_summary: Added the test (the route already behaved correctly).
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-integrity.dbtest.ts::11. The hint route is scoped to the caller (FAIL-117)
failures.prevention_notes: Every new route gets an other-user test (REQ-129 pattern).

failures.title: recompute_mastery() overwrote grades committed during the run
failures.symptom: In the review's race test 245 of 290 grades committed while recompute_mastery() ran were overwritten with the level from before the grade (local re-run: 312/312 lock-less, 297/297 with the grader's lock).
failures.root_cause: The recompute was one INSERT ... SELECT: every pair was computed from the snapshot taken when the statement started, and the upsert took no per-pair grading lock, so a grade committed after the snapshot was replaced with a level computed without it.
failures.fix_summary: recompute_mastery_pair() decides each pair under the grader's advisory lock (grade_lock_key(), same derivation as gradeLockName() with lowercase ids), in a statement started after the lock; recompute_mastery() loops it in one transaction (029b, tests) and the new procedure recompute_mastery_batched() commits every 500 pairs. Race re-run: 0 stale of 385-400 grades in every variant.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-recompute-race.dbtest.ts::a grade committed while recompute_mastery() runs keeps its level
backend/lib/mastery-recompute-race.dbtest.ts::a grade committed while call recompute_mastery_batched() runs keeps its level
failures.prevention_notes: Any bulk writer of a table the grader writes takes the grader's per-pair lock and reads after acquiring it; covered by a two-connection DB test.

failures.title: Skipping 029b passed every schema check
failures.symptom: A database with 029 applied and 029b skipped reported current in npm run migrate -- --status and /api/health, with every learner still on the old levels.
failures.root_cause: Schema probes only checked objects 029 creates; 029b is data work and nothing probed for it, and nothing compared stored levels with the rule.
failures.fix_summary: Probe on mastery_backup_029 tagged 029b_mastery_backfill.sql (status, migrationsToApply, /api/health); --status also prints how many stored levels differ from mastery_from_attempts() and how many graded pairs have no row (informational). mastery_from_attempts probe now checks the kind = 'lesson' version; new probe for recompute_mastery_batched/grade_lock_key.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-recompute-race.dbtest.ts::a database without 029b's backup table is reported as missing 029b
backend/lib/mastery-recompute-race.dbtest.ts::--status counts stored levels that differ from the rule
failures.prevention_notes: A data-only migration gets a probe on an object it creates, and the pre-completion checklist already requires a probe per migration the code depends on.

failures.title: Choice shuffle seeded from the raw objective id
failures.symptom: Found while merging fix/hardening onto feat/mastery-integrity: the lesson GET and hint route seeded the per-learner choice shuffle with the objective id as the app sent it, while /api/grade (after REQ-135 normalization) seeds it with the canonical lowercase id. An iOS client sending an uppercase id would see one order and be graded against another, so a right answer could be marked wrong.
failures.root_cause: REQ-134 built presentationSeed from raw id strings; REQ-135 lowercased ids only at lock keys and route edges. Two branches each correct alone disagreed once combined, because a derived string (the seed) depends on id spelling.
failures.fix_summary: presentationSeed lowercases both ids; the hint and grade routes use the canonical id from visibleObjective.
regression_tests: backend/lib/choice-order.test.ts::presentationSeed ignores the case of the ids (REQ-135)
backend/lib/hardening.dbtest.ts::the sessions route and grade route accept uppercase ids and treat them as the same row
failures.prevention_notes: Any string derived from an id (lock key, seed, map key) is built from the lowercase form; covered by the mixed-case hardening tests.

failures.title: Whitespace-only resend refused as a conflict
failures.symptom: A free-response retry that differed only by trailing whitespace got 409 instead of replaying the stored grade.
failures.root_cause: The mobile resend signature trims the answer but the request body does not; the server compared answers exactly.
failures.fix_summary: Answers are compared after trimming surrounding whitespace.
failures.prevention_notes: Idempotency identity compares normalized answers, the same normalization the client signs.

failures.title: New CS0-003 superseded check assumed a CS0-003 exam row exists on a fresh database
failures.symptom: test:db on a freshly migrated and twice-seeded database failed 'CYSAPLUS teaches CS0-004 ...': expected exactly one CS0-003 credential_exams row, found 0. It passed on the upgraded database, which had been seeded with CS0-003 first.
failures.how_detected: test (npm run test:db on a fresh database, as CI runs it)
failures.root_cause: The CySA+ track only ever seeds its current exam, so a CS0-003 row exists only on a database seeded before REQ-103. The test was written against the upgrade database and asserted the production shape as universal; the SAP-C02 test right above it already handles 0-or-1 rows for the same reason.
failures.fix_summary: Assert at most one CS0-003 row and that any present is superseded by CS0-004 with retirement_date 2026-12-22; the end-to-end upgrade path is covered by the 'CySA+ CS0-003 -> CS0-004 upgrade through the real seed code' suite, which seeds the CS0-003 shape itself.
failures.prevention_notes: Run test:db on both a fresh database and an upgraded one when a test reads rows that only older seeds create; exam-version tests follow the SAP-C02 pattern (loop over 0-or-1 rows) plus a self-contained upgrade suite.

failures.title: AWSDVA still taught DVA-C02 three weeks before its last test day
failures.symptom: The AWS Developer Associate course listed only DVA-C02 domains (32/26/24/18) and objectives although the DVA-C03 guide was published and registration had opened 2026-10-27; DVA-C02 can't be taken after 2026-11-30, so a learner starting now would study the wrong blueprint (no AI-security task, no container build/deploy, no presigned URLs).
failures.root_cause: REQ-102 built the retire-and-append mechanism and applied it to SAP-C03 but deliberately deferred DVA as a follow-up; the track was marked 'transitioning' with a comment, and nothing turned that comment into a tracked requirement or a test, so it relied on someone remembering.
failures.fix_summary: AWSDVA rebased onto DVA-C03: four C02 units retired at 2026-12-01T12:00Z with ids and history kept, four C03 units appended from the official guide (all 72 skills), credential DVA-C03 superseding DVA-C02.
regression_tests: backend/lib/exam-blueprints.dbtest.ts::AWSDVA teaches DVA-C03; any DVA-C02 row is kept
failures.prevention_notes: A deferred exam-version rebase is now registered as a requirement (REQ-104) rather than left as a seed comment; the catalog test pins AWSDVA to DVA-C03 and its supersession dates.

failures.title: Retire-and-append would list two units with the same title during a version change
failures.symptom: DVA-C03 reuses three DVA-C02 domain names (Development with AWS Services, Security, Troubleshooting and Optimization). With the C02 units kept and listed until retiredAt, the course page and attempt/error history (which show unit titles) would show two indistinguishable 'Security' units until 2026-12-01.
failures.root_cause: REQ-102's uniqueness test checked only active unit titles (the exam_domains naming concern); SAP-C03 happened to rename every domain, so the overlap window between retired and new units with equal names was never exercised.
failures.fix_summary: Retired DVA-C02 unit titles carry a ' (DVA-C02)' suffix (rows matched by sort_order, so ids and history are unchanged); new catalog-wide test requires unit titles unique within a track, retired units included.
regression_tests: backend/lib/catalog-blueprints.test.ts::unit titles are unique within a track
failures.prevention_notes: The catalog-wide test fails any future version change that reuses a domain name without renaming the outgoing unit; confirmed it fails when the suffix is removed.

failures.title: Lesson stepper showed no step as done on the Done screen
failures.symptom: On the lesson's Done step the Guess/Teach/Guided/Solo stepper rendered every step as not started (no check marks).
failures.how_detected: review while adding the skipped-Guided marker (REQ-106)
failures.root_cause: StepHeader computed the active index with STEPS.indexOf(step); STEPS has no 'done', so indexOf returned -1 and no step counted as past.
failures.fix_summary: Done now counts as past every step; a Guided step skipped through the adaptive suggestion is marked skipped (icon and spoken label), not done.
failures.no_test_reason: Render-only component in the screen file; mobile tests run pure modules only (node --test src/lib/*.test.ts). Needs a device check.
failures.prevention_notes: Index lookups into a step list must handle steps outside the list; prefer an explicit order map.

failures.title: Adding teach state to Position broke samePosition for callers without it
failures.symptom: mobile lessonProgress test 'samePosition ignores object identity but not content' failed: a position without teach state no longer equalled FRESH_POSITION.
failures.root_cause: samePosition compared JSON.stringify(a.teach) with JSON.stringify(b.teach); a position built without the new field stringified to undefined while FRESH_POSITION carried EMPTY_TEACH, so the restore guard would have saved a restored position again.
failures.fix_summary: Missing teach state is compared as EMPTY_TEACH.
failures.prevention_notes: When a field is added to a compared shape, default it in the comparison so older callers and saved data compare equal.

failures.title: Plain PBQ request served a scenario the learner had already answered
failures.symptom: GET /api/pbq?unitId= returned the unit's newest scenario from any learner, so a learner was handed a scenario they had already attempted and its repeat counted as a first exposure
failures.root_cause: The selection query filtered by unit only (order by generated_at desc limit 1); scenarios were treated as a per-unit cache like lesson_content, with no notion of who had seen what, although a unit accumulates many scenarios
failures.fix_summary: lib/pbq-scenarios.ts findUnseenScenario: newest visible scenario with no attempt by this learner; generate only when none is unseen
regression_tests: backend/lib/pbq-scenarios.dbtest.ts::serves a scenario the learner has not attempted
backend/lib/pbq-scenarios.dbtest.ts::a catalog scenario one learner answered is still served to another learner
failures.prevention_notes: Selection now lives in one tested library function; any cached content that a learner answers needs a per-learner seen filter, which the dbtest pins

failures.title: Simultaneous PBQ requests from one learner could each generate a scenario
failures.symptom: Two requests for the same unit at once (double tap, two devices, retry after a slow response) both found nothing to serve and both called the model, spending two generations and two rate-limit slots
failures.root_cause: Check-then-generate with no lock: the existence check and the insert are separated by a multi-second model call, and nothing serialised callers. A transaction advisory lock is unsuitable because it would hold a pooled connection idle in transaction across the model call
failures.fix_summary: Per-(learner, unit) lease in pbq_generation_claims (migration 036) with heartbeat and token release; waiters poll until release then serve the stored scenario; the rate limit is consumed only by the holder
regression_tests: backend/lib/pbq-scenarios.dbtest.ts::5 concurrent plain requests from one learner for one unit generate exactly one scenario
backend/lib/pbq-scenarios.dbtest.ts::5 concurrent fresh=1 requests (a burst of taps) generate exactly one scenario
failures.prevention_notes: Model-backed generation paths take a database lease (lesson_generation_claims, pbq_generation_claims); the concurrent test fails 4 of 11 with the lease disabled

failures.title: Recompute row-locked and rewrote every mastery row
failures.symptom: Every recompute_mastery() call row-locked every existing mastery row, even rows already equal to the rule, so a re-run blocked grades for its whole duration.
failures.root_cause: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE locks the conflicting row even when the WHERE skips the update.
failures.fix_summary: recompute_mastery_pair() compares the stored row with the rule first, without any lock, and returns when equal; only differing pairs take the lock and are written. No-op re-run on the fixture: 12 s, 0 rows locked.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-recompute-race.dbtest.ts::a recompute with nothing to change finishes while every row is locked elsewhere
failures.prevention_notes: Bulk upserts check for a difference before writing; ON CONFLICT ... WHERE is not a no-lock skip.

failures.title: 029b header understated the mastery row locks
failures.symptom: The 029b header said it locked only the mastery rows the recompute changed; on the review's fixture it locked every mastery row, and its timing omitted that a grade of a locked row waits until commit.
failures.root_cause: The lock description was written from the intended behaviour (WHERE skips unchanged rows), not measured; ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE locks skipped rows too.
failures.fix_summary: With FAIL-180, unchanged rows are not locked; header and runbook now state that a first run still changes (and locks) nearly every row, re-measured 58 s on the 1.9M-attempt fixture with reads <=21 ms, inserts <=135 ms, and mastery writes to changed rows waiting for the commit; recommend a quiet window.
failures.no_test_reason: Documentation of measured lock behaviour; the skip itself is tested by FAIL-180's test and the timing needs the 1.9M-row fixture (scratchpad probe.cjs), too large for test:db.
failures.prevention_notes: Lock and timing claims in a migration header come from a run with a concurrent probe on a production-sized fixture.

failures.title: Deploy gap: attempts of any kind counted as mastery evidence
failures.symptom: The review's gap.sql: a forged kind=quiz Solo success two days old plus one lesson Solo success written by the old code in the gap made Transfer-ready after the recompute.
failures.root_cause: mastery_from_attempts() filtered only format <> 'pbq'; the old grade route accepted kind from the app, so any kind of row with stage solo counted.
failures.fix_summary: Evidence (and the recompute's pair list) requires kind = 'lesson'; the 029 header documents that pre-029 history and gap rows are trusted as-is and that grading should be paused or the gap kept short; the schema probe checks for the new version.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-recompute-race.dbtest.ts::a forged other-kind row does not make Transfer-ready
backend/lib/mastery-recompute-race.dbtest.ts::an objective with only other-kind attempts has no evidence
failures.prevention_notes: Evidence rules name every column that identifies what an attempt was, not only the ones that excluded known cases.

failures.title: No single deploy and rollback order for 029/029b
failures.symptom: The deploy order lived in a migration header, missed the app update, the Vercel auto-deploy on merge, the post-deploy recompute and verification, and gave no rollback order.
failures.root_cause: Each review round added a step to the 029 header; no runbook owned the full sequence across database, Vercel and EAS.
failures.fix_summary: docs/deploy-runbook-mastery.md: check status, apply 029 then 029b before merging (Vercel deploys master on merge), deploy backend, call recompute_mastery_batched(), publish the OTA update, verify health and status counts; reverse rollback order; cleanup. Linked from the 029 header and the README.
failures.no_test_reason: Operational document; its commands are exercised by test:db (migrate, recompute_mastery_batched, restore) and migrate --status.
failures.prevention_notes: A release that spans database, backend and app ships one runbook with forward and rollback order.

failures.title: No adversarial cases in the grading eval
failures.symptom: grading-cases.json had no prompt-injection, fence-breaking, restated-question, empty, irrelevant or other-language answers, so the fence fix (FAIL-113) was never checked against the live grader.
failures.root_cause: The eval set was written for grading accuracy on honest answers only.
failures.fix_summary: 13 adversarial cases (adv-01..adv-13) with expected verdicts; not yet run against the live model (no API key here).
regression_tests: backend/scripts/eval/scoring.test.ts::has at least 10 adversarial cases covering injection
failures.prevention_notes: Prompt-boundary fixes add eval cases that attack the boundary.

failures.title: 029b restore unsafe statement by statement and rewrote identical rows
failures.symptom: The documented restore re-wrote rows that already held their backed-up values and was only described as a begin/commit block.
failures.root_cause: The update had no is-distinct-from check, and nothing said whether its statements could be run alone or again.
failures.fix_summary: The update skips rows already equal to the backup; the header states each statement is complete on its own and safe in either order and on a re-run.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-recompute.dbtest.ts::the restore statements run one at a time
failures.prevention_notes: Documented manual SQL is idempotent per statement and run by a test.

failures.title: Production could run without CHOICE_ORDER_SECRET
failures.symptom: With CHOICE_ORDER_SECRET unset, production silently used a key derived from AUTH_JWT_SECRET.
failures.root_cause: The dev fallback had no environment guard.
failures.fix_summary: choiceOrderKey() throws a clear error on first use when NODE_ENV=production and CHOICE_ORDER_SECRET is unset; fallback kept for dev/tests; .env.example and the runbook say it is required.
regression_tests: backend/lib/choice-order.test.ts::production requires CHOICE_ORDER_SECRET; development keeps the derived fallback
failures.prevention_notes: Secrets with a dev fallback are required in production.

failures.title: Account export omitted lesson_hint_reveals
failures.symptom: GET /api/account/export did not include the learner's Solo hint reveals added by migration 029.
failures.root_cause: The new per-user table was not added to EXPORT_SECTIONS.
failures.fix_summary: lessonHintReveals section added.
failures.prevention_notes: A new table with user_id gets an export section in the same change.

failures.title: 029 backup tables had no drop date
failures.symptom: mastery_backup_029 and error_log_backup_029 kept learner data indefinitely with no documented cleanup.
failures.root_cause: The backup was designed for rollback but its lifetime was never stated.
failures.fix_summary: 029b header and runbook: drop both tables by hand after 30 days, in the same change that removes the 029b probe; not automatic.
failures.no_test_reason: A manual, dated cleanup step; dropping the tables in a test would remove the 029b probe target (covered by FAIL-119's test).
failures.prevention_notes: Backup tables state their drop date where they are created.

failures.title: Coach guard did not know about open review questions
failures.symptom: With Today's review added, a learner could ask Ask the coach for the answer to a review question waiting in their session: openItemsFor listed only lesson items and PBQs, so the reply check had no key for it.
failures.how_detected: Blast-radius review of readers of attempts and open items while building REQ-108
failures.root_cause: The coach guard enumerates open items per source table; a new question source (review_session_items) was added without adding it to the enumeration. Nothing ties new assessment sources to the guard.
failures.fix_summary: openItemsFor also lists prepared, unanswered review questions in open sessions, with the correct option as the server-side key.
regression_tests: backend/lib/review-loop.dbtest.ts::the coach guard treats an unanswered review question as open
failures.prevention_notes: Pre-completion blast-radius check (REQ-137) applied to any new question source: grep openItemsFor and add the source.

failures.title: Recording the unit check id would have broken every graded answer before migration 037
failures.symptom: First draft of recordAttemptTx always named attempts.unit_check_item_id in its INSERT; on a database that has not had 037 applied (code deployed first, migrations by hand) every lesson and PBQ grade would fail with column does not exist.
failures.how_detected: Self-review against the deploy order notes in 029/031 before running tests
failures.root_cause: A shared write path was extended with a column from a new migration, while migrations are applied by hand and can lag the deploy.
failures.fix_summary: The column is named in the INSERT only when a unit check id is given; lesson and PBQ grading send the same statement as before plus assessment_type (031).
failures.no_test_reason: Needs a database without 037 while the test suite applies every migration; the schema probe for 037 reports the gap in /api/health instead.
failures.prevention_notes: Shared write paths only name columns from a new migration when the new feature uses them; schema probes added for 037/037b.

failures.title: Term extraction read action lists as terms
failures.symptom: A title like 'Engaging stakeholders: identifying and analyzing them, tailoring communication to their needs, and executing a stakeholder engagement plan' produced three clauses as named terms, which term coverage would then track.
failures.how_detected: Running termsFromTitle over all 5,277 seeded objective titles and reading a sample
failures.root_cause: The deterministic rule accepted any short comma list after a colon; some seed titles list skills (gerund clauses), not terms.
failures.fix_summary: A list where half or more of the items start with a lowercase -ing verb is left to the cached model extraction.
regression_tests: backend/lib/review-plan.test.ts::leaves non-list titles and clause lists to the model
failures.prevention_notes: Deterministic extraction is checked against the whole seed, not hand-picked titles.

failures.title: Readiness counted retired exam units after the exam-data merge
failures.symptom: After merging fix/exam-data (REQ-102, migration 033: course_units/objectives.retired_at) into the mastery-model base, courseReadiness() still read every unit and objective of a track, so a course whose old exam version had retired (SAP-C02 after 2026-11-17) would roll the retired domains into readiness and drag coverage down.
failures.how_detected: Blast-radius review of the merge before building mock exams, which reuse the readiness rollup.
failures.root_cause: REQ-102 added retirement and filtered it in every listing it knew about (progress-sql isActive); lib/readiness.ts came from the parallel REQ-100 branch and did not exist on fix/exam-data, so neither branch's author saw the other's reader. The text-level merge had no conflict there.
failures.fix_summary: courseReadiness() filters units and objectives with isActive() like the course view.
regression_tests: backend/lib/exam-practice.dbtest.ts::rules every format keeps::readiness ignores retired units (merge of REQ-102 into the readiness rollup)
failures.prevention_notes: Pre-completion checklist: after merging a branch that adds a visibility/filter column, grep every reader of that table on the merged tree, including files the other branch never had.

failures.title: Mock exams came out short of a domain's weight
failures.symptom: In development, a 20-question mock on a 60/40 course built 16-18 questions: domain A needed 6 per objective but one generation call per objective wrote 5, so the domain got fewer questions than its exam weight.
failures.root_cause: Item generation was planned one call per objective with an empty slot, regardless of how many slots that objective had, and slots were filled only from their own objective.
failures.fix_summary: Calls per objective = ceil(empty slots / items per call), one call each first so a tight budget still covers the blueprint, made in sequence per objective so later calls avoid earlier stems; a second fill pass takes items from another objective of the same unit so the domain keeps its share.
regression_tests: backend/lib/exam-practice.dbtest.ts::a mock exam end to end::creating a mock fills the shared bank once and returns no keys
failures.prevention_notes: The DB test asserts the per-domain question counts of a weighted mock, not only the total.

failures.title: Exam practice DB test was order-dependent (about 1 run in 10 failed)
failures.symptom: exam-practice.dbtest.ts failed intermittently: once because the coach-guard check expected one specific answer key among randomly chosen items, once because two answers could land on one objective and correctly produce Needs review, which the test did not allow.
failures.how_detected: Fresh-database run of npm run test:db, then the test looped 20 times.
failures.root_cause: The test asserted on one sample of a randomised selection (items and slot order are shuffled per session) instead of on properties every sample has.
failures.fix_summary: Assertions now hold for every possible selection (any key from the fake bank; any level below Independent), and the file was run 25 times in a row clean.
regression_tests: backend/lib/exam-practice.dbtest.ts::a mock exam end to end::submit grades on the server and records answered questions as attempts
failures.prevention_notes: Tests over randomised selection assert invariants, and a new DB test with random selection is looped before it is committed.

failures.title: New dbtest failed typecheck: randomUUID arrays typed as template-literal UUIDs
failures.symptom: tsc --noEmit: Argument of type 'string' is not assignable to parameter of type '${string}-${string}-...' in lib/coach-plan.dbtest.ts
failures.root_cause: Arrays built with Array.from(() => randomUUID()) infer node's branded UUID template type, so indexOf/includes with a plain string objective id fail to typecheck; the test ran under tsx (no typecheck) so only tsc caught it
failures.fix_summary: Annotated the id arrays as string[], as mastery-model.dbtest.ts already does
failures.prevention_notes: Run npx tsc --noEmit after writing a dbtest; tsx does not typecheck. Existing pre-completion checklist already requires typecheck.

failures.title: finishInsight: one SQL parameter used as varchar and text
failures.symptom: Course concept-set generation always ended 'failed': Postgres 'inconsistent types deduced for parameter $4'.
failures.root_cause: The same placeholder was assigned to course_insights.status (varchar) and compared in a CASE to a text literal, so Postgres deduced two types for it.
failures.fix_summary: Cast the parameter ($4::text) at both uses.
regression_tests: backend/lib/understanding.dbtest.ts::first request starts generation; the course is generated once; bad sets are dropped
failures.prevention_notes: Stateful SQL is exercised through a DB test before commit (pre-completion checklist); the failure surfaced there, not in production.

failures.title: Routes called next/server after() outside a request scope
failures.symptom: Comparisons and refresher routes returned 500 when invoked directly (tests, scripts): 'after was called outside a request scope'.
failures.root_cause: after() only works inside a Next request; route handlers imported and called directly have none, and the background generation call was made unconditionally.
failures.fix_summary: inBackground() wraps after() and falls back to an unawaited, error-swallowing call outside a request.
regression_tests: backend/lib/understanding.dbtest.ts::the route lists the card without answer keys; other courses' cards are hidden
failures.prevention_notes: Background work goes through inBackground(), which is safe in and out of a request.

failures.title: Regex escape lost inside a TS template literal SQL string
failures.symptom: learnedSetCandidates normalised confused_with with regexp '\s+' written as \s in a template literal, which JavaScript turns into a plain 's'.
failures.how_detected: Self-review of the generated source before the first DB test run
failures.root_cause: Backslash escapes in template literals are interpreted by JavaScript before the SQL reaches Postgres; \s is not a JS escape and collapses to 's'.
failures.fix_summary: Doubled the backslash so Postgres receives \s+.
regression_tests: backend/lib/understanding.dbtest.ts::a confusion shared by three learners gets one card
failures.prevention_notes: The learned-set DB test feeds 'Kinesis ' and 'kinesis' from different learners and requires them grouped as one confusion.

failures.title: Model-backed routes from parallel branches used the non-atomic rate limit
failures.symptom: Lab questions/report (REQ-106), exam item generation (REQ-109), Quiz me (REQ-110), explain-back (REQ-111), review question generation and grading and unit checks (REQ-108) all called checkRateLimit then recordAuthEvent, so N simultaneous requests each read 'under the limit' and all reached the model.
failures.how_detected: Merge review of every file the merged branches added, then a source scan
failures.root_cause: REQ-135 replaced the two-step pattern with consumeRateLimit on fix/hardening, but the feature branches were cut from feat/mastery-model before it and copied the older pattern; the merges had no text conflict in those new files.
failures.fix_summary: Each now calls consumeRateLimit (exam generation and review batches once per model call); the separate recordAuthEvent calls are gone.
regression_tests: backend/lib/integration-static.test.ts::no code outside lib/auth/rateLimit.ts calls checkRateLimit; recordAuthEvent is only for auth logging
failures.prevention_notes: The static test fails on any checkRateLimit call outside lib/auth/rateLimit.ts or recordAuthEvent outside auth routes; pre-completion checklist line on cross-branch contracts.

failures.title: Auto-merged grader skipped the assist rules for every non-lesson attempt
failures.symptom: After merging feat/review-loop, recordAttemptTx computed assistReason only for kind 'lesson' and took input.assistReason for everything else, so a PBQ revision (REQ-105) was recorded unassisted, an exam answer to a question already seen (REQ-109) was not a repeat, and explain-back 'reveal' / comparison-card 'hint' (REQ-111) were dropped -- all scoring as full unaided evidence.
failures.how_detected: Reading both sides' intent while resolving the grading-service conflict
failures.root_cause: review-loop and understanding each added their own caller-supplied assist field (assistReason vs assist) and review-loop rewrote the call site; git merged the line without conflict because the other branches changed assistReasonFor's body, not the call.
failures.fix_summary: One field (assist) for a caller-known reason; every kind goes through assistReasonFor (retry, caller reason, exam repeatAnySetting, typed repeat, lesson rules). Exam answers set repeatAnySetting; review answers pass assist and the schedule step honours a grader-detected repeat.
regression_tests: backend/lib/integration-merge.dbtest.ts::an exam question seen before is a repeat; a caller-known reason (review hint, explain-back reveal) is kept
failures.prevention_notes: DB tests cover each kind's assist; checklist line on cross-branch contracts.

failures.title: Tests written against an older rule or schema failed on the merged tree
failures.symptom: lesson-experience expected 029's evidence text; mastery-model inserted a 'lab' attempt with an objective (035's check refuses it); prompts.test's PBQ fixture lacked REQ-105's required modelAnswer/fixNext; review-loop and understanding tests asserted the pre-041 rule (unit checks ignored, one discrimination answer is format evidence).
failures.how_detected: test:db and npm test on the merged tree
failures.root_cause: Each branch's tests were correct for its own base; the integrated rule and schema changed what they assume.
failures.fix_summary: Updated each assertion to the integrated behaviour (031/041 evidence text, a unitcheck kind, full PBQ grade fixture, unit checks count, two discrimination answers needed), keeping what each test protects.
regression_tests: backend/lib/lesson-experience.dbtest.ts::a later lesson grade recomputes mastery without counting the lab report
backend/lib/review-loop.dbtest.ts::unit check evidence counts in the unit branch like a PBQ (041)
backend/lib/understanding.dbtest.ts::a discrimination answer is graded server-side and counts as application evidence; a repeat does not
failures.prevention_notes: Checklist: tests written against an older rule are updated, not deleted.

failures.title: Coach guard protected the unit's newest PBQ, not the one this learner is served
failures.symptom: With REQ-107 a learner is served the newest scenario THEY have not attempted; the guard still named the unit's newest scenario from anyone, so after answering it the scenario actually on screen was not held back.
failures.how_detected: Semantic review of every reader of pbq_scenarios after the merge
failures.root_cause: coach-guard.ts (REQ-100) and pbq-scenarios.ts (REQ-107) were written in parallel against different serving rules.
failures.fix_summary: The guard's PBQ subquery now picks the newest scenario of the unit this learner has not attempted, as GET /api/pbq does.
regression_tests: backend/lib/integration-guard.dbtest.ts::PBQ: the scenario guarded is the one this learner would be served next, not the unit's newest (FAIL-233)
failures.prevention_notes: DB test.

failures.title: New model-backed routes were cut off by the app's 15 s default timeout
failures.symptom: fix/mobile-flows-2 added a 15 s request timeout with a list of model routes that get 180 s; exam session creation, lab questions/report, explain-back, Today's review start and typed answers, unit checks and Quiz me were not in it, so they would fail while the server was still generating or grading.
failures.how_detected: Cross-checking MODEL_ROUTES against every route that calls the model after the merge
failures.root_cause: The timeout list was written on a branch that did not have those routes.
failures.fix_summary: Added the eight routes; reads on the same paths keep 15 s.
regression_tests: mobile/src/lib/apiClient.test.ts::routes added by exam, labs, explain-back, review, unit checks and Quiz me wait for the model
failures.prevention_notes: Mobile test; checklist line.

failures.title: Lab report drafts survived logout
failures.symptom: REQ-106 stores lab report answers under ascendra.labDraft.<user>.<objective>; FAIL-070's logout sweep (fix/mobile-flows-2) only knew draft, pbqProgress and lessonProgress keys, so a learner's lab answers stayed on a shared device.
failures.how_detected: Listing every AsyncStorage key the merged app writes
failures.root_cause: The sweep's key list was written on a branch without the lab draft.
failures.fix_summary: labDraft keys belong to their user and are swept and write-guarded like the others.
regression_tests: mobile/src/lib/mobileFlows2.test.ts::lab report drafts go with the account
failures.prevention_notes: Mobile test; checklist line.

failures.title: Account export missed lesson_progress_tombstones and had no coverage check

failures.title: Mock-exam answer graded blank or stale: unordered saves, submit without flush
failures.symptom: On a slow network the last exam answer (or any whose save failed) was graded as Not answered: Submit did not wait for in-flight saves or retry failed ones, the server closes the session at grading and refuses later saves with 409, and the app's 409 handler just showed results. Two quick changes to one question could also land out of order and leave the older answer stored.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 mobile (H1), read of exam.tsx and exam-sessions.ts
failures.root_cause: Each change sent its own unnumbered fire-and-forget PUT; nothing tracked in-flight or failed saves, so neither the app nor the server could order them or know an answer was missing before grading.
failures.fix_summary: Saves go through a per-session queue: one in flight per question, numbered (seq) from the server's saveSeq, failed fields kept and retried every 5 s and on demand, flushed before Submit and Leave; Submit refuses with the unsaved question numbers while any save has failed (except at time-up). The server stores save_seq (migration 047) and ignores a save numbered at or below it with 200 {saved:false, stale:true}.
regression_tests: and lists what is still unsaved
mobile/src/lib/examSaveQueue.test.ts::one save in flight per question; changes made meanwhile are merged and sent next
backend/lib/exam-practice.dbtest.ts::a save numbered below the last applied one is ignored
not an error; the view returns the number
failures.prevention_notes: Server-side sequence check in the same UPDATE as the status check; the client queue is the only save path on the exam screen.

failures.title: Unit check showed missed parts as covered beside a failing verdict
failures.symptom: A unit check could show every sub-part as a green covered tick (and say covered to TalkBack) next to a partial or incorrect verdict.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 mobile (H2), read of unit-check.tsx and lib/unit-check.ts
failures.root_cause: Unit checks were graded with the plain gradeResultSchema (missedParts only), so the screen matched missedParts to sub_parts by exact text; any rewording or Part 2: prefix broke the match and an unmatched part defaulted to covered. REQ-107 had already moved PBQs off this guess.
failures.fix_summary: Unit checks are graded with pbqGradeResultSchema; normalizePartScores lines the scores up with the check's labels; partScores are stored on the attempt (replayed too) and returned. The screen renders rows from them; without scores a part is Not scored separately, never covered; misses are amber To work on.
regression_tests: mobile/src/lib/unitCheck.test.ts::the audit's case: reworded missedParts and no per-part scores never show a missed part as covered
