failures.prevention_notes: Any multi-part grade shown per part must come from per-part scores (pbqGradeResultSchema), never from label matching.

failures.title: Network errors reached learners as raw SyntaxError text and lost the HTTP status
failures.symptom: A Wi-Fi sign-in page or proxy HTML error surfaced as SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'; offline as Network request failed; the 401 refresh and 429 handling never ran; chat showed (error getting reply: ...) as a coach message.
failures.root_cause: The client parsed JSON outside its error handling and passed fetch failures through unchanged.
failures.fix_summary: The body is parsed inside the handling: a non-JSON response is an ApiError with its status (a 2xx portal page counts as 502) and a calm message; fetch failures become NetworkError with a calm message; 5xx never shows server internals; screens use friendlyError; chat shows a banner with Retry and keeps the text.

mobile/src/lib/apiClient.test.ts::a network error that is not a timeout is a NetworkError carrying the original
failures.prevention_notes: All bodies parsed through parseBody inside the client's error handling.

failures.title: A stolen access token alone could change the account email and take the account
failures.symptom: POST /api/account/email accepted { newEmail } with only a bearer token; confirming it then forgot-password gave the attacker the account (audit 3 RAN the chain).
failures.root_cause: The email-change route was written as a profile edit, not as a credential change; the old address was only told after the change.
failures.fix_summary: Re-authentication (password, TOTP/backup code, or fresh Google sign-in) required; old address alerted at request time with a cancel link that also signs out everywhere; confirmation re-checks token_version and cancel; only the newest request is live.

failures.prevention_notes: Pre-completion checklist: credential-changing actions need re-authentication and end sessions; replay ids are bound to their item; every new route uses readJson, textField and visibility checks; regression tests named here.

failures.title: A stolen access token could replace an enabled authenticator and mint backup codes

failures.fix_summary: With MFA on, setup requires reauth and marks the pending secret (totp_pending_reauth_at); enable refuses unmarked secrets; enabling ends other sessions and returns a fresh access token.

failures.prevention_notes: Pre-completion checklist: credential-changing actions need re-authentication and end sessions; replay ids are bound to their item; every new route uses readJson, textField and visibility checks; regression tests named here.

failures.root_cause: CI only typechecked and unit-tested mobile.
failures.fix_summary: CI runs expo-doctor@1.21.6 report-only (reason in ci.yml); the JS bundle is already exported by the backend build.
failures.no_test_reason: CI configuration; exercised by CI itself.
failures.prevention_notes: CI step; make it blocking after the expo install --check bump.

failures.title: A fresh review session took 65 sequential queries
failures.symptom: POST /api/review/sessions with a fresh plan: 65 queries, 1.09 s p50 at 15 ms round trip.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: One insert per planned item, and three to five queries per item while preparing (terms, coverage, lesson, unseen questions, assign), plus a re-read of what was just written.
failures.fix_summary: Close/open/last-stats in one statement, session and items in one insert, one prepareContext read and one assignItems write (with title terms) for all items, planned items passed to prepare, drop skipped when all prepared. 10 queries with cached questions; 304 ms p50 at 15 ms.
regression_tests: backend/lib/perf-audit3.dbtest.ts::a fresh plan of 12 cached questions takes at most 10 queries and no model call
failures.prevention_notes: The dbtest counts statements on the pg client.

failures.title: Answered-today check ran once per due row
failures.symptom: dueObjectives' not-exists over all of a learner's session items per due objective; review/today 68 ms p50 for the 26k learner.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: Correlated subquery with a date cast on answered_at, so no index could serve it.
failures.fix_summary: Non-correlated NOT IN over a UTC time range on answered items, partial index review_session_items_answered (046). Whale review/today 68.6 -> 10.7 ms p50.
regression_tests: backend/lib/perf-audit3.dbtest.ts::a question already answered is not served again; an objective answered today is not due
failures.prevention_notes: Test pins today/yesterday semantics.

failures.title: Course view made 9 sequential queries
failures.symptom: GET /api/courses/:id: 9 queries (track, units, objectives, acknowledgement, readiness x3, blueprint x2).
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: Each part of the response was fetched separately.
failures.fix_summary: Acknowledgement and an attempt stamp ride on the track query; readiness and the exam blueprint are cached. Warm: 3 queries.
regression_tests: backend/lib/perf-audit3.dbtest.ts::warm view is 3 queries; a new answer invalidates the cached readiness
backend/lib/perf-audit3.dbtest.ts::a required disclaimer is reported from the same first query
failures.prevention_notes: Query budget in the dbtest.

failures.title: Readiness recomputed (mastery_detail per objective) on every course view
failures.symptom: 145 ms p50 typical, 2.1 s for 1.3k-5k attempts, 21.6 s for 26k attempts, every home-screen load.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: Readiness is computed live with no reuse between views.
failures.fix_summary: Per learner/course cache (60 s, 5,000 entries) keyed on the learner's newest attempt, so any grade invalidates it on every instance. Warm: 17 ms typical, 10-13 ms heavy.
regression_tests: backend/lib/perf-audit3.dbtest.ts::warm view is 3 queries; a new answer invalidates the cached readiness
backend/lib/perf-audit3.test.ts::hit within the TTL for the same stamp; a new answer (stamp) or the TTL recomputes
backend/lib/perf-audit3.test.ts::invalidateUser drops that learner only; the size stays bounded
failures.prevention_notes: In-process limitation documented in docs/operations-runbook.md.

failures.title: GET /api/errors had no limit
failures.symptom: Every unresolved error_log row was returned (42 KB for a 1.3k-attempt learner, unbounded growth).
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: Written when lists were short; never paged.
failures.fix_summary: limit (default 200, max 500), offset, total via count(*) over (), nextOffset; the home screen uses total for its due count.
regression_tests: backend/lib/perf-audit3.dbtest.ts::limit and offset paging with total and nextOffset; bad values are 400
failures.prevention_notes: Paging test.

failures.title: Learner history by unit had no index
failures.symptom: attempts?trackId walked the learner's history (82 ms, 26k learner); readyUnitChecks looked up unit checks per unit on the user_id prefix only.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: Only (user_id, objective_id) and (user_id, created_at) existed.
failures.fix_summary: 046 adds attempts (user_id, unit_id, created_at desc). Whale attempts?trackId 81.6 -> 15.8 ms p50.
regression_tests: backend/lib/perf-audit3.dbtest.ts::the schema probe passes and the planner uses the indexes for a learner-scoped read
failures.prevention_notes: Probe in schema-status.

failures.title: Foreign keys without indexes made account deletion scan whole tables
failures.symptom: auth_events.user_id and ai_calls.user_id (ON DELETE SET NULL) and attempts.unit_id had no index: deleting one account scanned 6M auth_events and 1.2M ai_calls rows.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: Indexes were added for read paths only.
failures.fix_summary: 046 adds auth_events_user, ai_calls_user_created, attempts_unit (partial where user_id is not null).
regression_tests: backend/lib/perf-audit3.dbtest.ts::the schema probe passes and the planner uses the indexes for a learner-scoped read
failures.prevention_notes: Probe in schema-status.

failures.title: Under concurrent load the 5-connection pool queued requests for seconds
failures.symptom: 50 clients, 15 ms injected round trip: p50 1.77 s, p95 16.5 s, 13.9 req/s.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: Requests making 9-65 sequential queries held pool connections for most of a second each.
failures.fix_summary: Round-trip reductions above. Same test after: p50 814 ms, p95 2.8 s, 52.5 req/s.
failures.no_test_reason: Pure performance; covered by the recorded load test and the per-route query budgets.
failures.prevention_notes: Benchmark (load test) recorded in the commit message and runbook.

failures.title: Every transaction paid two round trips to start; the rate limiter six per call
failures.symptom: BEGIN and set_config were separate statements; consumeRateLimit was begin, set_config, lock, count, insert, commit.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: Each step was written as its own statement.
failures.fix_summary: BEGIN plus SET LOCALs is one simple query of constants; count-and-insert is one statement after the lock (still atomic). Rate limit: 4 round trips.
regression_tests: backend/lib/perf-audit3.dbtest.ts::an allowed call is 4 statements; a refused call records nothing; 20 at once allow exactly the limit
backend/lib/perf-audit3.test.ts::BEGIN and the three SET LOCALs are one statement string with constants only
failures.prevention_notes: Statement-count test plus the existing timeout test.

failures.title: AI cost rows could be lost when the function froze after the response
failures.symptom: logAiCall wrote fire-and-forget with no after()/waitUntil.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: Serverless freezing after the response was not considered.
failures.fix_summary: Inside a request the write goes through next/server after(); outside one it runs at once as before.
regression_tests: backend/lib/perf-audit3.test.ts::outside a request after() is unavailable and the write still happens straight away
failures.prevention_notes: In-request behaviour depends on the platform; outside-request fallback is tested.

failures.title: Server errors reached only console.error
failures.symptom: No error tracker or alerting; a 500 went unnoticed unless a learner wrote in.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: No hook point existed.
failures.fix_summary: lib/error-tracker.ts called from serverError; sends to Sentry's store endpoint when ERROR_TRACKER_DSN is set, no-op otherwise.
regression_tests: backend/lib/perf-audit3.test.ts::with a Sentry DSN: one event to the store endpoint
backend/lib/perf-audit3.test.ts::a failing transport never throws into the request
failures.prevention_notes: Unit tests.

failures.title: A deploy missing a required setting went live and failed on a learner's request
failures.symptom: Settings are read lazily where used; health stayed green.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: No check of required env anywhere before use.
failures.fix_summary: /api/health checks required settings (names only): 503 misconfigured in production, warning elsewhere.
regression_tests: backend/lib/perf-audit3.test.ts::production missing a required setting is misconfigured
backend/lib/perf-audit3.test.ts::outside production a missing setting is only a warning
backend/lib/perf-audit3.test.ts::Anthropic credentials: a static key or both federation ids
failures.prevention_notes: Unit tests.

failures.title: Data migrations were only ever tested on an empty database
failures.symptom: 029b, 031b, 037b and 041b (about 8.5 minutes on the fixture) never ran over a row in CI.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: The database CI job builds the schema from zero.
failures.fix_summary: CI backfill job: 001-028, synthetic history (1,500 learners, 122k attempts), the rest, batched recompute, and a check that the backfills did work and levels match the rule.
failures.no_test_reason: CI configuration; backfill-check.sql is the assertion and was run locally.
failures.prevention_notes: CI job, run locally (1m44s).

failures.title: Vercel installed with npm install and no Node version was declared
failures.symptom: installCommand npm install could drift from the lockfile; no engines field (CI 24, local 22).
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: Defaults never revisited.
failures.fix_summary: npm ci in vercel.json and build-webapp.sh; engines.node >=22 <25 in both packages.
failures.no_test_reason: Deployment configuration; no runtime behaviour to test.
failures.prevention_notes: Config.

failures.title: No restore procedure or drill existed
failures.symptom: Nobody knew how to get the database back or how long it would take.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: Backups were assumed, not tested.
failures.fix_summary: docs/restore-drill.md: dump, restore to scratch, --status, row counts, app smoke, with a drill log.
failures.no_test_reason: Operational procedure; verified by running the drill.
failures.prevention_notes: Quarterly drill log in the doc.

failures.title: Rollback backups were never dropped after 30 days
failures.symptom: mastery_backup_* tables (53-87 MB each on the fixture) had no reminder or job.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: The runbook's Cleanup section relied on memory.
failures.fix_summary: migrate --status lists each backup with size and age and flags those past 30 days.
regression_tests: backend/lib/perf-audit3.test.ts::backups past 30 days are flagged; jit on is called out
failures.prevention_notes: Unit test.

failures.title: @types/node 20 against Node 22/24 runtimes
failures.symptom: Types lagged the runtime by two majors.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 performance report (benchmark on the 2.75M-attempt fixture)
failures.root_cause: Pinned and never bumped.
failures.fix_summary: @types/node 22.20.5 (tsc clean against it); lockfile edited for that package and undici-types only.
failures.no_test_reason: Type definitions only; tsc is the check.

failures.title: Course view served the old exam blueprint for up to 60 s after an exam-version change
failures.symptom: exam-blueprints.dbtest 'v2 with retirement still ahead' got TST-01 instead of TST-02 with the first blueprint cache.
failures.how_detected: Full test:db run during the task
failures.root_cause: The new blueprint cache was keyed on the course only.
failures.fix_summary: Key includes subject_tracks.credential_exam_id, read by the course view's first query.
regression_tests: backend/lib/exam-blueprints.dbtest.ts::v2 with retirement still ahead: old units stay listed alongside the new ones; exam moves to the new version
failures.prevention_notes: Existing dbtest caught it.

failures.title: Deleting a heavy account scanned three large tables per deleted attempt
failures.symptom: Deleting the 26k-attempt fixture account ran over 13 minutes (cancelled) while holding its locks; error_log, review_log and review_session_items attempt_id (ON DELETE SET NULL) had no index.
failures.how_detected: Account-delete benchmark on the audit fixture during this task
failures.root_cause: Foreign keys into attempts were added by feature migrations (037-039) without an index; the audit only listed app_users keys. Found while timing the account delete for MEDIUM-7.
failures.fix_summary: 046 adds partial attempt_id indexes on error_log, review_log, review_session_items, exam_session_items and placement_items; a dbtest fails if any foreign key into app_users or attempts lacks a leading index.
regression_tests: backend/lib/perf-audit3.dbtest.ts::every foreign key into app_users or attempts has an index led by its column
failures.prevention_notes: The guard test catches a new unindexed key into app_users or attempts.

failures.title: Support and course requests answered 500 for a NUL or lone surrogate
failures.symptom: POST /api/support with a NUL character or half an emoji in subject, body or course name failed the INSERT (invalid byte sequence for encoding UTF8: 0x00) and returned 500.
failures.how_detected: Re-verifying Audit 3 product L2 (Request a course) against the code; fail-before test
failures.root_cause: The route validated with its own trimmedString (type and length only) instead of lib/text-input.ts textField, which every other learner-text route adopted in REQ-135; the support route predates that and was never moved over.
failures.fix_summary: trimmedString now also requires textField to accept the value, so unstorable text is a 400.
regression_tests: backend/lib/product-basics.dbtest.ts::FAIL-400: a NUL or half an emoji in a field is a 400
failures.prevention_notes: Every route that stores typed text checks it with textField; the regression test covers each support field.

failures.title: Support request hourly cap could be raced past
failures.symptom: Requests sent at once all counted the last hour's rows under the cap of 10 and all inserted, each emailing a human.
failures.how_detected: Re-verification while adding Explore's Request a course; fail-before test with 14 concurrent requests
failures.root_cause: Count-then-insert in two statements with no lock; consumeRateLimit (REQ-135) exists for exactly this but the support route kept its own check.
failures.fix_summary: The route calls consumeRateLimit('support_request', userId, 10 per hour), which counts and records under an advisory lock.
regression_tests: backend/lib/product-basics.dbtest.ts::FAIL-401: requests sent at once can't get past the hourly cap
failures.prevention_notes: Rate limits use consumeRateLimit, never a count followed by a write.

failures.title: Course page primary button did nothing, and said Continue studying with nothing started
failures.symptom: With zero progress the button read Continue studying; when the first unfinished unit (by counts) listed no objectives, pressing it did nothing.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 product M4, re-verified in course/[trackId]/index.tsx
failures.root_cause: The target was found in two steps inline in the screen: the first unit whose mastered count was below its total, then an objective inside that unit only; nothing handled an empty list or the not-started state.
failures.fix_summary: src/lib/nextStep.ts picks across all units in course order: Start course, Continue (half-done first) or Review, or no button when there are no objectives.
regression_tests: mobile/src/lib/productBasics.test.ts::FAIL-402: a first unfinished unit with no objectives listed no longer makes the button do nothing
failures.no_test_reason: The old logic was inline in the screen (no component renderer here), so there is no fail-before run; the helper test pins the new behaviour.
failures.prevention_notes: Navigation targets are computed in a tested helper, not inline in a screen.

failures.title: Review told a brand-new learner they were all caught up
failures.symptom: The Review hub's empty state said All caught up / Nothing is due right now to someone who had never studied anything.
failures.root_cause: The empty state did not distinguish nothing scheduled yet (nextDueOn null) from nothing due today.
failures.fix_summary: src/lib/emptyStates.ts reviewEmpty(nextDueOn) says what Review is and offers a next action when nothing is scheduled.
regression_tests: mobile/src/lib/productBasics.test.ts::FAIL-403: Review doesn't tell someone who hasn't learned anything that they're 'all caught up'
failures.no_test_reason: Old copy was inline in the screen; the helper test covers the new behaviour.
failures.prevention_notes: Empty-state copy lives in src/lib/emptyStates.ts with tests.

failures.title: Terms acceptance never recorded; Google sign-up skipped it
failures.symptom: app_users had no terms columns and no table recorded acceptance; the agree checkbox existed only on the phone, and a new Google account was created without seeing the Terms.
failures.root_cause: Consent was treated as a client-side form check, not data; Google sign-up was added later as a separate path.
failures.fix_summary: Migration 048 terms_acceptances; register and new Google accounts record the current version with source; GET /api/onboarding and POST /api/onboarding/terms ask everyone else once on launch; in the export.
regression_tests: backend/lib/product-basics.dbtest.ts::sign-up records the current version with its source; an old or missing version records nothing
backend/lib/product-basics.dbtest.ts::the register and Google sign-up routes both record the acceptance they are sent
backend/lib/product-basics.dbtest.ts::a new account must accept; only the current version is accepted; the first time is kept
mobile/src/lib/productBasics.test.ts::the app's terms version is the server's current one
failures.prevention_notes: A mobile test pins the app's terms version to the server's; a static test pins both sign-up routes to the helper.

failures.title: Privacy policy misstated what goes to the AI provider
failures.symptom: The policy said only Ask Coach messages went to an unnamed AI provider; seven grading/feedback features also send learner text to Anthropic, and retention claimed rolling purges that the code does not do.
failures.how_detected: Audit 3 product H3; re-verified by grepping callClaude purposes and every delete statement
failures.root_cause: The page was written when chat was the only model call and was not revisited as grading features were added; no check ties the page to the code.
failures.fix_summary: Section 5 names Anthropic and every feature that sends typed text, what is sent with it, and Anthropic's training and retention terms with sources; section 6 states actual retention (no automatic purge of expired tokens or sign-in records).
regression_tests: mobile/src/lib/productBasics.test.ts::FAIL-405: names Anthropic and every feature that sends what a learner types
failures.prevention_notes: A test fails if the page loses the provider name or any learner-text feature; adding an AI purpose that sends learner text should add it to the page and the test.

failures.title: Not-affiliated disclaimers named only CompTIA
failures.symptom: Disclaimer, Terms and FAQ named only CompTIA while the catalog uses marks from AWS, Microsoft, Google, PMI, NCSBN and others; no course showed its own exam body.
failures.root_cause: Disclaimers were written for the first (Security+) course and never updated as the catalog grew.
failures.fix_summary: Course pages show a line naming exam.providerName (src/lib/vendor.ts); the Disclaimer lists every provider in the catalog; Terms, FAQ and Settings name the main ones.
regression_tests: mobile/src/lib/productBasics.test.ts::FAIL-406: the Disclaimer page lists the catalog's trademark owners
failures.prevention_notes: The course line is built from credential_providers data, so a new vendor is named without a code change; TRADEMARK_OWNERS should be updated with the catalog.

failures.title: Racing copies of one unit check submission each called the model
failures.symptom: 20 simultaneous copies of one clientAttemptId on the unit check route made 20 model calls for 1 stored attempt.
failures.root_cause: The replay check ran before any claim, so every copy reached the grader; REQ-117's grading claim covered only /api/grade, /api/pbq and review answers.
failures.fix_summary: withGradingClaim around rate limit, grading and recording; waiters replay the stored result through the route's own replay binding.
failures.prevention_notes: Any new graded route that takes a clientAttemptId and calls the model goes through withGradingClaim.

failures.title: Racing copies of one explain-back submission each called the model
failures.symptom: 20 simultaneous copies of one clientAttemptId on the explain-back route made 20 model calls for 1 stored attempt.
failures.root_cause: The replay check ran before any claim, so every copy reached the grader; REQ-117's grading claim covered only /api/grade, /api/pbq and review answers.
failures.fix_summary: withGradingClaim around rate limit, grading and recording; waiters replay the stored result through the route's own replay binding.
failures.prevention_notes: Any new graded route that takes a clientAttemptId and calls the model goes through withGradingClaim.

failures.title: Racing copies of one lab report submission each called the model
failures.symptom: 20 simultaneous copies of one clientAttemptId on the lab report route made 20 model calls for 1 stored attempt.
failures.root_cause: The replay check ran before any claim, so every copy reached the grader; REQ-117's grading claim covered only /api/grade, /api/pbq and review answers.
failures.fix_summary: withGradingClaim around rate limit, grading and recording; waiters replay the stored result through the route's own replay binding.
failures.prevention_notes: Any new graded route that takes a clientAttemptId and calls the model goes through withGradingClaim.

failures.title: Quiz me replayed another attempt's verdict and feedback for a reused client attempt id
failures.symptom: POST /api/coach/quiz/answer with a clientAttemptId already used on another question (or any other attempt) returned 200 with that attempt's verdict and feedback (incl. its explanation) and wrote nothing.
failures.root_cause: answerQuizTurn looked up the stored attempt by (user, clientAttemptId) only; REQ-116 bound replays on review/comparison/explain-back/unit check but missed the Quiz me route.
failures.fix_summary: The stored attempt must match the turn's question (kind quiz, stage coach_quiz, objective, question text) via replayMatches; otherwise answerQuizTurn returns replay_conflict and the route answers 409 REPLAY_CONFLICT.
failures.prevention_notes: Every route that replays by client id checks the stored attempt is for the same item (pre-completion checklist, REQ-116 line).

failures.title: Lab report answered a reused client attempt id with 400 instead of the shared 409
failures.symptom: POST /api/objectives/:id/lab/report with an id already used on another lab returned 400 'clientAttemptId was already used for a different answer', unlike grade, review, unit check and explain-back (409, shared message).
failures.root_cause: The lab route kept its own hand-written binding from REQ-106 when REQ-116 introduced lib/replay-binding.ts; REQ-120 kept it unchanged.
failures.fix_summary: replayMatches with a new labObjectiveId target field; mismatch answers conflict(REPLAY_CONFLICT).
failures.prevention_notes: Replay bindings go through lib/replay-binding.ts so status and wording stay shared.

failures.title: Unit check refused a resend of an already-graded id with 400 after the unit became ineligible
failures.symptom: A resend of a graded unit-check clientAttemptId returned 400 'Study every objective in this unit before its check.' once the unit gained an objective the learner had not studied, so the app never got the stored result.
failures.root_cause: The route checked eligibility before gradeUnitCheck's stored-result lookup; eligibility can change between the first send and the resend.
failures.fix_summary: gradeUnitCheck replays (with its binding) first and only then refuses a new submission when the unit is not eligible (ReviewError 400, UNIT_CHECK_NOT_ELIGIBLE).
failures.prevention_notes: Replay lookups run before any state-dependent refusal, as /api/grade does.

failures.title: Regenerate error helper called every 429 'wait a few minutes', including weekly and monthly plan limits
failures.symptom: regenerateErrorMessage returned REGENERATE_RATE_LIMITED ('Give it a few minutes') for any 429; with REQ-122 a regenerate can be refused for the week's allowance or the month's AI cap, so the lesson screen would have told the learner to retry in minutes when the next version opens days later
failures.how_detected: review while adding plan limits to the regenerate route
failures.root_cause: The helper keyed only on the status code because 429 meant only the 10-minute rate limit when it was written; a new meaning for an existing status reached a client helper that summarised by status instead of showing the server's message
failures.fix_summary: A 402/429 whose body carries upgrade, allowance or aiPaused shows the server's own message (which names when it opens again); other 429s keep the rate-limit text
regression_tests: mobile/src/lib/billing.test.ts::a regenerate refused for the plan shows the server's message
failures.prevention_notes: Plan refusals carry a machine-readable field (upgrade / allowance / aiPaused) beside a learner-ready message; client helpers that map statuses to text check for those fields first (src/lib/billing.ts billingSignal)

failures.title: npm install of one package rewrote unrelated libc fields in mobile/package-lock.json
failures.symptom: npm 10.9.9 'npm install react-native-purchases' also dropped the libc: [glibc]/[musl] entries of four unrelated optional native packages in the lockfile
failures.how_detected: git diff review of the lockfile before committing
failures.root_cause: The lockfile was written by an npm that records libc for platform-specific optional dependencies; the local npm doesn't, and re-serialises the whole tree on any install
failures.fix_summary: Kept the committed lockfile and added only the four new package entries and the root dependency (scripted merge); npm ci verified afterwards
failures.no_test_reason: A tooling behaviour of the local npm version, not product code; caught by reading the lockfile diff
failures.prevention_notes: Read the lockfile diff after adding a dependency; it should contain only the new packages. Use the same npm major/minor that wrote the lockfile when one is available

failures.title: Deleting a course with labs and lab answers failed (labs key and the labtask check blocked the objective's deletion)
failures.symptom: With the first draft of migration 050, deleting a subject track whose objectives had labs failed with 'update or delete on table objectives violates foreign key constraint labs_objective_id_fkey'; with labs set to cascade, the attempts_labtask_shape check (lab_id and objective_id required on every labtask row) and an immediate ON DELETE SET NULL key on attempts.lab_id still failed the same delete, because attempts.objective_id is SET NULL when an objective goes.
failures.how_detected: test (lib/labs.dbtest.ts after() hook, then the dedicated test)
failures.root_cause: The new tables and constraints were designed for inserts only. attempts keeps answers as history when what they were about is deleted (every item key on attempts is ON DELETE SET NULL), so a check that a labtask row always names its objective and lab cannot hold after a deletion, and labs had no ON DELETE at all. Found by the lab DB test's own cleanup (deleting its test tracks) failing.
failures.fix_summary: labs.objective_id and lab_runs.lab_id ON DELETE CASCADE; attempts_labtask_shape only requires a lab type in format 'open' (and no lab_id on other kinds); that a new labtask answer names its lab and objective is enforced in recordAttemptTx, as 035's rule for 'lab' is. attempts.lab_id keeps the lab id as history.
regression_tests: runs and lab answers works and keeps the answers as history
backend/lib/labs.dbtest.ts::a labtask attempt must name its lab and objective; the database refuses a lab id on any other kind or a pbq format
failures.prevention_notes: A check or key added to attempts must still hold after every ON DELETE action on attempts' existing keys (objective_id, unit_id, pbq_scenario_id are SET NULL); test deleting a course that has the new rows, not only inserting them.

failures.title: A deferred foreign key on attempts.lab_id broke later DDL on attempts in the same transaction
failures.symptom: lib/mastery-recompute.dbtest.ts failed 6 tests with 'cannot CREATE INDEX "attempts" because it has pending trigger events' after attempts.lab_id got a DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED foreign key (the fix tried first for FAIL-480).
failures.root_cause: A deferred foreign key queues an after-trigger event for every row inserted into attempts, whatever lab_id holds; Postgres refuses DDL on a table with pending trigger events, so any transaction that inserts attempts and then alters or indexes attempts fails (the recompute test re-runs migration 029 that way, and a migration could do the same). The deferral was chosen to dodge the ordering of two SET NULL actions without considering its effect on every other writer of attempts.
failures.fix_summary: attempts.lab_id has no foreign key: it is a plain indexed column written only by lib/labs.ts recordStep inside the transaction that reads the lab, with recordAttemptTx refusing a labtask answer without its lab (rationale in the migration's section 5).
regression_tests: runs and lab answers works and keeps the answers as history
failures.prevention_notes: Never add a deferrable constraint to attempts (or any hot table migrations alter): run the full npm run test:db after any constraint change on attempts, not only the feature's own tests.

failures.title: Lab engine's feature key 'labs' did not exist in the billing config ('lab')
failures.symptom: After merging feat/lab-engine into feat/tiers-billing lib/labs.ts exported LABS_FEATURE = 'labs' for requireFeature while lib/billing-config.ts named the feature 'lab'; requireFeature(user; LABS_FEATURE) would not type-check and isFeature('labs') was false
failures.how_detected: review while wiring decision 10 after the merge
failures.root_cause: The two branches were built in parallel and each guessed the other's key; LABS_FEATURE was a plain string constant with no tie to the Feature type; so the mismatch could only show up when the gate was finally wired
failures.fix_summary: One key 'labs' in FEATURES for every kind of lab (self-reported and build/case); LABS_FEATURE declared 'as const satisfies Feature' so an unknown key is a compile error; the self-reported lab routes use LABS_FEATURE
regression_tests: backend/lib/billing-config.test.ts::the labs key is one billing feature shared by every kind of lab (FAIL-510)
failures.prevention_notes: A feature key shared across modules is typed against the Feature union (satisfies Feature); the cross-branch contract list in .ai/checklists/pre-completion.md names feature keys

failures.title: Merged lab routes skipped the Free one-course check
failures.symptom: The lab list / progress / view / run routes from feat/lab-engine had no requireCourseAccess; with billing on a Free learner could list and run labs in every course while every other study route limits Free to one course
failures.how_detected: review of the merged routes against docs/billing.md's gated-route list
failures.root_cause: The lab engine was written before the billing branch existed; the merge carried no text conflict on these new files; so the cross-branch rule that every study route checks the free course was never applied to them
failures.fix_summary: requireCourseAccess on the list and progress routes (by track; unit; objective) and in gateLab for opening or starting a lab; reading or finishing a run already started stays open (decision 6)
regression_tests: backend/lib/labs.dbtest.ts::Pro and billing off: every lab is full; Free's sample is in their one course and counts as a graded answer (FAIL-511)
failures.prevention_notes: After merging a branch that adds study routes into one with plan gating; check each new route against the gated-route list in docs/billing.md (pre-completion checklist item added)

failures.title: Launch comp skipped accounts dated a moment ahead of the app clock
failures.symptom: lib/billing.dbtest.ts launch-comp test failed intermittently: a second --launch-comp --apply comped 0 accounts although one was created just before it
failures.how_detected: test (flaky run of the new launch-comp DB test)
failures.root_cause: runLaunchComp selected created_at <= a JS Date taken at run time; a JS Date has millisecond precision while timestamptz has microseconds (and the database and app clocks can differ); so an account made in the same millisecond or under clock skew was left out
failures.fix_summary: No time filter: every row in app_users when the statement runs is an account that exists at run time; idempotency comes from the fixed grant id per account
regression_tests: backend/lib/billing.dbtest.ts::dry run changes nothing; --apply gives every account Pro for 90 days once; a second run comps only new accounts (FAIL-512)
failures.prevention_notes: Compare database timestamps with the database's own clock (or not at all) rather than with a JS Date passed in

failures.title: Lesson step state lost on navigation
failures.symptom: Returning to a lesson after going back to the course restarts at the Guess step, on every course
failures.root_cause: Lesson step lived only in useState on the lesson screen; navigating back pops/unmounts it and the mount effect resets step to guess. Nothing persisted the learner's place; only graded attempts are saved server-side.
failures.fix_summary: Per-objective snapshot in AsyncStorage, restored after lesson load, validated by lessonProgress.parseSnapshot (lesson fingerprint, 7-day age, schema version)
failures.prevention_notes: Multi-step screen state that a learner would expect to survive navigation must be persisted, not held only in component state; the parse rules are unit tested

failures.title: Answered lesson check re-asked and recorded twice
failures.symptom: Answering a Guided or Solo check, leaving before Continue, and returning asked the same check again; answering again recorded a second attempt. A retry after a dropped connection could also record twice.
failures.root_cause: Graded result lived only in CheckStep component state, and /api/grade had no way to recognise a resubmission of the same answer, so every POST inserted an attempt and moved mastery.
failures.fix_summary: Check state saved with the lesson position; per-answer clientAttemptId with a unique index on attempts and replay of the stored result
failures.prevention_notes: Grading writes are idempotent per client attempt id; attempt-id reuse rules are unit tested

failures.title: Account export mislabelled every section from mastery on
failures.symptom: Export file put favorites under mastery, mastery under attempts, etc.; study sessions missing
failures.root_cause: Promise.all of 8 queries destructured positionally into 7 names after favorites query was added in REQ-082
failures.fix_summary: Queries keyed by section name in lib/account-export.ts
failures.prevention_notes: Section name and query live in one record so they cannot drift apart; integration test checks each section's rows

failures.title: Line B's Try it self-report would break on line A's lab constraint
failures.symptom: Merging #12 as written: POST /api/objectives/:id/lab inserted a kind 'lab' attempt with objective_id set, which A's 035 check attempts_lab_not_mastery_evidence (kind <> 'lab' or objective_id is null) rejects, so every 'I did it' would 500; A's latestLabReport would also have shown the self-report as a lab report.
failures.how_detected: merge review of A's constraints against B's insert
failures.root_cause: The two lines modelled the same kind 'lab' attempt differently and were developed apart: B kept the objective in objective_id; A moved lab rows to lab_objective_id precisely so they can never be read as mastery evidence. A textual merge has no conflict there, so nothing flagged it.
failures.fix_summary: recordLabCompletion writes lab_objective_id with objective_id null and format 'lab'; latestLabReport skips format 'lab'; the Try it step follows A's lab rules (plan, clinical/fitness acknowledgement).
failures.prevention_notes: When merging two lines, check every new INSERT against the other line's constraints on the same table; the release-merge dbtest runs the real insert against the merged schema.

failures.title: Rollback could not drop retired_at: a pre-release view depends on it
failures.symptom: The first rehearsal of scripts/rollback-release-2026-11-07.sql failed: cannot drop column retired_at of table course_units because view view_track_progress depends on it.
failures.how_detected: rehearsal step D (rollback on the production-state database)
failures.root_cause: 033 redefined two pre-release views (001/022) to read retired_at; a catalog diff of tables, columns, constraints, indexes, functions and triggers does not show a changed view definition.
failures.fix_summary: The rollback restores master's view_unit_mastery and view_track_progress definitions before dropping the columns; the rehearsal compares full schema dumps, so any other changed definition fails it.
failures.prevention_notes: Rollback scripts are tested by a full pg_dump --schema-only comparison, not a hand-written object list.

failures.title: Line B's 026 cannot run on plain Postgres (CI) without Supabase's roles
failures.symptom: 026_enable_rls.sql revokes from anon and authenticated; on the CI postgres:16 service those roles do not exist, so migrate --all would fail with 'role anon does not exist' and the database jobs would go red after the merge.
failures.how_detected: merge review against A's CI database jobs
failures.root_cause: Line B had no database CI job; the migration assumed Supabase, where the roles always exist.
failures.fix_summary: CI (database, backfill, rehearsal, live evals) creates the two roles NOLOGIN before migrating; 052 guards its own revoke on their existence. 026 itself is unchanged (production recorded it).
failures.no_test_reason: CI configuration; exercised by the rehearsal script, which creates the roles the same way.
failures.prevention_notes: Every database job applies migrations to a plain Postgres with the Supabase roles present.

failures.title: A lesson with a lab prompt offered the same lab twice (Try it step and Done-screen lab card)
failures.symptom: On the merged release, an objective with a lab_prompt showed B's optional Try it step after Solo and A's lab card on the Done screen, both with the same prompt and disclaimer.
failures.root_cause: Line B (#12, REQ-096) and line A (REQ-106) each built a lab entry point on objectives.lab_prompt. The 2026-11-07 merge reconciled their data model (FAIL-523) but kept both entry points, because the merge resolved code, not what the learner sees on one screen.
failures.fix_summary: tryItLab returns null when objectiveHasLab: the lab card (lab_prompt on a plan with labs, as GET /api/objectives/:id/lab returns it) or a build/case lab listed for the objective. The lesson GET then sends labPrompt null and the app shows no Try it step; POST /api/objectives/:id/lab answers 404.
regression_tests: backend/lib/release-merge.dbtest.ts::an objective whose Done screen shows the lab card offers no Try it step
backend/lib/release-merge.dbtest.ts::a lab the learner can see counts
failures.prevention_notes: Pre-completion checklist: after merging two lines, check each side's rule survived and that one screen does not show one thing twice.

failures.title: Merged lesson generation dropped line B's rule that practice questions see the teaching text
failures.symptom: lessonPracticePrompt was called without teach, so the 'Teaching text the learner has just read (test this; do not contradict it)' block was never sent; fade and solo checks were written blind to the lesson they follow and could test something it did not teach or contradict it.
failures.root_cause: Line A ran the intro and practice calls in parallel for latency; line B (#6, REQ-089) made the practice call depend on the intro's teach text. The merge kept A's runGeneration, and lessonPracticePrompt's teach parameter is optional, so dropping it type-checked and every test still passed.
failures.fix_summary: runGeneration awaits the intro, hands it to the caller, then calls practice with meta.teach = intro.teach; claudeGenerator.practice passes it to lessonPracticePrompt; checkedPractice's one retry inherits it. Validation, fact-check gate, holdbacks, leases and heartbeat unchanged. Evals mirror production.
regression_tests: backend/lib/audit3-ai.dbtest.ts::the practice prompt carries the teaching text the intro produced
backend/lib/lesson-regen.dbtest.ts::practice starts only after the intro finishes and is given its teaching text
backend/lib/lesson-regen.dbtest.ts::a held-back practice half is regenerated once
failures.prevention_notes: The mocked-model test fails if the practice prompt lacks the teaching text; checklist asks for each side's rule to be checked after a merge.

failures.title: Email-change 'this wasn't me' link stopped working 7 days after the request expired
failures.symptom: The retention purge deleted email_change_tokens 7 days after expires_at; cancelEmailChangeToken needs that row (cancel_token_hash), so a learner who found the alert later got 'already used' and their devices were not signed out.
failures.root_cause: The merge adopted line B's 7-day window for all one-time tokens; line A's cancel link (REQ-116) depends on the email_change_tokens row after expiry and was not considered when choosing the window.
failures.fix_summary: RETENTION.emailChangeDays = 30; purgeExpired deletes email_change_tokens 30 days after expiry and the other one-time tokens at 7 days as before. Privacy Policy and data inventory state the period.
regression_tests: backend/lib/release-merge.dbtest.ts::purge boundary: kept until 30 days after expiry
backend/lib/release-merge.dbtest.ts::the cancel link still works for a request that expired 8 days ago
backend/lib/retention.test.ts::privacy policy states the email-change request period (REQ-139)
failures.prevention_notes: Checklist: a retention window applies to every reader of the rows it deletes, mailed links included; retention.test.ts pins the policy text.

failures.title: A new review entry could be due at once when the server's local date was behind the database's
failures.symptom: mastery-integrity.dbtest.ts 'Only due review entries advance' failed (expected review_stage 0, got 1) when run in an evening in America/Los_Angeles and passed under UTC (CI); same failure on unmodified master. In production terms: a missed answer's review entry, meant to be first due tomorrow, could be due immediately, so the next correct answer advanced it early and skipped the 1-day review.
failures.how_detected: flaky local test run (TZ=America/Los_Angeles after 16:00 PST)
failures.root_cause: recordAttemptTx (backend/lib/grading-service.ts) and POST /api/errors (backend/app/api/errors/route.ts) computed next_review_at as tomorrow from new Date() + setDate, formatted with toDateOnlyString's local getters: the Node process's time zone. Every due check (grading-service, review-store, GET /api/errors, the review views) compares next_review_at <= current_date: the database session's zone (UTC in Supabase and CI). When Node's local date was a day behind the database's, 'tomorrow' equalled the database's today and the entry was due at once; a day ahead, it was due a day late. CI and Vercel run UTC, which hid it.
failures.fix_summary: Both inserts write next_review_at = current_date + 1 in SQL, so it is set and compared on one clock; the JS date and the toDateOnlyString imports are gone from those paths.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-integrity.dbtest.ts::a new review entry is first due tomorrow by the database's date
backend/lib/mastery-integrity.dbtest.ts::a correct answer leaves a not-yet-due entry alone and moves a due one exactly once
failures.prevention_notes: A date that SQL compares with current_date is computed in SQL (current_date + n), never from the Node process's local date; review-schedule code already uses UTC days (review-scheduler.ts utcDay). The regression test runs both writers under UTC-12 and UTC+14 and asserts one of them disagrees with the database's date, so it fails on the old code at any wall-clock time, including under TZ=UTC.

failures.title: Old store builds show an empty Solo multiple-choice list
failures.symptom: On the installed store app (built from c3e13ab) the lesson's Solo step showed Multiple choice / Free response with Multiple choice selected by default and no answer options: only a disabled Submit and the confidence picker. The learner was stuck unless they tapped Free response.
failures.how_detected: Owner report from production (phone, store build)
failures.root_cause: REQ-134 moved the Solo choices behind POST /api/objectives/:id/hint and sent soloChoices: [] in the lesson. FAIL-039 checked the old screen only for crashes (the .map on the hint button of an intermediate build); the store build has no hint flow and renders soloChoices directly as its default answer mode, so an empty list left it with nothing to pick. The server had no way to tell an old build from a new one, since the app sent no version.
failures.fix_summary: The app sends X-Ascendra-Client: 1 on every request (native and web; CORS allows it). The lesson GET/POST, for a request without it, records the Solo hint reveal (lesson_hint_reveals, same item key as the hint route) and then sends the Solo choices in the learner's fixed shuffled order (lessonForClient). /api/grade then accepts the old build's chosenIndex through the same order, and every Solo answer to the item is assisted, capped at Guided.
regression_tests: backend/lib/mastery-integrity.dbtest.ts::9b. Old app builds get the Solo choices
failures.prevention_notes: Before changing what a response carries, read the STORE build's screen (the last release that shipped to the stores, not the last merge), for how it renders the field, not only whether it dereferences it. The app now declares its protocol, so the server can keep serving old builds what they understand; raise CLIENT_PROTOCOL when a payload change needs it.

failures.title: Release rollback runbook gave a stale count of dropped tables
failures.symptom: docs/deploy-runbook-integration.md said the rollback script drops 59 tables while scripts/rollback-release-2026-11-07.sql dropped 61 on master (64 with migration 060).
failures.how_detected: review while adding migration 060's rollback lines
failures.root_cause: The count is hand-written prose next to the script; migrations that added tables to the drop list (055, 056, 058) edited the list and the parenthetical but not the number.
failures.fix_summary: Counted the tables in the script's drop list (63 with migration 060) and corrected the runbook.
failures.no_test_reason: Documentation number; the rehearsal compares schemas, not the prose count. The runbook now names which migrations' tables are in the list so the next edit sees the count beside them.
failures.prevention_notes: When a migration adds a table to the rollback drop list, update the runbook's table count in the same change (recount the list).

failures.title: Old app builds could never accept the Terms after the 2026-11-09 bump
failures.symptom: Agree and continue failed with 'version must be the current terms version (2026-11-09)'; the Terms gate looped on every app build that bundles TERMS_VERSION 2026-11-07
failures.root_cause: PR #67 bumped LEGAL_VERSIONS and the server accepted only CURRENT_TERMS_VERSION, assuming every client ships the new text at the same time. Installed native builds cannot be updated without an OTA (EXPO_TOKEN unset) or a store release, and cached web bundles lag too. The server had no way to tell an old build from a new one for this, and no update-required path, so the raw validation string reached learners.
failures.fix_summary: Clients send X-Ascendra-App; requests without it may accept the previous Terms version, recorded as sent, which satisfies their gate; headered clients still need the current one; MIN_APP_VERSION gives a 426 update_required with an Update required screen instead of raw errors
failures.prevention_notes: Pre-completion checklist: bumping a legal or protocol version moves the old value to PREVIOUS_LEGAL_VERSIONS and is checked against the installed builds (legacy clients without X-Ascendra-App); a version gate never returns a raw validation string to the app

failures.title: A wrong reauth password was refreshed and resent, spending two tries
failures.symptom: Typing a wrong password or code to confirm it's you (change email, MFA setup) counted twice against the 10-per-15-minutes reauth budget and rotated the refresh token
failures.root_cause: The API client treats every 401 outside /api/auth/* as an expired access token and refreshes then resends once. lib/auth/reauth.ts answers a wrong secret with 401 plus reauthRequired, which is about the input, not the session.
failures.fix_summary: client.ts skips the refresh-and-retry when the 401 body has reauthRequired: true (isReauthRefusal)
failures.prevention_notes: A 401 that means 'what you typed is wrong' carries reauthRequired and the client never refreshes on it

failures.title: Linux+ archive script exited 0 and miscounted when gzip failed
failures.symptom: With gzip failing, the model script printed 'archived 2 file(s)' and exited 0 (reproduced), although the brief requires a non-zero exit on any failure.
failures.root_cause: set -e does not fire for a command that fails on the left of && ('gzip ... && rm'), a well-known Bash exception the answer relied on without testing.
failures.fix_summary: Explicit 'if ! gzip ...; then rm partial .gz; die; fi' before removing the original; the explanation and rubric say why set -e alone is not enough.
regression_tests: backend/lib/labs-audit-comptia.test.ts::Linux+ archive script stops with exit 1 and keeps the log when gzip fails (FAIL-583)
failures.prevention_notes: The test extracts the model script and runs it against a failing gzip; scripts in model answers are executed, not read.

failures.title: Security+ V8 CVSS key used E:Attacked for a published exploit
failures.symptom: The brief said only that a working exploit had been published, which is E:P (POC) in CVSS v4.0 and scores 8.9 High, but the key gave E:A and 9.3 Critical.
failures.root_cause: Exploit Maturity values were taken as 'exploit exists = Attacked'; CVSS v4.0 reserves Attacked for reported attacks or exploit toolkits.
failures.fix_summary: Brief now states exploitation in the wild has been reported, so E:A and 9.3 hold; the answer adds E:P 8.9 and E:U 8.1 (computed with the cvss library).
regression_tests: backend/lib/labs-audit-comptia.test.ts::Security+ V8 CVSS lab: reported attacks justify E:A and the 9.3 key; a PoC alone is 8.9 (FAIL-584)
failures.prevention_notes: CVSS scores in labs are computed from the full vector with a calculator, and the brief must state the facts each metric value rests on.

failures.root_cause: The lab was written from long-standing (2009 ADA) values; the REQ-142 source pass found the disagreement but deliberately left the lab unchanged for a clinical reviewer, and no reviewer pass followed, so the wrong key stayed live.

failures.title: JavaScript lab's model-answer server crashed on a null body

failures.fix_summary: Reject a parsed value that is not a plain object with 422; collect Buffer chunks and count bytes; corrected the race-condition explanation (races need an await between read and write).
failures.prevention_notes: Model-answer code that a learner may copy is executed by a test, not only read.

failures.title: MSCS keys: password parameters below OWASP minimum, heap answer missing its premise

failures.root_cause: Parameters came from older defaults; the data-structure premise was implicit.
failures.fix_summary: Argon2id at m=19 MiB, t=2, p=1 and scrypt at N=2^17 with maxmem raised (both run); bcrypt as legacy; brief states scores only go up, answer says what to use otherwise.
failures.prevention_notes: Security parameters cite the current OWASP cheat sheet with a date; a model answer states every premise its correctness depends on in the brief.
