failures.title: Seeded sim documents named objectives that are not in their course catalogs
failures.symptom: npm run seed failed: sims: CCRNADULT has 0 active objectives titled 'Cardiac tamponade: recognising it in the post-operative patient and escalating to the surgeon'; the TicketBurst base also named three secondary objectives that are not AWSSAA titles
failures.how_detected: first seed of migration 062 on a fresh Postgres 16
failures.root_cause: Phase 1a ported the prototypes as engine-only documents and never seeded them, so nothing resolved a document's objective title against the catalog; the titles were written from the prototypes, not copied from the course
failures.fix_summary: Pointed tamponade at 'Care of the patient after cardiac surgery' (tamponade and hemodynamic monitoring as secondary) and the TicketBurst secondary objectives at AWSSAA titles; the seed refuses a title that does not match exactly one active objective
failures.prevention_notes: Every seeded sim document's objective and secondary objectives must be exact catalog titles; objectives.test.ts checks this without a database

failures.title: Email link scanners spent verification links on GET; set_password links cleared the password for the scanner
failures.symptom: Clicking the verification link said 'This verification link is invalid or has expired' for users behind Outlook Safe Links or a corporate mail gateway; for a REQ-116 set_password link the password was cleared and the one-hour reset link was shown only to the scanner
failures.root_cause: app/verify-email/page.tsx called verifyEmailToken during the GET render. Mail security scanners prefetch every link in a message, so the scanner's GET spent the single-use token before the person clicked. GET must be safe: a link that changes state needs a deliberate POST.
failures.fix_summary: GET only reads the token (inspectVerifyToken) and renders a 'Verify my email' button; a server action (POST) spends it and redirects to ?result=; set_password results carry the reset token so that page links to the reset form. A used link on a verified account says 'Your email is already verified. You can log in.'
failures.prevention_notes: Pages opened from email links render a confirm button on GET and change state only on POST; tests call the page component and assert nothing was written

failures.title: 'Check your email' screen claimed a link was sent after a login refused for an unverified email
failures.symptom: After login answered 403 'Please verify your email', the app showed 'Verification link sent ... We sent a verification link to <address>' though the login sent nothing; no hint that a reset also recovers the account
failures.root_cause: login.tsx and register.tsx both routed to verify-email-pending.tsx with only the address, and the screen's copy was written for the sign-up case
failures.fix_summary: Screens pass from=login|register; copy comes from src/lib/verifyEmailPending.ts; resend is the primary action after a refused login; Forgot password offered on the screen

failures.title: Email-change confirm and cancel links were spent on GET; a scanner opening the cancel link signed every device out
failures.symptom: A scanner prefetch of the confirm-email-change link applied the change before the person clicked (their click then said invalid); a prefetch of the cancel link in the alert cancelled the change and revoked every session
failures.root_cause: Same GET-spends pattern as FAIL-670: both pages called the consuming function while rendering
failures.fix_summary: GET reads only (inspectEmailChangeToken, inspectCancelToken) and shows a button; server actions spend the tokens

failures.title: A completed password reset left an unverified account locked out (login 403)
failures.symptom: A learner whose verification mail never arrived could reset the password but login still answered 403 'Please verify your email before logging in.'
failures.root_cause: reset-password set the password and revoked sessions but never recorded that the reset link, opened from the inbox, proves the address; recovery and verification were treated as unrelated
failures.fix_summary: The reset transaction sets email_verified_at = coalesce(email_verified_at, now()) and spends pending verification links (a leftover set_password link would otherwise clear the new password)
regression_tests: backend/lib/email-verification.dbtest.ts::forgot password then reset then log in (FAIL-673)

failures.title: Resend send failures were silent: routes said 'check your email' when nothing was sent
failures.symptom: Sign-up, resend, reset and MFA-code requests all reported success while no mail went out; nothing in Vercel logs
failures.how_detected: review (lead) and production data: a 2026-11-08 sign-up with two unused verification tokens
failures.root_cause: The Resend SDK returns { data, error } and does not throw on a refused send (bad sender, unverified domain, quota). lib/email.ts awaited emails.send() and ignored the result, so a 403 from the resend.dev test sender looked like a delivered mail.
failures.fix_summary: send() checks the result and throws EmailSendError (kind, code, status; no address, token or provider message); enumeration-safe routes log email_send_failed and keep their generic answers; serverError maps EmailSendError to 503 for signed-in routes; best-effort alerts log instead of swallowing
failures.prevention_notes: An SDK that reports failure in its return value is checked at the call; a test drives the real Resend client with a refused response

failures.title: Production sends mail from Resend's test sender and nothing reported it
failures.symptom: Real users received no verification, reset or MFA mail; /api/health said ok
failures.root_cause: EMAIL_FROM is unset in production, so lib/email.ts falls back to onboarding@resend.dev, which Resend delivers only to the Resend account's own address. The health check (REQ-118) checked RESEND_API_KEY but not the sender.
failures.fix_summary: /api/health reports email: unconfigured with a warning in production while EMAIL_FROM is unset or @resend.dev. Owner action still open: verify the domain in Resend and set EMAIL_FROM (docs/operations-runbook.md, Email sender).

failures.title: Logout with biometric unlock left the server session live for up to 30 days
failures.symptom: With biometric unlock on, Log out cleared the device but never called /api/auth/logout; the refresh token family stayed valid server-side until expiry (30 days)
failures.root_cause: endSession returned early when biometrics were on: revoking would have left the biometric-sealed copy of the token behind, and replaying a revoked token next launch reads as theft and revokes the whole family. The fix chosen was to keep the session live instead of deleting the sealed copy with it, and the launch decided 'locked' from the preference alone, so it had no way to know no session was left.
failures.fix_summary: Logout always revokes server-side: with the refresh token, or with only the access token (POST /api/auth/logout ends that token's family). The sealed copy is deleted and ascendra_biometric_session=0 makes the next launch go to sign-in; the biometric preference stays and the next sign-in seals the new session.
failures.prevention_notes: Every sign-out path revokes on the server before clearing local state, whatever the device stores

failures.title: Sheets and dialogs drew above the lock screen
failures.symptom: An open menu, date picker, confirmation or the What's new / study notice sheet stayed visible and tappable above the lock after time away
failures.root_cause: React Native's Modal is its own native window (a portal on web), so no view in the main tree, the lock overlay included, can draw above it. REQ-177 drew the lock as an overlay to keep screens mounted and did not account for open Modals.
failures.fix_summary: All Modals go through SheetModal, which sets visible=false while the lock is up; the component that opened the sheet stays mounted so it returns after unlock.
failures.prevention_notes: Static test fails if any screen or component renders a raw <Modal>

failures.title: Web refresh token readable by any injected script (sessionStorage)
failures.symptom: The web app kept its 30-day refresh token in sessionStorage, where any script running in the page could read and exfiltrate it
failures.root_cause: expo-secure-store has no web implementation; secureStorage routed web to sessionStorage for its browser-session lifetime, and the backend only accepted the refresh token in a JSON body, so there was no httpOnly option.
failures.fix_summary: Web sign-in and refresh set an HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict browser-session cookie on /api/auth/refresh and omit refreshToken from the body; cookie use requires our Origin and the platform header; old sessionStorage tokens are deleted and exchanged once.
failures.prevention_notes: Sign-in and refresh routes answer through sessionResponse; cookie readers check cookieRequestAllowed

failures.title: A retired objective's lesson could still be served or generated by direct id
failures.symptom: Retired objectives (REQ-102 retired_at) were left out of every listing, but GET/POST /api/objectives/:id/lesson served a stored lesson for one and, on a miss, called the model to generate one -- for the retired CMPCBS degree-plan lines that would have written a new lesson on removed degree-plan content.
failures.how_detected: review while retiring CMPCBS degree-plan objectives (REQ-195)
failures.root_cause: Retirement was enforced only in listing queries (isActive in course, unit, review, prefetch); visibleObjective answered only 'may this caller see it', and the lesson route and ensureGeneration had no notion of retired.
failures.fix_summary: visibleObjective returns retired; the lesson route answers 404 for a retired objective before reading or generating; loadObjective carries retired and ensureGeneration throws RetiredObjectiveError as a backstop.
regression_tests: backend/lib/cmpcbs-general-courses.dbtest.ts::GET and POST on a retired objective answer 404 even with a stored lesson; nothing is generated
backend/lib/cmpcbs-general-courses.dbtest.ts::a single retired line inside a unit that stays is not served either
failures.prevention_notes: Retired is now part of the objective lookup every lesson route uses, and generation refuses a retired objective itself.

failures.title: CMPCBS presented one university's degree plan and name as our product
failures.symptom: The CMPCBS track's description named the university and its 2026-2027 degree plan; units carried its course codes and gates citing its grade rules; 20 objectives were degree-plan logistics (elective lists, residency credits) whose lessons taught plan placement, not a subject; the labs cited the university's catalog.
failures.root_cause: REQ-142/161 built the track by mirroring a published degree completion plan rather than defining general courses, so plan logistics and the school's marks became course content; REQ-187 then authored lessons for the logistics instead of removing them.
failures.fix_summary: Track renamed Computer Science Degree Foundations; course units retitled as general courses with dated open-textbook sources; composition and two neutral religion surveys reframed in place with authored sourced lessons; 17 logistics objectives retired (6 whole units plus 3 lines via the new per-objective objectiveRetiredAt), no row moved; labs cite open texts.
regression_tests: the course lists only what is taught
failures.prevention_notes: The REQ-195 tests refuse the school's name anywhere in the track or its labs and course codes in active titles, gates and objectives, and pin the row shape so content can only be retired, not removed or reordered.

failures.title: Pre-gate re-check ran as the production owner with the app's key and pulled items itself
failures.symptom: content-recheck.yml used PROD_DATABASE_URL (owner, bypasses RLS) and secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; apply inserted item_status 'quarantined' directly and logged calls to ai_calls
failures.root_cause: REQ-187 R6 reused the lesson-fixes pattern (owner URL, direct quarantine) for a job whose decisions come from a model, so a checker false positive pulled live content with no person in the loop, and its spend shared the app's key and caps
failures.fix_summary: Runs as a LOGIN member of content_recheck (migration 064) via RECHECK_DATABASE_URL, refuses privileged roles (lib/recheck-guard.ts), stages findings in item_holdbacks only, estimate/check/apply modes with a hard dollar budget, usage tallied in-job (lib/run-budget.ts), separate RECHECK_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
failures.prevention_notes: sandbox.test.ts fails if a job file writes item_status or calls confirm/clear; the guard refuses any role that can write item_status or content

failures.title: Verify by execution had no sandbox: R4/P7 was inert in production
failures.symptom: claudeGenerator.runCode was unavailableVerifier, so no verification program ever ran and a program-detectable wrong key was never caught
failures.root_cause: Running model-written code inside a Vercel request needs an isolated runner that did not exist; REQ-187 shipped the interface only
failures.fix_summary: Programs are queued in exec_checks (exec_unverified) at store time, fail closed if queueing fails; hourly content-sandbox.yml runs them in docker --network none (lib/sandbox-runner.ts) after escape tests and stages disagreements
failures.prevention_notes: sandbox.test.ts walks app/ imports and fails if the request path reaches the runner, child_process, vm or eval

failures.title: Hourly sandbox workflow passed green with no database secret
failures.symptom: content-sandbox.yml (interrupted draft) printed a notice and exited 0 when RECHECK_DATABASE_URL was unset, so a missing setup looked healthy every hour
failures.how_detected: review of the uncommitted REQ-196 work
failures.root_cause: Draft chose a soft skip to avoid hourly failure noise, contradicting the decision that the workflow refuses to run without the secret
failures.fix_summary: First step fails with an error naming the secret and the runbook section; the queue step has no skip branch; added a max_minutes time budget
failures.no_test_reason: Workflow YAML; checked with actionlint and by reading the step, no workflow test harness in the repo
failures.prevention_notes: Runbook states both workflows fail at their first step until the secret exists

failures.title: omni gate failed on a commit message citing another branch's requirement ID
failures.symptom: After the REQ-198 commit, omni gate failed: controlled.requirement_id REQ-189 cited in a commit message but not found in .ai/requirements/requirements.json
failures.how_detected: omni gate run after the map commit
failures.root_cause: The commit message named REQ-189 (interactive labs), which is registered only on the unmerged feature/interactive-labs branch, not on master, which this branch is based on. The gate checked before committing (it passed) but not after, and the gate output was piped through tail, so its failure did not stop the next command.
affected: commit message of the REQ-198 main commit
failures.fix_summary: Reworded the unpushed commit message to name the branch (feature/interactive-labs) instead of the ID, and re-applied the map commit unchanged (tree identical). The gate passes.
failures.no_test_reason: Process slip in a commit message. The gate already catches it; no code changed.
failures.prevention_notes: Cite only requirement IDs that exist in the base branch's registry, and refer to unmerged work by branch name. Run omni gate after the last commit, without a pipe that hides its exit status.

failures.title: A sim notice announcing a reload was wiped by that reload
failures.symptom: After a desync, useSimRun set 'The run was out of step with the server and has been reloaded from the server's copy.' and then called start(false), whose first step is setNotice(null); the learner saw no explanation for the run jumping
failures.how_detected: code review while wiring the journal into useSimRun
failures.root_cause: start() reset every piece of screen state, including the notice line, and the callers set their notice before calling it; React applied both updates in order, so the reset won
failures.fix_summary: start(restart, carry?) takes the notice to show after the reload; every reload with an explanation (desync, refused command, discarded journal) passes it
failures.no_test_reason: the bug lives in React state ordering inside a hook that needs React Native to run; the mobile suite runs pure modules under node --test with no renderer
failures.prevention_notes: A caller that reloads the run passes its message through start's carry argument instead of setting the notice first

failures.title: A sim sync sent every unsent command in one request, past the step route's 500-command limit
failures.symptom: useSimRun.flush posted s.pending whole; with more than 500 unsent commands (a long offline stretch, now also a long journal) the step route answers 400 and the app retried the same oversized batch forever with 'Not saved to the server yet'
failures.how_detected: review of the step route's limits while designing journal replay
failures.root_cause: the app and server limits were written separately; nothing tied the app's send size to SIM_LIMITS.commandsPerRequest
failures.fix_summary: flush sends at most SEND_BATCH (500) commands and sends the next batch after each acknowledgement
regression_tests: mobile/src/sim/journal.test.ts::a send never exceeds the step route's per-request limit
and a journal never exceeds a run
failures.prevention_notes: SEND_BATCH and JOURNAL_MAX_COMMANDS are pinned to the server's SIM_LIMITS by a test that imports both

failures.title: Study paths could recommend a course REQ-194 hid
failures.symptom: With REQ-198 and REQ-194 merged, GET /api/courses/:id/path still listed a catalog course whose hidden_at had passed as the step before or after
failures.root_cause: REQ-198's coursePaths resolved path codes against every catalog row; it was written before migration 065 added subject_tracks.hidden_at, so it had no hidden filter. Neither branch could see the other.
failures.fix_summary: The lookup leaves out catalog courses whose hidden_at has passed, except the course being viewed
failures.prevention_notes: A dbtest pins that a hidden course is skipped as a step and still shows its own path

failures.title: GCP DevOps exam-change email said the course was not rewritten
failures.symptom: backend npm test failed in exam-changes.test.ts ('' !== '2026-11-23'); the notice text told learners the course had not been rewritten for the 2026-11-23 guide
failures.root_cause: REQ-197 wrote its notice and test against the course before #81 (REQ-183) re-authored it to the new guide and removed its review date. The notice restates course state that another branch changed.
failures.fix_summary: courseDid says the new sections are new units and the old units retire on November 23; the test checks the effective date, retire day and new weights
failures.prevention_notes: The notice test reads the seed, so a later course change fails it until the notice is updated

failures.title: Sim feature gates passed env where #73 now takes the course
failures.symptom: backend tsc failed in lib/sims.ts (3 calls): ProcessEnv is not assignable to CourseRef
failures.root_cause: #73 (REQ-170) inserted a course argument before env in hasFeature and requireFeature so plans are read per category; REQ-190 called the old signature. At runtime the env object would have been read as the course reference.
failures.fix_summary: simAccess and gateSim pass sim.track_id; listSims passes its scope, as lib/labs.ts does
failures.prevention_notes: Typecheck on the integrated tree; course-scoped gates take a CourseRef

failures.title: The sim sheet drew above the app lock
failures.symptom: mobile npm test failed: 'no screen or component opens a raw React Native Modal' listed src/sim/SimPanels.tsx
failures.root_cause: REQ-190's sim Sheet used React Native's Modal, written before REQ-192 (FAIL-691) required every sheet to go through SheetModal; a raw Modal is its own window and shows above the lock overlay
failures.fix_summary: The sim Sheet uses SheetModal, hidden while the lock is up
failures.prevention_notes: The FAIL-691 static test catches any raw Modal

failures.title: A billed model answer that failed to parse was recorded at zero cost
failures.symptom: callClaudeStructured used messages.parse; a reply that was cut off or off-schema was logged in ai_calls with no tokens, so its cost never counted against any budget
failures.how_detected: pre-launch audit batch F1 (review of commit 00a3a70)
failures.root_cause: messages.parse throws on an unparseable answer before the response (and its usage) reaches loggedCall, which reads usage from the returned value
failures.fix_summary: Structured calls use messages.create and parse the text locally inside loggedCall's check, so usage is recorded whether the check passes or not (error codes invalid_structured_output, no_parsed_output)
failures.prevention_notes: lib/ai-spend-gate.test.ts enumerates every model call site and route from the source and fails on a new one that bypasses the gate

failures.title: About 13 model routes had no per-learner spend check at all
failures.symptom: Grade, pbq, lab steps and report, guess-feedback, explain-back, unit checks, review, coach quiz and item re-checks called the model with no requireAiBudget or requireAiAllowance, so a free account could spend without a cap
failures.how_detected: pre-launch audit batch F1 (review of commit 00a3a70)
failures.root_cause: The checks were per route and written for chat and regenerate; grading was exempted on the argument that it is cheap, and a new route copying a grading route inherited the exemption
failures.fix_summary: One gate inside loggedCall for every call with a userId, two daily pools (coach, grading) so grading has its own allowance rather than an exemption; userId is a required CallOptions field so a new call site cannot omit it
failures.prevention_notes: lib/ai-spend-gate.test.ts enumerates every model call site and route from the source and fails on a new one that bypasses the gate

failures.title: A learner could start sprints that generated about 960 Sonnet batches a day
failures.symptom: createSession checked only a count (40 an hour) before generating, and only mock exams called requireFeature, so a loop of sprints made about 960 writer calls plus fact-checks a day on a free account
failures.how_detected: pre-launch audit batch F1 (review of commit 00a3a70)
failures.root_cause: The cost of generation was bounded by a rate, never by money, and the budget check was never part of the session build
failures.fix_summary: createSession looks at the budget first (canAffordAiSpend) and builds from the bank only when the learner cannot afford a generation; each call also reserves its own cost; GENERATION_RATE is 12 an hour
failures.prevention_notes: lib/ai-spend-gate.test.ts enumerates every model call site and route from the source and fails on a new one that bypasses the gate

failures.title: The first shared lesson generation was charged to nobody, and could be started 2,880 times a day
failures.symptom: The first generation of a lesson passed userId undefined to the model, so no budget saw it; the GET and prefetch rate was 20 per 10 minutes
failures.how_detected: pre-launch audit batch F1 (review of commit 00a3a70)
failures.root_cause: The shared lesson serves everyone, so it was recorded with no learner; the same went for lab questions and course insights
failures.fix_summary: GenerationOptions.triggeredBy charges it to the learner whose request started it; lab questions and insights take the triggering learner; the rate is 20 an hour
failures.prevention_notes: lib/ai-spend-gate.test.ts enumerates every model call site and route from the source and fails on a new one that bypasses the gate

failures.title: Parallel requests overshot the daily AI budget
failures.symptom: N requests sent at once each read spend under the cap and all went through, so a learner could spend N calls past the budget
failures.how_detected: pre-launch audit batch F1 (review of commit 00a3a70)
failures.root_cause: The check read the spend and reserved nothing; the cost was only recorded after the call returned
failures.fix_summary: Before each call its worst-case cost is reserved as an ai_calls row under a per-learner advisory lock and settled in place with the real usage
failures.prevention_notes: lib/ai-spend-gate.test.ts enumerates every model call site and route from the source and fails on a new one that bypasses the gate

failures.title: The spend checks failed open when the database errored
failures.symptom: A database error while reading spend counted as zero spend (ai-budget.ts, entitlements.ts monthly cap), so the cap disappeared while the database was failing
failures.how_detected: pre-launch audit batch F1 (review of commit 00a3a70)
failures.root_cause: The reads ended in .catch(() => 0), chosen so a logging problem would never block a learner, and applied to enforcement as well
failures.fix_summary: The gate, requireAiBudget and requireAiAllowance throw AiSpendUnavailableError (503) when the spend cannot be read; the plan summary display keeps the soft answer; only a missing ai_calls table counts as no spend
failures.prevention_notes: lib/ai-spend-gate.test.ts enumerates every model call site and route from the source and fails on a new one that bypasses the gate

failures.title: Item re-checks were uncharged and uncapped
failures.symptom: Each report could start a Sonnet re-check with no userId, and a learner could send 480 reports a day
failures.how_detected: pre-launch audit batch F1 (review of commit 00a3a70)
failures.root_cause: recheckItem was written as shared background work; the report rate limit bounded reports, not re-checks
failures.fix_summary: The re-check is charged to the reporter and each learner may start 10 a day; past that the claim is given back and the report stands
failures.prevention_notes: lib/ai-spend-gate.test.ts enumerates every model call site and route from the source and fails on a new one that bypasses the gate

failures.title: The Anthropic client had a 10-minute timeout and two retries, and AI routes had no maxDuration
failures.symptom: A hung request could hold a function and a connection for half an hour, and a flaky upstream triple a call's cost
failures.how_detected: pre-launch audit batch F1 (review of commit 00a3a70)
failures.root_cause: The SDK defaults were never set
failures.fix_summary: Client timeout 90 s with one retry; the AI routes export maxDuration (60 to 300, at most the Hobby plan ceiling with Fluid compute)
failures.prevention_notes: lib/ai-spend-gate.test.ts enumerates every model call site and route from the source and fails on a new one that bypasses the gate

failures.title: Pre-generated practice questions were written without the teaching text
failures.symptom: A pre-generated lesson's practice half was requested in the same batch as its intro, so it never saw the teaching text; the questions could test or contradict something the learner was not taught.
failures.how_detected: REQ-208 pipeline comparison (docs/release-2026-11-07.md named it a follow-up)
failures.root_cause: REQ-139 (FAIL-527) changed the app to write teach first and practice from it, but the batch script still built both halves independently; nothing compared the two pipelines.
failures.fix_summary: Two batches: collect of the ended intro batch checks the teaching text and builds the practice requests from it (lessonPracticePrompt teach), collect of the practice batch saves.
failures.prevention_notes: Any generation path that exists beside the app's lesson route is compared with runGeneration (order, inputs, checks) in the same change; pre-completion checklist item on parallel generation entry points.

failures.title: Pre-generation never asked for or queued a verification program
failures.symptom: Python, JavaScript and academic lessons made by the batch carried no soloVerification program and queued no exec check (REQ-196).
failures.root_cause: The request omitted verify: wantsVerification(ctx) and the save path did not call queueExecCheck.
failures.fix_summary: practiceParams passes verify for the course; saving goes through checkedPractice with queueExec, which queues the program and holds the half back if it cannot be queued.
failures.prevention_notes: Saving goes through the app's own checkedIntro/checkedPractice, so a gate added there applies here.

failures.title: Pre-generation fact-check drifted from the app's gate
failures.symptom: The batch path fact-checked with no course context and the objective's id as its title, did not shuffle the stored answer position, and treated an item with no verdict as passing.
failures.root_cause: The gate was re-implemented inline in collect instead of calling the app's code; the inline copy filtered the verdict map's values, so a missing verdict was never seen.
failures.fix_summary: Collect shuffles with shufflePractice, then runs checkedPractice (ctx, objective title, missing verdict fails, holdback rows) with a generator that refuses the app's one retry.
failures.prevention_notes: No second copy of a gate: call checkedIntro/checkedPractice.

failures.title: Hidden courses and authored objectives were not excluded from pre-generation
failures.symptom: A course hidden by REQ-194 hidden_at would be paid for, and an objective with an authored lesson would be generated although the app never generates it.
failures.root_cause: The selection query predates hidden_at (migration 065) and authored lessons (REQ-195) and was not updated with them.
failures.fix_summary: One selection (selectCandidates) filters shared tracks, hidden_at passed, retired unit or objective, any lesson row, authored; collect re-applies it.
failures.prevention_notes: After a visibility column or a never-generate rule is added, every reader of the table is checked (pre-completion checklist, FAIL-200).

failures.title: Collecting a batch could overwrite a voided or corrected lesson and ignored later retirement
failures.symptom: saveLesson replaces a shared lesson whose check was pulled, so a lesson voided by the lessons:fix workflow after submit would have been replaced by the batch's text; an objective retired after submit was still saved.
failures.root_cause: Collect trusted the objective list from submit time and relied on saveLesson, whose conflict rule is written for the app's regenerate, not for a bulk insert.
failures.fix_summary: Collect re-selects eligible objectives, skips any with a lesson row of any kind, re-checks right before the write, and counts skipped.
failures.prevention_notes: A bulk writer states its overwrite rule and tests it against a pulled row.

failures.title: Pre-generation skipped the check of the teaching text's own uncertainty
failures.symptom: Teaching text the writer flagged as uncertain (REQ-187 P8) could be stored; only the practice half was checked.
failures.root_cause: The batch script predates P8 and checked uncertaintyOf on the practice half only.
failures.fix_summary: Stage 1 runs checkedIntro on every intro; an unsure one is logged as a lesson_intro holdback and not continued.
failures.prevention_notes: Same as FAIL-972.

failures.title: Pre-generation spend was not in ai_calls and its log writes could be lost
failures.symptom: Batch usage was never written to ai_calls, so daily totals missed it; the live fact-check rows are written without being awaited and the script closed the pool right after, so rows could be lost.
failures.root_cause: Batch results were read for lessons only; ai_calls logging assumes a long-lived server. A first version of the new insert also failed on an untyped parameter and logged only a warning, caught by the test.
failures.fix_summary: Batch usage is recorded once per batch and model as purpose pregen (idempotent, dated at batch end); fact-checks use purpose pregen_fact_check; flushAiCallLog() waits for pending writes before exit.
failures.prevention_notes: A script that calls the model awaits flushAiCallLog before closing the pool.

failures.title: A pre-generation run would have counted toward the global daily AI ceiling
failures.symptom: A planned $50 run recorded in ai_calls would reach the recommended $5 AI_GLOBAL_DAILY_CEILING_USD at once and pause chat, regenerate and first-time shared lessons for every learner for the rest of the UTC day.
failures.root_cause: The ceiling sums every ai_calls row; pregen is owner-started and has its own cap, which the sum cannot tell.
failures.fix_summary: globalSpendSinceUsd leaves out purposes starting pregen; the rows stay in the table; documented in docs/billing.md.
failures.prevention_notes: A new purpose that is not learner-driven says whether it counts toward the ceiling.

failures.title: Pre-generation would have printed model text into the CI log
failures.symptom: recordHoldback prints the first claims of a held-back item with console.warn; in a workflow log that is model-written content.
failures.how_detected: REQ-208 review of the workflow log
failures.root_cause: The warning was written for a server log; the workflow's rule is counts only.
failures.fix_summary: Collect suppresses [item-quality] warnings while it runs, prints failure causes as categories, and keeps the claims in item_holdbacks.
failures.prevention_notes: A job whose log is shared prints counts only; tests assert that planted claims and teaching text never appear.

failures.title: Pre-generation had no spend cap, a typical-cost estimate and no guard against a second submit
failures.symptom: The estimate was a typical figure (about 2 cents a lesson, batch only, no fact-check), submit had no cap, could take the whole catalog, could run twice, and used ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (the app's) with a state file that cannot survive a CI runner.
failures.root_cause: The script was written to be run by hand by a developer who watches the bill.
failures.fix_summary: Upper-bound estimate (max_tokens, discount, fact-check), --max-usd with a whole-unit priority cutoff checked again on the built requests, tracks and cap required to submit, refusal while a batch runs, a dedicated key and no state file.
failures.prevention_notes: Anything that spends money has a cap that is an upper bound and a test of the refusal.

failures.title: The global daily AI ceiling did not stop most model paths after F1 and batch 10 were merged
failures.symptom: With AI_GLOBAL_DAILY_CEILING_USD reached, exam item generation, item re-checks, review writing, quiz questions, PBQ and unit-check writing, labs and shared lesson generation still reached the model; only chat, regenerate and a first lesson were stopped, by their routes
failures.how_detected: B11 merge of F1 onto batch 10: typecheck, then reading the hook F1 left for batch 10
failures.root_cause: F1 built the spend gate with a no-op setGlobalCeilingCheck hook for batch 10 to fill, and batch 10 was built on batch 9 without the gate. Neither branch contained the call from one to the other, so the merge was textually clean and the ceiling covered only the three routes that checked it themselves (REQ-201's own risk note listed the rest as open)
failures.fix_summary: The gate's default hook is now the REQ-201 ceiling, lazily imported: every call that writes or checks content is refused with a 429 paused AiAccessError and no model request; owners, the grading pool (REQ-201: grading never stops) and purposes starting pregen (REQ-208) stay open; with no ceiling set it reads nothing
failures.prevention_notes: ai-spend-ceiling.test.ts walks every AiPurpose, so a new purpose is either blocked or on the exempt list by its pool; the dbtest drives the real sprint, first-lesson, re-check and review calls through the real ceiling sum. The pre-completion checklist now names hooks one branch leaves for another

failures.title: A ceiling reached part-way through a sprint was reported as a failed generation
failures.symptom: When the global ceiling was reached between the sprint's affordability check and its first generation call (the ceiling sum is cached 60 s), the learner got a 409 'couldn't be prepared just now' instead of the paused 429
failures.how_detected: B11 merge of F1 onto batch 10: typecheck, then reading the hook F1 left for batch 10
failures.root_cause: exam-sessions.ts treated only AiBudgetError as a spend refusal; the ceiling throws AiAccessError, a different class from the same gate, so it was counted as a real generation failure
failures.fix_summary: Both refusal classes mean paused: the session is built from the bank, and with nothing in the bank the original AiAccessError is thrown
failures.prevention_notes: A refusal the gate can raise is handled by every caller that special-cases refusals (grep instanceof AiBudgetError when adding one); the dbtest pins the mid-sprint case

failures.title: Pre-generation (REQ-208) did not compile against the spend gate and broke its purpose-union test
failures.symptom: Typecheck failed on the merged tree: Record<AiPurpose, AiPool> lacked pregen and pregen_fact_check, and the request builders in lib/pregen.ts lacked the now-required userId. The union scanner in ai-spend-gate.test.ts then counted pregen twice
failures.how_detected: B11 merge of F1 onto batch 10: typecheck, then reading the hook F1 left for batch 10
failures.root_cause: REQ-208 added purposes and call sites on a base without REQ-202's required userId option and purpose-to-pool map; the scanner read the text up to the next interface and picked up REQ-208's PREGEN_PURPOSE_PREFIX constant that now sits between them
failures.fix_summary: Both pregen purposes are in the coach pool (never reserved: no learner), pre-generation passes userId null, and the scanner stops at the union's own semicolon
failures.prevention_notes: tsc fails on the merged tree for a missing pool and a missing userId; the scanner no longer depends on what follows the union

failures.title: A stolen access token could enroll the attacker's authenticator
failures.symptom: With MFA off, POST /api/auth/mfa/setup and /enable needed only an access token, so a thief could add their own authenticator and lock the owner out.
failures.root_cause: Reauthentication was required only when mfa_enabled was already true; the first factor on an account was unprotected.
failures.fix_summary: setup requires checkReauth whenever the account has any proof method (hasReauthProof); enable refuses a pending secret that wasn't started with proof; enabling emails a security alert.
failures.prevention_notes: A route that adds or replaces a sign-in method asks for proof whenever the account has one (pre-completion checklist, Auth and abuse)

failures.title: A stolen access token could link any Google identity
failures.symptom: POST /api/auth/oauth/google/link attached any verified Google identity with only an access token, no alert and no email match; that identity then signs in as the account.
failures.root_cause: The route authenticated the session but never asked the owner to confirm, and sent nothing to the account address.
failures.fix_summary: checkReauth before the token is verified; a security alert naming the Google address after a new link. Requiring the Google address to equal the account address is left to the owner (product decision).
failures.prevention_notes: Same checklist line: adding a sign-in method needs proof and tells the owner

failures.title: The pending email-MFA code could be guessed without limit
failures.symptom: POST /api/auth/mfa/email/enable had no attempt limit on the 6-digit code, valid for 10 minutes.
failures.root_cause: The route compared the code and returned 401 with nothing counting or limiting misses.
failures.fix_summary: consumeRateLimit 5 per 10 minutes; the fifth wrong code clears the pending code; a success clears the count.
failures.prevention_notes: Any single-use code comparison sits behind consumeRateLimit and is dropped after its last try

failures.title: Backup-code regeneration allowed unlimited password guesses
failures.symptom: POST /api/auth/mfa/backup-codes checked the password with no rate limit.
failures.root_cause: It called verifyPassword directly instead of spending the shared REAUTH_EVENT budget like change-password and unlock.
failures.fix_summary: consumeRateLimit(REAUTH_EVENT) before verifyPassword; the wrong-password 401 carries reauthRequired.
failures.prevention_notes: Every password or code check outside login spends the REAUTH_EVENT budget

failures.title: The eleventh correct unlock in 15 minutes was refused
failures.symptom: The app lock asks for the password on each return from the background; after 10 successful unlocks in 15 minutes the next correct one returned 429.
failures.root_cause: checkReauth counted every attempt, right or wrong, against the 10-per-15-minute lockout meant for wrong guesses.
failures.fix_summary: An attempt is still counted while it is checked (concurrent guesses stay capped) and given back (refundRateLimit) when it proves correct; successes have their own 120-per-15-minutes ceiling (REAUTH_SUCCESS_EVENT).
failures.prevention_notes: A lockout budget counts failures; successes get a separate ceiling

failures.title: Two tabs refreshing together signed the learner out everywhere
failures.symptom: Two simultaneous cookie refreshes presented the same token; the loser looked like token theft and revoked the whole family.
failures.root_cause: rotateRefreshToken treated any already-revoked token as reuse, with no allowance for a cross-tab race.
failures.fix_summary: A token replayed within REFRESH_REUSE_GRACE_SECONDS (10) of its own rotation, while its family is live, gets its own live token (at most 6 per rotation, one guarded statement); later replays revoke the family as before. auth-races and session-cookie tests keep the family revoke outside the window.
failures.prevention_notes: Reuse detection tests must say which side of the grace window they exercise

failures.title: Logout with an expired access token returned 400 and the session stayed live
failures.symptom: POST /api/auth/logout with only a stale access token (the normal case after time away) answered 400 refreshToken is required, leaving the refresh family alive for up to 30 days.
failures.root_cause: The bearer path used requireUser, which refuses expired and version-stale tokens.
failures.fix_summary: verifyAccessTokenForLogout accepts a token this server signed, past expiry but no older than 30 days, and revokes its family scoped to its user.
failures.prevention_notes: Sign-out paths accept what a stale client holds (pre-completion checklist, Sessions)

failures.title: Logout with an already-rotated refresh token left the successor live
failures.symptom: POST /api/auth/logout, and web DELETE /api/auth/refresh, with a token that had already rotated revoked only that spent token.
failures.root_cause: revokeRefreshToken matched one token_hash instead of its family.
failures.fix_summary: revokeRefreshToken revokes every live token in the presented token's family.
failures.prevention_notes: Revoke by family_id, never by one token

failures.title: A junk token in the body cleared a valid web session cookie
failures.symptom: POST /api/auth/refresh from the web app with a bad refreshToken in the body answered 401 and cleared the good cookie.
failures.root_cause: The failure path cleared the cookie for any web 401, whichever credential failed.
failures.fix_summary: The cookie is cleared only when the cookie itself failed or there was nothing to refresh with; a body that names a token leaves it alone.
failures.prevention_notes: Clear a credential only when that credential failed

failures.title: Credential writes ran as separate statements
failures.symptom: change-password, mfa/enable, mfa/email/enable and backup-code regeneration issued several writes without a transaction, so a failure part-way left a changed password with live old sessions, MFA on with no backup codes, or a method with none.
failures.root_cause: The statements were independent queries.
failures.fix_summary: Each runs in withTransaction (endOtherSessions takes the transaction); the two enables claim the pending secret in the same update so a repeat enables once.
failures.prevention_notes: Writes that change a credential and end sessions share one transaction; tested by injecting a failure with a trigger

failures.title: A Google-only account could be deleted with only an access token
failures.symptom: DELETE /api/account for an account without a password needed no proof.
failures.root_cause: The route's only confirmation was the password, skipped when none was set.
failures.fix_summary: Accounts without a password go through checkReauth (Google sign-in or a code); the app asks for it.
failures.prevention_notes: Destructive actions confirm with whatever proof the account has

failures.title: Connecting Google left every other session signed in
failures.symptom: A new Google link is a new way to sign in as the account, but the other devices' sessions and access tokens stayed live, so a session that was already stolen outlived the link.
failures.how_detected: owner decision on the F2 batch, checklist rule (2026-11-09)
failures.root_cause: The link route only inserted the oauth_accounts row; unlike change-password and enabling MFA it did not call endOtherSessions.
failures.fix_summary: A new link ends every other refresh family and bumps token_version in the same transaction as the insert, keeps this device's session and returns a fresh accessToken; relinking the same identity ends nothing; the alert email says other devices were signed out.
failures.prevention_notes: Every route that adds a sign-in method calls endOtherSessions in its own transaction

failures.title: Exam start sent twice returned a 500
failures.symptom: Two starts with one clientSessionId: the slower answered 500 (unique violation exam_sessions_user_client_unique)
failures.root_cause: createSession checked for the session, then built questions, then inserted without any lock or on-conflict handling; two requests passed the check together
failures.fix_summary: The insert runs under an advisory lock; the replay is returned (and a mock's counted use is given back); 23505 on that index maps to 409
failures.prevention_notes: A route that replays by client id re-reads the stored row under the same lock that guards the insert, and maps its unique violation to a 4xx

failures.title: Five concurrent exam starts left three sessions in progress
failures.symptom: Five starts with different clientSessionIds each abandoned the open session and inserted; three stayed in_progress
failures.root_cause: The abandon-then-insert transaction was not serialised, so each update ran before the others' inserts were visible
failures.fix_summary: An advisory lock on (user, course, mode) makes starts take turns
failures.prevention_notes: A one-open-row-per-key rule needs a lock or a unique index, not abandon-then-insert

failures.title: One failed regenerate locked an objective for every learner for 6 hours
failures.symptom: After one learner's regenerate was held back twice, every learner's generation for that objective answered 'held back' for six hours
failures.root_cause: recentlyHeldBack filtered item_holdbacks by objective only; the holdback row recorded no scope
failures.fix_summary: item_holdbacks.scope_user_id (069); the cooldown reads own-scope holdbacks only; a shared holdback cools down shared generation only
failures.prevention_notes: A cooldown or limit keyed by an object is checked for who it should block

failures.title: A database blip while queueing the exec check started the 6 hour cooldown
failures.symptom: One failed queueExecCheck call recorded a NOT_SERVED holdback and refused the objective for everyone for six hours
failures.root_cause: A queue failure is ours, but it was recorded as the content being held back
failures.fix_summary: The failure is logged and refused as a retryable 503; nothing is recorded as a holdback
failures.prevention_notes: Only a verdict on the content may start a content cooldown; our own failures are retryable

failures.title: Held-back and unsent-email refusals were hidden behind a 5xx
failures.symptom: Learners never saw the held-back guidance or the unsent-email message; the app showed 'something went wrong on our side'
failures.root_cause: ContentHeldBackError and EmailSendError answered 503, and mobile/src/lib/errorMessage.ts masks every 5xx body
failures.fix_summary: Both answer 409 with held/retryable flags; the regenerate screen shows a held body's message
failures.prevention_notes: A message written for the learner goes out as a 4xx, because the app hides 5xx text

failures.title: A lesson key confirmed wrong came back in mock exams
failures.symptom: A confirmed-wrong lesson check was served again in the next mock, and answers given to it counted
failures.root_cause: copyAnsweredLessonChecks copied lesson checks into exam_items without a pulled filter; confirmItemWrong did not pull or void the copy; the stored re-check skipped source lesson copies
failures.fix_summary: Pulled checks are not copied and their copies are not served; confirming a lesson check pulls its copies and voids their attempts; the re-check covers lesson copies
failures.prevention_notes: Every copy of a keyed item is pulled with the item

failures.title: A cleared item could never be pulled again
failures.symptom: After a person cleared an item, later flags only raised flag_count and it stayed served
failures.root_cause: recordFlag's existing-row branch never reconsidered a cleared status
failures.fix_summary: Learners who flag after the clear count; at the threshold the item is quarantined again
failures.prevention_notes: A person's decision covers what they weighed, not what comes later

failures.title: A failed regenerate wiped the saved lesson position
failures.symptom: A regenerate whose practice half was held back or failed left the learner with the old lesson and no saved place in it
failures.root_cause: startRegeneration cleared lesson_progress as soon as the new intro existed, before anything was stored
failures.fix_summary: Cleared only after the new lesson is stored, and not a position saved since the regenerate started
failures.prevention_notes: Destroy the old state only after the new state is stored

failures.title: A regenerate that stored nothing kept its weekly use
failures.symptom: A learner charged one of the week's regenerations when the practice half was held back after the response
failures.root_cause: withAllowance only gave the use back if the first half failed; the practice half runs after the response
failures.fix_summary: The use is released whenever the generation ends without a stored lesson
failures.prevention_notes: A counted use is released on every path that stores nothing, including work done after the response

failures.title: Retired objectives were still reachable
failures.symptom: Hints, grading, guess-feedback, explain-back, prefetch, lab, refresher, item reports, PBQ and unit routes served or recorded for retired objectives and units, and spent model calls
failures.root_cause: Only the lesson route checked VisibleObjective.retired
failures.fix_summary: taughtObjective and VisibleScenario.retired; 404 on retired
failures.prevention_notes: A route keyed by an objective uses taughtObjective unless it must read history

failures.title: Retired content stayed in review
failures.symptom: Review entries, a resumed session and the enrolment trigger kept retired objectives and units
failures.root_cause: The review readers, the resume path, the trigger and the seed did not apply retired_at
failures.fix_summary: errors?due=1 hides retired rows; resume drops them; the seed resolves a retired unit's entries; the trigger skips them (069)
failures.prevention_notes: Every reader of a table with retired_at applies it, including resumed state and triggers

failures.title: Re-answering a seen Solo item counted as spaced review
failures.symptom: A repeat answer to a seen Solo question moved the objective's due review entries on
failures.root_cause: reviewEvidence excluded hint and retry but not repeat
failures.fix_summary: A lesson repeat is not review evidence (a PBQ re-attempt still is)
failures.prevention_notes: Evidence rules exclude every assisted reason

failures.title: GET /api/attempts?limit=-1 returned 500
failures.symptom: limit=-1 reached Postgres as a negative LIMIT
failures.root_cause: The limit was Number()-ed and clamped to a max only
failures.fix_summary: A limit that is not a whole number of 1 or more is a 400
failures.prevention_notes: Numeric query parameters are validated at the route

failures.title: Objectives retitled in place kept content for the old title
failures.symptom: A stored lesson and items written for an old objective title were served under the new title
failures.root_cause: The seed matches objectives by sort_order and updated the title without touching generated content
failures.fix_summary: A changed title deletes stored lessons (a person-corrected one kept) and pulls the objective's review, quiz and exam items
failures.prevention_notes: A seed that rewrites a key field invalidates what was generated from it

failures.title: The placement check could ask a lesson question that had been pulled
failures.symptom: A lesson check quarantined by a learner report or a re-check was still asked by the placement check, and a correct answer could place the learner past objectives on the strength of a key nobody trusts
failures.how_detected: found live on 2026-11-10 while checking placement
failures.root_cause: candidatesFor in lib/placement.ts reads lesson_content directly and did not apply lessonServableSql, which every reader in lesson-store.ts applies; placement was added before the pull-a-check rule and never revisited
failures.fix_summary: candidatesFor applies lessonServableSql(lc): an objective whose Guided or Solo check is quarantined is not a candidate, and a course left with fewer than MIN_CANDIDATES has no placement check
failures.prevention_notes: The dbtest pulls a Guided check and a Solo check and walks a whole placement. Other lesson_content readers are listed in the B13 release notes for review (exam-items.ts, review-store.ts)

failures.title: A shared holdback was scoped to the learner who started the generation, so its cooldown never applied
failures.symptom: A shared first generation whose teaching text was held back twice stored its holdback with scope_user_id set to the learner who opened the lesson; the shared cooldown (scope_user_id null) never saw it and each reopening paid for the same refusal again
failures.how_detected: B13 merge of F3 onto F1: reading both sides of lesson-generation.ts
failures.root_cause: F3 took a holdback's scope from meta.userId, which was undefined for a shared generation. F1 made meta.userId the learner a shared generation is charged to. Both were right alone; merged, one field meant two things, and the text merged cleanly
failures.fix_summary: GenerateMeta gains sharedScope (set for a shared generation); a holdback's scope comes from it (and from checkedPractice's shared flag), while meta.userId stays the learner charged
failures.prevention_notes: The dbtest starts a shared generation as a learner with held-back teaching text and with a held-back practice half, checks the stored scope and that the next learner makes no model call

failures.title: Account deletion promised nothing stays, but report notes and review-queue copies did
failures.symptom: The delete page and policy said nothing about you stays in the database after deletion. item_flags.user_id is on delete set null, so a deleted learner's note (up to 500 characters) stayed in the row, and content_review_queue.evidence.recentNotes held copies of up to three notes.
failures.root_cause: Only the app_users cascade was relied on. item_flags and the queue keep rows without a user link, and nobody checked what text those rows hold; the queue copies the notes at detection time, so deleting the flag row alone would not have removed them.
failures.fix_summary: DELETE /api/account now collects the learner's notes (item_flags.note and content-report bodies), removes each from every queue row's recentNotes, and clears item_flags.note in the same transaction; the policy, delete page and inventory list what stays.

failures.title: The 2026-11-10 legal bump would have trapped installed builds in a loop
failures.symptom: With the combined bump, an installed build that sends X-Ascendra-App and the 2026-11-09 versions was refused (400) or, if the previous version were accepted for it, never asked again after updating.
failures.how_detected: design review before the bump (FAIL-560 read first)

failures.fix_summary: Builds now send X-Ascendra-Legal with the text they carry. Three generations (no header, X-Ascendra-App only, declared) each accept their own version, recorded as sent; a declaring build must accept the current one. PREVIOUS/UNDECLARED/LEGACY_LEGAL_VERSIONS added.

failures.title: The export included sign-in events of an earlier holder of the same address
failures.symptom: signInEvents matched user_id = $1 OR identifier = the account's email with no date bound, so events logged for the address before this account existed were exported to its owner.
failures.root_cause: Events before sign-in carry only the address, and an address can be freed and registered again within the 90-day retention; the query treated the address as proof of identity.
failures.fix_summary: Address-matched events must have user_id null and created_at >= the account's created_at.

failures.title: Tests from batch 10 and F3 called model routes as learners who had not accepted the study notice
failures.symptom: After F4 was merged, ai-access.dbtest.ts (several tests) and retired-objectives.dbtest.ts failed with 403 study_notice_required where they expected 200 or a 404/429
failures.how_detected: B14 merge: npm run test:db (12 failures)
failures.root_cause: REQ-205 makes the study notice a precondition of every route that sends learner text and updated the fixtures it knew about (30 files). Batch 10 and F3 wrote new fixtures on branches without that guard, so their users never accepted it

failures.title: The study-notice test failed when its random first lab was on a gated course
failures.symptom: legal-privacy-f4.dbtest.ts, 'a learner who has not accepted the notice gets 403 study_notice_required', failed on 'lab submit' with an undefined code in about one run in five, whatever else ran before it
failures.how_detected: B14 merge: one failure in the full test:db run that passed on rerun; reproduced about one run in five
failures.root_cause: The test took the first lab by random UUID. Lab submit runs requireAcknowledgementForObjective before requireStudyNotice; on a nursing, PT or fitness course that guard answers first with the same words and no code, so the assertion on body.code failed depending on the seed's random ids. Not a leak from an earlier test: the files run in separate processes and the database is unchanged by them
failures.fix_summary: The test picks its lab from an ungated course; 12 reruns on a twice-seeded database all pass
failures.prevention_notes: A test that needs 'any row' from seeded data picks it with the property it relies on, not the first by random id

F5 moved the screen to a handoff set by setMfaHandoff, and updated only the call it knew of (the first Google call). The two edits sat in one hunk, so the text conflict was the only warning

failures.title: The web app connected to the database as the table owner
failures.symptom: The app's DATABASE_URL was the owner login (Supabase postgres): it bypassed RLS and could run DDL, rewrite schema_migrations and read rollback backups, so a leaked URL or an injection bug had no ceiling.
failures.root_cause: No runtime role was ever created: 026/052 enabled RLS with no policies and relied on the owner bypass, and nothing in CI connected as anything but the owner.
failures.fix_summary: Migration 071 creates NOLOGIN app_runtime with per-table DML, an app_runtime_all RLS policy per table (no BYPASSRLS), select-only schema_migrations and no rollback copies; app_runtime_sync() repeats it; test:db also runs as app_runtime.

failures.title: Project functions executable by PUBLIC with a mutable search_path
failures.symptom: The Supabase advisor flagged function_search_path_mutable; 19 functions and one procedure had EXECUTE for PUBLIC (and the API roles by default).
failures.root_cause: Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC on every new function and no migration revoked it or set search_path.
failures.fix_summary: 071 revokes EXECUTE from PUBLIC, anon and authenticated and sets search_path = public, pg_temp on each function (the procedure cannot carry a SET clause and COMMIT); app_runtime_sync() does it for later functions.

failures.title: Database TLS certificate never verified
failures.symptom: Every database connection used ssl { rejectUnauthorized: false }: encrypted, but anyone on the path could present their own certificate.
failures.root_cause: The shared helper hard-coded no-verify and two scripts copied it; there was no way to supply a CA.
failures.fix_summary: lib/db-connection.ts: DATABASE_CA_CERT (PEM or path) or PGSSLROOTCERT pins the CA and verifies; unset keeps the old behaviour; an unreadable CA throws instead of falling back; db.ts, apply-migration and seed share it.

failures.title: A plain query had no server-side statement_timeout
failures.symptom: query() had only the driver's client-side timeout, which stops waiting but leaves the statement running on the server, holding a connection and locks.
failures.root_cause: Only withTransaction set statement_timeout (SET LOCAL); query() takes a fresh client per call and a session SET does not survive a transaction pooler.
failures.fix_summary: app_runtime carries statement_timeout 25s at the role level (works through any pooler); other roles get it in the startup packet except on pooler hosts/ports unless DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS is set.

failures.title: Production migration job could hang or hide a failed status
failures.symptom: 'Status before' ended in || true so a wrong password looked like 'nothing to report'; the job had GitHub's 6-hour default timeout and no lock_timeout beyond each file's own.
failures.root_cause: The workflow tolerated every non-zero exit instead of the one meaning 'objects missing'; the runner relied on each migration author remembering SET LOCAL lock_timeout.
failures.fix_summary: timeout-minutes 30; status-before tolerates only exit 2; apply-migration sets a session lock_timeout (5s, MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT) before each transaction.

failures.title: Error reports lost when the serverless function froze
failures.symptom: reportError fired a fetch and returned; on Vercel the invocation is frozen after the response, so many reports never left.
failures.root_cause: Fire-and-forget (void fetch) assumes the process keeps running.
failures.fix_summary: reportError hands the send to Next's after() and falls back to sending immediately outside a request; onRequestError awaits sendErrorReport (the documented contract for that hook).

failures.title: Server errors logged the whole error object, including Postgres detail
failures.symptom: console.error(label, err) printed node-postgres' detail/where/parameters; a unique violation's detail reads Key (email)=(learner@example.com) already exists.
failures.root_cause: The 500 path logged the object for debugging convenience; Postgres puts row values in detail.
failures.fix_summary: lib/error-summary.ts: only name, code and a 200-character message with e-mail addresses masked go to the log; the tracker event masks e-mails in message and stack.

failures.title: No Content-Security-Policy and no HSTS
failures.symptom: Responses carried no CSP and no Strict-Transport-Security.
failures.root_cause: next.config.js set four baseline headers only; the Expo web export and the Next-rendered pages had no policy.
failures.fix_summary: security-headers.js: enforced CSP for the web app (own-origin script, no eval), a separate one for the Next-rendered pages (inline script allowed), default-src none for the API, HSTS max-age one year; CSP_REPORT_ONLY switch; checked in a browser against a local build.

failures.title: Static route containment check was a prefix test and everything was immutable
failures.symptom: startsWith(PUBLIC_DIR) is true for /../public-secrets/x; every file under public/ was cached immutable for a year.
failures.root_cause: A string prefix is not path containment; one Cache-Control for all files.
failures.fix_summary: resolveInside compares with a path separator; immutable only for Expo's content-hashed filenames, one hour revalidate for the rest.

failures.title: Public health check exposed internals and missed the ledger and mail sender
failures.symptom: /api/health named missing environment variables and migration filenames to anyone; it did not compare schema_migrations with the code; an unset EMAIL_FROM was a warning on a 200.
failures.root_cause: One response for every caller; probes check objects, never the ledger; REQ-191 chose a warning.
failures.fix_summary: Public answer is status, schema and short commit; details need Authorization: Bearer CRON_SECRET; ledger vs shipped migration files (traced into the function) gives ledger_incomplete 503; production with unset/resend.dev EMAIL_FROM is misconfigured 503.

failures.title: Keepalive printed the health response body into a public log
failures.symptom: The daily keepalive run cat'ed the response body.
failures.root_cause: Written when the body was harmless.
failures.fix_summary: The body goes to /dev/null; only the status code is printed.

failures.title: CI supply-chain gaps
failures.symptom: Workflows without a top-level permissions block, EXPO_TOKEN given to every step of the OTA job, mobile npm audit report-only, no dependabot, floating base images in the sandbox, mixed Node 22/24.
failures.root_cause: Defaults were left in place as workflows were added one at a time.
failures.fix_summary: permissions contents:read on ci, migrate and keepalive; EXPO_TOKEN per step; Node 24 everywhere; dependabot; sandbox base images by digest; blocking mobile audit gate with lockfile-only npm audit fix (19 to 7 findings). Every third-party action is pinned to a commit SHA with a vX.Y.Z comment (newest patch tag of the major version in use): .github/scripts/pin-actions.mjs resolves tags with git ls-remote (peeled ^{} entry for annotated tags); PENDING_PINS is empty and the test rejects any new unpinned action.

failures.fix_summary: An alert job (needs: exec, if: failure(), issues: write only) opens one deduplicated issue.

failures.root_cause: Notes were written as prose.
failures.fix_summary: scripts/rollback-064.sql and rollback-071.sql are real SQL, run in a rolled-back transaction by a DB test; docs/ops/migration-rollbacks.md covers 065 and 067.

failures.title: The pre-generation workflow was written without F6's pinning and Node rules
failures.symptom: pregenerate.yml (REQ-208) used actions/checkout, setup-node and upload-artifact on floating v4 tags and Node 22, failing the REQ-207 hardening test on the merged tree. It runs with the production database URL and an Anthropic key, so an unpinned action there is the worst place for one
failures.root_cause: REQ-208 and REQ-207 were built in parallel; the pin-everything rule and the one-Node-major rule did not exist when the workflow was written, and a new workflow file has no text conflict with a rule that lives in a test
failures.fix_summary: The three actions are pinned to the commits and version comments the other workflows use; Node is 24 like every other workflow
failures.prevention_notes: workflow-hardening.test.ts reads every file in .github/workflows, so a workflow added later is held to the same pins and Node major

failures.title: A restored backup failed the schema check once migration 071 existed, so the drill and the real restore procedure were broken
failures.symptom: backup-drill-test.sh: 'Schema is MISSING objects the code needs: app_runtime role and app_runtime_sync(); no PUBLIC execute ...(071)'; RESTORE DRILL FAILED. The same on F6's own branch. A real restore into a new Supabase project would have shown the same
failures.how_detected: B16 merge: backend/scripts/ci/backup-drill-test.sh; reproduced on fix/f6-ops-hardening by itself
failures.root_cause: The 071 probe checks things a database dump never holds: the role (a cluster object), PUBLIC's revoked EXECUTE (an ACL; after pg_restore --no-privileges a function's proacl is null and the default grants PUBLIC execute) and the role's grants. F6 added the probe and the privilege layer without running the drill's restore path, which loads only the public schema without privileges. The probe was right, the restore procedure was missing a step
failures.fix_summary: restore-drill.sh re-applies 071 (safe to run twice) after pg_restore and before the status check; the runbook's real-restore step and restore-drill.md say to do the same. The probe is not loosened, and the backup itself is unchanged
failures.prevention_notes: The drill is the test: it fails if a migration adds something a dump does not carry and no recovery step re-creates it. Checked on a brand-new cluster with no app_runtime role as well as on the dev cluster

failures.title: Logging a pace command failed with a 500: sim_run_commands type check predates the new commands
failures.symptom: The first dbtest that synced a pace command to a clinical sim got HTTP 500 from the step route; begin, teach and chapter would have failed the same way. Runs that never log one were unaffected.
failures.how_detected: backend/lib/sims.dbtest.ts, new REQ-209 tests against a migrated database
failures.root_cause: Migration 062 restricts sim_run_commands.type to act, choose, skip, pause, resume, reason and end with an inline check. REQ-209 added four command types in the engine, parser and app but the unit tests never touch Postgres, so nothing noticed the check.
failures.fix_summary: Migration 073 widens the check (NOT VALID, drop the old, validate; idempotent); lib/schema-status.ts probes for it; docs/sims.md 5.4f says to apply it before the backend.
regression_tests: and exactly the new command types are allowed (REQ-209)
backend/lib/sims.dbtest.ts::a legitimate 3x run is accepted; the same ticks with no pace logged
failures.prevention_notes: A new command type needs a dbtest that syncs it through the step route, and a migration if the table constrains the value.

failures.title: Skip to the next change would be on offer at every moment because the q15 check is always pending
failures.symptom: In the first draft the calm-skip offer appeared from tick 0 and could skip over the recognition window, the thing the case is meant to test.
failures.how_detected: Own review of the calm-skip rule against the golden paths while writing pacing.test.ts
failures.root_cause: The tamponade q15 drainage check is a recurring timer with a wait, so some wait is always pending (the old authoring note in docs/sims.md 3 said so and the q15 note called skip always available). An offer built on 'a wait is pending' inherited that.
failures.fix_summary: A wait.routine flag (engine minor 1) marks recurring checks; calmSkip ignores routine waits and requires nothing due inside 60 sim seconds; the linter's wait-always-pending warning ignores routine waits; the q15 authoring note is rewritten.
regression_tests: backend/lib/sim/pacing.test.ts::nothing to offer at the start: the only wait is the routine q15 check
mobile/src/sim/pacing.test.ts::nothing to offer at the start: only the routine q15 check is pending
failures.prevention_notes: An offer or prompt keyed to 'a wait is pending' must say what counts as a change; recurring checks are marked routine.

failures.title: Biometric unlock was switched off when leaving the launch lock to sign in or create an account
failures.symptom: Reported by Nick on the Android preview build (2026-11-11 release): biometrics are turned off after navigating to Create account. With biometric unlock on the app opens on the lock screen; its only way to the login and Create account screens is 'Use password instead', and afterwards Settings showed biometric unlock off
failures.how_detected: user report (Nick), confirmed by code reading
failures.root_cause: useFallbackSignIn ('Use password instead') called clearBiometricEnrollment, which deleted BIOMETRIC_ENABLED_KEY as well as the sealed session; unlockWithBiometric did the same on a missing or rejected sealed token. REQ-192 had made a plain logout keep the preference but left these paths on the old drop-everything behaviour. The preference is one per device, not per account, so every later sign-in on the device started with it off
failures.fix_summary: clearBiometricEnrollment became endSealedSession(reason): it always deletes the sealed token and writes the session flag 0; only logoutAll also deletes the preference (keepsBiometricPreference in src/lib/sessionStore.ts). The next password sign-in seals the new session again
failures.prevention_notes: loginWorkflow.test.ts fails if anything but disableBiometric and the logoutAll branch deletes the preference key or if an auth screen touches biometric state

failures.title: The login screen's biometric button turned biometrics off after a plain logout
failures.symptom: Found while tracing FAIL-1002 (code reading): after a plain logout the login screen still shows 'Use <fingerprint>'; tapping it fails with 'Couldn't unlock' and switches biometric unlock off
failures.how_detected: code review while debugging the reported biometric bug
failures.root_cause: REQ-192 made logout delete the sealed refresh token and write the session flag 0 but the login button was still gated only on biometricAvailable && biometricEnabled. unlockWithBiometric then read an empty key and called clearBiometricEnrollment
failures.fix_summary: AuthContext tracks the sealed-session flag in state and exposes biometricSignInReady (showBiometricSignIn: hardware and preference and a sealed session); login.tsx shows the button only then. A missing token no longer drops the preference (FAIL-1002)
failures.prevention_notes: loginWorkflow.test.ts pins the gate and that every write of the session flag updates the state the button reads

failures.title: The two-factor code field was excluded from Android autofill
failures.symptom: Found while checking the reported login autofill bug: the MFA challenge's code field had textContentType oneTimeCode only, so Android offered no code suggestion there
failures.how_detected: code reading of node_modules/react-native ReactTextInputManager.kt while debugging the autofill report
failures.root_cause: textContentType is iOS-only. react-native's Android TextInput sets IMPORTANT_FOR_AUTOFILL_NO when autoComplete is absent (ReactTextInputManager.setTextContentType), so the field was opted out of autofill on Android
failures.fix_summary: autoComplete one-time-code (sms-otp on Android) for codes; off for backup codes
failures.prevention_notes: loginWorkflow.test.ts pins the hint and the autofill props of login and register and that TextField forwards them unchanged

failures.title: Every live PBQ scenario was held back for wording caveats, so generation never succeeded
failures.symptom: Nick, 2026-11-10: 'Generating pbqs is throwing an error and not working'. Production: both pbq_generate calls ever made were held back as uncertain (claims such as 'control type labels may differ from the textbook taxonomy')
failures.how_detected: Owner report; Vercel runtime logs ([item-quality] held back pbq (uncertain)) and ai_calls
failures.root_cause: The shared accuracy rule asks the writer to list every claim it is unsure of; for an invented scenario the fast model listed caveats about terminology and paraphrase, and the route held back on any listed claim with no second attempt
failures.fix_summary: The PBQ prompt says invented settings and wording caveats are not claims and to use the exam's standard terms; a held-back scenario is written once more before the learner is asked to retry. Real uncertain facts are still held back and logged
failures.prevention_notes: pbq-holdback.dbtest.ts covers held-back-then-served, two held back, and the prompt wording

failures.title: A held-back PBQ scenario showed 'something went wrong on our side' instead of its message
failures.symptom: The app showed a generic error when a scenario was held back
failures.how_detected: Reading the route while debugging FAIL-1000
failures.root_cause: UserFacingError defaults to 503, and the app replaces any 5xx message with the generic one (the same issue FAIL-884 fixed for lessons)
failures.fix_summary: The held-back answer is a 409 carrying 'We couldn't write a scenario we're confident in just now. Please try again.'
failures.prevention_notes: pbq-holdback.dbtest.ts asserts the 409 and the message

failures.title: PBQ scenarios were still held back after FAIL-1000: the writer listed 'this scenario is invented' as an uncertain claim
failures.symptom: Nick, 2026-11-10 20:09, after the FAIL-1000 fix deployed: 'Couldn't write a scenario they are confident in for pbq.' Production item_holdbacks: both attempts held back with disclaimer-only claims at medium confidence
failures.how_detected: Owner report; item_holdbacks rows for SECPLUS
failures.root_cause: The fast model treats uncertainClaims as a place for disclaimers; prompt wording did not stop it, and any listed claim held a PBQ back. A PBQ has no answer key (graded holistically), so the claim list is a poor gate for it
failures.fix_summary: For PBQs only the writer's low confidence holds a scenario back (with one retry, then a 409); listed claims at medium/high confidence are logged and the scenario is served
