failures.title: Review sessions could pick a pulled (quarantined or confirmed wrong) question
failures.symptom: Review sessions could pick a pulled (quarantined or confirmed wrong) question (Audit 2026-11-11 H1)
failures.how_detected: Audit of 2026-11-11 (reproduced in a DB test first)
failures.root_cause: prepareContext (the session builder's one-query read of unseen cached questions) had no pulled-item filter; unseenItems(), which had it, was no longer called
failures.fix_summary: review-store.ts prepareContext adds servableSql('review', ri.id); unseenItems removed
failures.prevention_notes: A query that replaces another carries over every filter of the one it replaces; item-quality.dbtest.ts now checks the filter on the live read path

failures.title: A review was 'due' minutes after the last one and a correct answer then climbed a rung
failures.symptom: A review was 'due' minutes after the last one and a correct answer then climbed a rung (Audit H8)
failures.how_detected: Audit of 2026-11-11 (reproduced in a DB test first)
failures.root_cause: Due dates are UTC calendar days: an answer at 23:50 was due at 00:00. Nothing required elapsed time, so a correct answer counted as a spaced review
failures.fix_summary: A review is due only when its date has come and 24 h (MIN_REVIEW_GAP_HOURS; first set at 18, changed to a full day by Nick, 2026-11-10) have passed since the last review or enrolment: scheduler, advanceDueSchedule, dueObjectives, nextDueOn. Elapsed time, not the learner's local date, because the app sends that date and the server only checks it to within a day
failures.prevention_notes: A spacing rule is stated in elapsed time; a test enrols at 23:50

failures.title: One correct unassisted answer in the first sitting made an objective Independent
failures.symptom: One correct unassisted answer in the first sitting made an objective Independent (Owner decision)
failures.how_detected: Audit of 2026-11-11 (reproduced in a DB test first)
failures.root_cause: mastery_detail opened Independent on a single format win with accuracy over the threshold; no later evidence was required (Nick, 2026-11-10: a follow-up session is needed)
failures.fix_summary: Migration 074 restates mastery_detail: Independent and Transfer-ready need a second unassisted correct format win spacing_gap_hours (24 h) after the first; 074b backs up and recomputes every learner
failures.prevention_notes: A change to the mastery rule is a migration with a recompute and a test that a stored level follows

failures.title: Exam submit read a snapshot while saves were still accepted, and recorded attempts before flipping the session out of in_progress
failures.symptom: Exam submit read a snapshot while saves were still accepted, and recorded attempts before flipping the session out of in_progress (Audit M1, M5)
failures.how_detected: Audit of 2026-11-11 (reproduced in a DB test first)
failures.root_cause: submitSession read the items, recorded each attempt in its own transaction, and only then locked the session. A save in that window was acknowledged and never graded; an abandoned session's answers were counted
failures.fix_summary: submitIn: one transaction that locks the session row, flips it to submitted, then reads, grades and records; saveItem takes the row FOR SHARE so a save is refused after the claim
failures.prevention_notes: State changes that decide what a later read may see are claimed under a row lock before the read

failures.title: An exam attempt was recorded for an item already confirmed wrong
failures.symptom: An exam attempt was recorded for an item already confirmed wrong (Audit M2)
failures.how_detected: Audit of 2026-11-11 (reproduced in a DB test first)
failures.root_cause: submit recorded every answered item without looking at item_status
failures.fix_summary: submit skips items with a confirmed_wrong status; the exam item rows are locked FOR SHARE and confirmWrongIn takes the conflicting lock, so a confirm in flight is waited for
failures.prevention_notes: A recorder reads the pulled state under the same lock the puller takes

failures.title: An exam submit could get stuck after a partial failure, and ran without a duration limit

failures.title: Every silent token refresh asked for a fingerprint, and a cancelled prompt signed the learner out
failures.symptom: With biometric unlock on, each silent refresh wrote the sealed key, which prompts on Android; cancelling it signed out after the server had already rotated the token
failures.root_cause: AuthContext.refresh re-sealed the rotated token with requireAuthentication on every refresh and called clearAuth on any failure in that block
failures.fix_summary: Silent refresh keeps the token in memory and marks the sealed copy stale; it is sealed at sign-in, unlock and when the app goes to the background; a failed seal falls back to the plain key and never signs out
failures.prevention_notes: The listed regression test pins the rule; the mobile gate (npx tsc --noEmit and npm test) runs it on every change.

failures.title: Any failed refresh (offline, timeout, 5xx) wiped the session

failures.fix_summary: Only a 401 from refresh signs out; otherwise the token is kept, the failure is thrown to the screen, and a cold start shows Try again / Sign out
failures.prevention_notes: The listed regression test pins the rule; the mobile gate (npx tsc --noEmit and npm test) runs it on every change.

failures.title: A restore into a cluster without app_runtime and content_recheck failed, and the CI drill could not see it
failures.symptom: pg_restore --schema=public into a fresh cluster ends with about 120 'role "app_runtime" does not exist' / 'role "content_recheck" does not exist' errors on every CREATE POLICY; a real restore would not complete
failures.root_cause: Roles belong to the cluster and a dump holds none, but the dump's RLS policies are TO app_runtime / TO content_recheck (migrations 064, 071). The drill and runbook created neither role before pg_restore; the CI drill restored into the same cluster the source was migrated on, where both roles already existed. content_recheck's grants were also never re-applied (--no-privileges)
failures.fix_summary: scripts/restore/01 creates both roles NOLOGIN before pg_restore; after 071 the drill applies 02 (064's grant block); runbook and drill docs give the same order; CI restores on a second postgres service and refuses a restore cluster that is the same server or already has the roles
failures.prevention_notes: The CI test shows a plain restore failing on the fresh cluster (canary), then the drill passing, and compares the restored roles' privileges with the source's (1625 facts)

failures.prevention_notes: Refusals the learner can act on carry a stable code in the body; the gate's error type owns that code, so a new gate cannot lose it at the route

failures.title: Security+ V7 was missing whole SY0-701 sub-objectives (3.3, 4.2, 4.7, 5.5) and parts of 1.2, 2.4, 4.1
failures.symptom: Readiness could say 'ready' without data protection, asset management, automation or audits being taught
failures.root_cause: The course was written at headline level and never checked against CompTIA's objective list
failures.fix_summary: One appended objective per official sub-objective; two IAM lines outside 4.6 retired in place
failures.prevention_notes: The test lists every SY0-701 (v5.0) sub-objective's topics

failures.title: Security+ V7 practice exams were single-answer only
failures.symptom: No 'choose two' or ordering/matching items for SY0-701
failures.root_cause: The seed's question-format text named only 'multiple choice and performance-based'
failures.fix_summary: Format text now states single/multiple response, drag-and-drop and performance-based, per CompTIA's page

failures.title: Security+ V7 incident-response lab used NIST 800-61r3 CSF IDs instead of the exam's seven steps
failures.symptom: The lab taught a framework newer than the one SY0-701 4.8 tests
failures.root_cause: Lab written from NIST r3
failures.fix_summary: Lab leads with preparation, detection, analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned; NIST as a mapping

failures.title: PT courses taught superseded APTA ethics documents
failures.symptom: The DPT course taught the 2020 Code's eight principles; NPTE-PTA cited the PTA Standards of Ethical Conduct
failures.root_cause: APTA replaced both with one Code effective 2026-01-01
failures.fix_summary: Retired in place; replacements name the 2026 Code's principles and nine Ethical Commitments

failures.title: PT courses taught the pre-2021 Medicare maintenance rule for PTAs
failures.symptom: Said a PTA may not deliver skilled maintenance programs
failures.root_cause: CMS MM12071 (effective 2021-01-01) lets the PT delegate furnishing maintenance therapy; the BPM text quoted predates it
failures.fix_summary: Retired and replaced in DPT and NPTE-PTA

failures.title: Heart-failure weight flag printed 1.8 kg as 3 lb
failures.symptom: Three PT labs said '1.8 kg (3 lb)'
failures.root_cause: Unit conversion error (1.8 kg = 3.97 lb)
failures.fix_summary: Now 4 lb; a test checks every kg/lb pair in the seed
failures.prevention_notes: Generic kg/lb conversion check

failures.title: CNA, LPN/VN, ADN and BSN study-emphasis weights were shown as exam blueprints
failures.symptom: '% of exam' labels, blueprint-weighted readiness, the study plan and the coach prompt used our own weights as an exam's
failures.root_cause: Nothing distinguished a vendor blueprint from our emphasis
failures.fix_summary: credential.domainWeights 'study_emphasis'; exam_domains unweighted; the server (STUDY_EMPHASIS_TRACK_CODES, read from subject_tracks so every database role can use it) drops the weights from every blueprint use
failures.prevention_notes: Server-side, so every installed app build is covered

failures.title: Sarcopenia taught as protein change only
failures.symptom: DPT line said ageing changes existing fibres' protein, not cell number
failures.root_cause: OpenStax A&P 2e 10.6: ageing fibres die
failures.fix_summary: Retired and replaced

failures.title: Learner-facing text mixed British and US spelling
failures.symptom: Seed, app and server text used British spellings
failures.how_detected: Owner request (Nick, 2026-11-10, via the lead session)
failures.root_cause: No spelling standard or check
failures.fix_summary: 2,718 words converted in string content; seed keeps lessons on spelling-only retitles; legal text and published sims excluded with reasons; lesson-fix lookups accept the pre-sweep British title
failures.prevention_notes: lib/us-spelling.test.ts fails on listed British words in learner-facing strings

failures.title: CCRN taught the retired 'healthcare-associated pneumonia' category
failures.symptom: Pneumonia classification included HCAP
failures.root_cause: 2016 IDSA/ATS HAP/VAP guideline removed it
failures.fix_summary: Retired and replaced with HAP/VAP

failures.title: PT and EMS courses were told to reason by the nursing process
failures.symptom: Prompt framing keyed on the healthcare category
failures.root_cause: Framing ignored the subcategory
failures.fix_summary: Framing follows the subcategory

failures.title: Lesson writer and fact-checker never saw the units' dated key values
failures.symptom: A CNA lesson could contradict the lab's 2025 AHA choking sequence
failures.root_cause: Unit sources carried no values and multi-unit batches carried no unit references
failures.fix_summary: UnitSource.keyValues reach the current-facts block, review writer and checker items; launch-course values added where the seed records them

failures.title: Tamponade focused start gave away its key cue and asked the scored question ~60 s in
failures.symptom: Summary named the drainage stop; question at tick 840 after a 780 start
failures.root_cause: Authored summary and start tick
failures.fix_summary: Version 2: no cue in the summary; start at 720 so >= 120 sim s before the question
failures.prevention_notes: Test holds the 120 s floor

failures.title: Tamponade brief said the clock runs in real time while the default is 3x
failures.symptom: Start screen 'How it works' contradicted the pace
failures.root_cause: Brief predates REQ-209 pacing
failures.fix_summary: Version 2 brief states 3x by default and 1x on request

failures.title: Tamponade CVP model disagreed with its own teaching prompt
failures.symptom: Model +0.6 mmHg per 500 mL vs taught ~3 mmHg
failures.root_cause: Prototype value kept
failures.fix_summary: Version 2: cvpPer500 = 3; goldens' CVP snapshots updated, outcomes unchanged

failures.title: Two simultaneous 'turn off' requests left two-factor 'on' with no method and skipped the last-method code
failures.symptom: An account could end with mfa_enabled = true, no authenticator and no email codes: sign-in asked for a code step it could never pass, and neither request needed the emailed confirmation code.
failures.root_cause: Each disable route read the OTHER method's state, decided from it whether this was the last method, and wrote mfa_enabled = <other still on> as three separate steps. Two requests (one per method) each saw the other still on, so both wrote true.
failures.fix_summary: The decision and the write are one transaction with the user row locked (lib/auth/mfaMethodOff.ts turnOffMfaMethod); a method that became the last since the caller looked answers 409 and writes nothing; sign-in treats 'on with no method' as off (mfaStepRequired); migration 075 repairs rows already in that state.
failures.prevention_notes: A decision that depends on another row's state is made and written under one lock (checklist: Account security).

failures.title: A Google-only account could not regenerate its backup codes
failures.symptom: The backup-codes route demanded a password; an account without one always got 'Incorrect password'.
failures.root_cause: The route compared a password only and was never moved to the shared confirm-it's-you check (lib/auth/reauth.ts) the other routes use.
failures.fix_summary: The route uses checkReauth (password, authenticator or backup code, or a fresh Google sign-in) with the shared budget; the mobile screen offers the matching proof.
failures.prevention_notes: Every route that asks the caller to confirm it's them goes through checkReauth.

failures.title: A rejected Google ID token was a 500 reported to the error tracker, and the sign-in route had no per-IP limit
failures.symptom: Any stale, forged or wrong-app token produced a server error and an error-tracker event; one address could hammer the route.
failures.root_cause: verifyGoogleIdToken let the library's rejection escape as a plain Error, which serverError treats as ours; the route had no limit like register's.
failures.fix_summary: verifyGoogleIdToken throws GoogleTokenError for a rejected token (a transport or configuration fault still throws its own error); the sign-in and link routes answer 401 without reporting; sign-in has a per-IP limit (30 per 15 minutes, keyed by a hash of the address).
failures.prevention_notes: A caller's bad input is a 4xx and not reported; per-IP counters store a hash, not the address.

failures.title: Google sign-in that attached to an existing password account told its owner nothing
failures.symptom: Anyone who controlled a Google account with the same verified address got a new way into a password account with no notice to the account's inbox (the explicit link route does mail).
failures.root_cause: The sign-in route's attach path inserted the oauth_accounts row and logged in; only the link route sent the alert.
failures.fix_summary: A first attach to an existing, verified account mails the account address a 'Google sign-in connected' alert (Nick's decision); later sign-ins and new accounts mail nothing.
failures.prevention_notes: Every path that adds a sign-in method mails the account address (checklist: Account security).

failures.title: Login had no per-IP ceiling
failures.symptom: The five-try limit is per (address, IP) pair, so one IP trying a different address each time was never stopped by it.
failures.root_cause: The only limits were per pair and per account.
failures.fix_summary: A per-IP ceiling (60 wrong password checks per 15 minutes) comes before the pair check; an attempt is counted while checked and given back when the password is right; over the ceiling answers exactly like a wrong password.
failures.prevention_notes: A limit keyed by one dimension has a ceiling on the other.

failures.title: Error reports sent the request path with its query string, which carries one-time tokens
failures.symptom: Verification, reset and email-change tokens (in ?token=) reached the error tracker.
failures.root_cause: instrumentation.ts passed request.path, which Next documents as including the query, as the route.
failures.fix_summary: routeOnly strips the query and fragment in instrumentation.ts and again in errorEvent.
failures.prevention_notes: Nothing from a URL beyond its path goes to a third party.

failures.title: The verify-email result page's redirect URL carried the password-reset token
failures.symptom: The one-hour reset token sat in /verify-email?result=set_password&reset=<token>: in request logs, error reports and browser history.
failures.root_cause: The server action handed the token to the next page through the query string.
failures.fix_summary: The action stores it in a short-lived httpOnly cookie scoped to /verify-email (lib/reset-handoff.ts); the page reads the cookie; a browser that refuses it is pointed to 'Forgot password'.
failures.prevention_notes: Nothing sensitive goes in a redirect URL (checklist: Web screens).

failures.title: The next Terms bump would have stranded builds that declared the version before it
failures.symptom: PREVIOUS_LEGAL_VERSIONS held one generation; at the next bump the old previous would move out and builds still declaring it could no longer accept their own text.
failures.root_cause: The acceptable generations were a fixed current/previous/undeclared/legacy set, not a list.
failures.fix_summary: Previous generations are a list (EARLIER_LEGAL_VERSIONS beside PREVIOUS_LEGAL_VERSIONS); a build declaring any of them accepts exactly that one; the rule is a pure function tested against a simulated bump.
failures.prevention_notes: The bump procedure in the checklist pushes the old previous onto EARLIER_LEGAL_VERSIONS.

failures.title: Terms and Privacy agreement was enforced only by the app
failures.symptom: A request made without the app, or by a build that skipped the prompt, got every signed-in route whether or not the account had agreed.
failures.root_cause: The launch gate was client-side; requireUser checked identity only.
failures.fix_summary: requireUser reads the account's acceptances in its existing query and answers 403 { code: 'terms_required' } with a plain message unless the account accepted what its client must accept (legalContext rules unchanged); open routes: accept, onboarding, auth/me read, account export and delete, logout-all, support. dbtests are preloaded with enforcement off (lib/test-setup.ts) and the enforcement suites turn it on.
failures.prevention_notes: A new signed-in route is enforced by default; the sweep test lists the open routes.

failures.title: Revoking a listed session revoked one token row, not its family; the list showed duplicate sessions
failures.symptom: A session holding a second live token (a replayed rotation) stayed signed in after 'sign out this device', and appeared twice; the screen said 'immediately' though the access token lives 15 more minutes.
failures.root_cause: The routes listed and revoked refresh_tokens rows, not families.
failures.fix_summary: The list is one entry per family; DELETE revokes the family (revokeRefreshFamily); the screen's wording says up to 15 more minutes.
failures.prevention_notes: Revoke by family_id, never one token (checklist: Account security).

failures.title: No maximum password length on change and reset
failures.symptom: A multi-megabyte new password was hashed.
failures.root_cause: Register capped passwords at 1024 characters; change-password and reset-password did not.
failures.fix_summary: One MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH in lib/auth/passwords.ts used by all three.
failures.prevention_notes: One constant for a limit several routes share.

failures.title: A password change left pending reset links and sign-in challenges valid
failures.symptom: A reset link mailed earlier, or a sign-in code step earned with the old password, still worked after the change.
failures.root_cause: change-password ended sessions but, unlike reset-password, did not spend the other outstanding credentials.
failures.fix_summary: The same transaction marks the account's reset tokens and login challenges consumed.
failures.prevention_notes: A route that changes a credential spends every other outstanding credential in the same transaction.

failures.title: An authenticator code could be used twice inside its window
failures.symptom: Someone who saw a code could reuse it for up to 90 seconds, at sign-in or as a proof.
failures.root_cause: Nothing remembered which 30-second step was last accepted.
failures.fix_summary: app_users.totp_last_step (migration 075); spendTotpCode accepts only a later step with one guarded UPDATE, at sign-in and in reauth; enabling records its own code's step.
failures.prevention_notes: A single-use code is spent atomically.

failures.title: Emailed sign-in codes skipped the per-address mail limit
failures.symptom: Each new sign-in attempt (a new challenge) could email the address again without the hourly limit every other mail has.
failures.root_cause: send-email-code only had the per-challenge cap.
failures.fix_summary: The route spends mayEmail(address) and answers a plain 429 over the limit.
failures.prevention_notes: Anything that mails an address goes through mayEmail (checklist: Auth and abuse).

failures.title: A support content report looked up an objective without visibility
failures.symptom: Any objective id, including in another learner's private course, was confirmed to exist and mailed to support.
failures.root_cause: The route queried objectives by id alone.
failures.fix_summary: It uses visibleObjective(id, userId).
failures.prevention_notes: Client-supplied ids go through lib/visibility.ts (checklist: Auth and abuse).

failures.title: The inbound email webhook had no replay protection
failures.symptom: A replayed or retried delivery forwarded the same message again.
failures.root_cause: Nothing recorded the Svix delivery id.
failures.fix_summary: inbound_email_events (migration 075): claim by svix-id, release on failure so retries work, complete on success, stale claims taken over after 5 minutes, purged after 7 days.
failures.prevention_notes: A webhook records its delivery id.

failures.title: Catalog review findings were stored unchecked
failures.symptom: Wrong types, non-http URLs, oversized text and a future checkedAt were stored; a future date pushed a track's next review out of sight; the two writes were separate statements.
failures.root_cause: The route inserted the body's fields as sent.
failures.fix_summary: The fields are validated, checkedAt is capped at now, and the finding and the freshness update share one transaction.
failures.prevention_notes: A machine caller's input is validated like a learner's.

failures.title: The paid-access rule was duplicated with a hard-coded 24 hour grace
failures.symptom: Changing the grace in lib/entitlements.ts would have left 'paying' in paid AI mode disagreeing.
failures.root_cause: lib/ai-access.ts carried its own copy of the SQL with 24 typed in.
failures.fix_summary: GIVES_ACCESS and GRACE_HOURS are exported from lib/entitlements.ts and reused; a paid-mode test covers active, canceled, within and past the grace, and expired.
failures.prevention_notes: A shared rule is defined once.

failures.title: A learner-facing error went out as a 5xx, so the app hid its words
failures.symptom: UserFacingError defaulted to 503 and several throw sites used 502/503; the app shows 'something went wrong on our side' for any 5xx. Regeneration also said 'check your connection' for a server message
failures.root_cause: A status default of 503 and per-site 5xx codes; the app dropped the server's text for every 5xx
failures.fix_summary: UserFacingError is always 4xx (default 409, a 5xx request is clamped); every throw site fixed; AI-paused message is a 429; the app keeps the server's error for 502/503 and regenerate shows server words
failures.prevention_notes: generation-gate.test.ts scans every source file for a UserFacingError with a 5xx status

failures.title: Comparison cards finished 'ready' with no cards when every card was held back
failures.symptom: Production: 4 of 4 comparison cards held for disclaimers; the course was marked ready and never retried
failures.root_cause: Any listed claim held a card, and a generation that saved nothing still finished as ready
failures.fix_summary: Low confidence or a disagreeing check holds a card; one steered retry; nothing saved with anything held or unchecked finishes 'failed' (retried on a later visit)
failures.prevention_notes: understanding.dbtest.ts: listed disclaimers save the card; low twice ends failed

failures.title: The distractor lint rejected correct questions
failures.symptom: Questions with 'Read-only access', 'two-factor' or 'three-way handshake' failed the lint and the generation failed
failures.root_cause: The word splitter broke hyphenated compounds apart ('only'), the count request matched 'two-factor', and cue words were checked against the right answer
failures.fix_summary: Hyphenated compounds are one word; a number starting a compound is not a count request; cue words only in distractors; a second lint-only failure is logged and served
failures.prevention_notes: generation-gate.test.ts lint cases

failures.title: A lesson intro was regenerated after its practice half failed
failures.symptom: The learner read an intro, the practice half failed, and the next request wrote a different intro before trying practice again
failures.root_cause: The accepted intro was not kept anywhere once generation failed
failures.fix_summary: The accepted intro is kept (per process, 30 minutes) and reused; only practice is retried; the cooldown after a content-check failure is 10 minutes, and a lesson held back says why
failures.prevention_notes: lesson-holdback.dbtest.ts: retry reuses the intro; one intro call in total

failures.title: Listed disclaimers held back lessons, quiz, review, unit check and exam items; a failed fact-check call was treated as a holdback
failures.symptom: Production item_holdbacks: lesson_intro 3 of 9 held for disclaimers; a provider error on the fact-check logged a holdback and could start a cooldown
failures.root_cause: uncertaintyOf blocked on any listed claim and the gate failed closed by recording a holdback on the content
failures.fix_summary: Block only on the writer's low confidence or a fact-check that disagrees with the key; log listed disclaimers; one retry steered with the claims; a held item is a 409 naming the reason; a failed fact-check call is a retryable 409 with no holdback
failures.prevention_notes: generation-gate.ts is the one gate; the pre-completion checklist names it

failures.title: A PBQ waiter regenerated after the holder's scenario was held back
failures.symptom: A second request waiting on the lease took it and wrote again after the first was refused
failures.root_cause: The waiter treated 'nothing stored' as 'the holder failed'
failures.fix_summary: A waiter that finds a holdback logged since it started gets the same 409 and does not generate
failures.prevention_notes: generation-gate.dbtest.ts PBQ waiter test

failures.title: Review reported 'nothing due' when reviews were due but none could be prepared, and left an empty session
failures.symptom: Due items, no question could be written: the app said nothing was due
failures.root_cause: startSession returned null for an empty session, the same answer as 'nothing due'
failures.fix_summary: Returns session null with unavailable N and a message; the empty session row is removed; the app shows 'couldn't be prepared' with Try again
failures.prevention_notes: mastery-honesty.dbtest.ts FAIL-1016

failures.title: Two requests for one unit check each wrote and paid for a check
failures.symptom: Concurrent requests both found nothing unseen and both called the model
failures.root_cause: No single-flight on unit-check writing
failures.fix_summary: Writing takes the learner's lease for the unit (the PBQ lease); waiters serve what was stored or get the holder's 409
failures.prevention_notes: generation-gate.dbtest.ts unit check tests

failures.title: Rate-limit messages showed internal event names
failures.symptom: 'Too many lesson_regenerate attempts. Try again later.'
failures.root_cause: The message was built from the event name
failures.fix_summary: One plain sentence
failures.prevention_notes: generation-gate.test.ts

failures.title: A bad date on course create was a 500
failures.symptom: sourceVerifiedAt 'soon' reached the INSERT and failed with Postgres 22007
failures.root_cause: No validation of the two date fields; 22007/22008 were not client-input codes
failures.fix_summary: isCalendarDate check with 400 naming the field; 22007 and 22008 answer 400
failures.prevention_notes: generation-gate.test.ts isCalendarDate

failures.title: A lab step counted a graded use that was not given back when nothing was stored
failures.symptom: The use is counted before grading; a failed write or a replayed copy kept it
failures.root_cause: Release only on a grader throw
failures.fix_summary: releaseOnce; released on grader throw, write failure and replay
failures.prevention_notes: generation-gate.test.ts source checks

failures.title: Sim reasoning kept its counted use when the grader threw
failures.symptom: gradeSimReasoning threw after the use was counted
failures.root_cause: Release only on the grader's own failed flag
failures.fix_summary: releaseOnce; released on throw, write failure and a stored duplicate
failures.prevention_notes: generation-gate.test.ts source checks

failures.title: Grading claim expired at 120 s while PBQ grading may run 180 s
failures.symptom: A slow live grade could be taken over and graded twice
failures.root_cause: CLAIM_EXPIRY_SECONDS below the longest grading route
failures.fix_summary: 200 s, and a test keeps it above the longest grading route's maxDuration
failures.prevention_notes: generation-gate.test.ts

failures.title: Two copies of one chat message each paid for a reply
failures.symptom: Racing copies passed the stored-reply check and both called the model
failures.root_cause: No in-flight claim on the chat message id
failures.fix_summary: withGradingClaim on chat:<message id>; waiters replay the stored reply
failures.prevention_notes: generation-gate.test.ts source check

failures.title: The global AI ceiling could be passed by a stale cached sum
failures.symptom: Cached 60 s per instance
failures.root_cause: The check reads a cached sum and takes no lock
failures.fix_summary: Fresh read within 20% of the ceiling; documented as soft with headroom (a lock on every model call was judged too large)
failures.prevention_notes: docs/billing.md section

failures.title: A sprint or mock whose every item was held back said 'no practice questions yet'
failures.symptom: Questions were written and held back; the learner was told there were none
failures.root_cause: The session did not know items were held
failures.fix_summary: generateForObjective reports held and unchecked; the session says every question was held back, or could not be checked
failures.prevention_notes: generation-gate.dbtest.ts FAIL-1025

failures.title: Generated labs were held back on any listed claim, and a failed checker call was logged as a holdback
failures.symptom: A lab whose writer listed a harmless claim (or whose checker could not confirm one) was held back with no retry; a checker call that threw was written to item_holdbacks as fact_check_error, as if the lab had failed
failures.how_detected: Nick asked on 2026-11-10 for labs to follow the same rule as the other generated items
failures.root_cause: lab-generation.ts predated the REQ-216 gate: saveGeneratedLab used uncertaintyOf (any listed claim), judgeLabCheck published only on zero reasons including unsupportedClaims, had no steered retry, and treated a thrown checker as a verdict on the lab
failures.fix_summary: saveGeneratedLab runs on generateGated: holds only on low confidence, a content rule (new problemsOf, reason invalid) or a checker disagreement (labCheckVerdict); one steered retry via modelLabWriter; held twice returns a plain-words outcome (describeSaveOutcome); a failed or empty checker call is held_check_error, retryable, no holdback row
failures.prevention_notes: labs.dbtest.ts: listed and unconfirmed claims store, the retry is steered once, a thrown checker leaves no holdback row; ai-spend-gate.test.ts registers the new operator-only writer call

failures.title: Lab key-suspect flag test slept a fixed 200 ms
failures.symptom: CI Database job failed once on PR #130: item_flags row not yet written when checked
failures.root_cause: The key-suspect flag is written after the response; the test waited a fixed 200 ms instead of for the row
failures.fix_summary: Poll for the flag row (up to 5 s) instead of a fixed sleep

failures.title: Emailed sign-in codes shared the five-an-hour per-address mail budget with reset and verification mails
failures.symptom: Someone who knew an email-only account's password (or, for the reverse direction, anyone who knew the address) could use up the five-an-hour per-address mail budget, after which the learner's sign-in codes answered 429 for up to an hour; sign-in codes in turn used up the budget password-reset links needed.
failures.how_detected: Review of batch G4 (REQ-219); approved follow-up
failures.root_cause: REQ-219 (FAIL-1114) put the sign-in code route under mayEmail, whose single counter (auth_events event mail_to_address, keyed by address) every address-targeted mail shares. Reset and verification routes are open to anyone who knows an address, so a stranger could spend the one shared budget.
failures.fix_summary: mayEmailSignInCode: its own event (mfa_code_mail_to), five an hour per address, same auth_events storage and key; the route uses it, mayEmail is unchanged for every other mail. No migration.
regression_tests: backend/lib/accounts-security-g4.dbtest.ts::FAIL-1240: sign-in codes have their own hourly mail budget
failures.prevention_notes: Each kind of mail that someone other than the account holder can trigger, and each that the holder needs in order to get in, has its own named per-address budget in lib/auth/mailLimit.ts; a new mail kind picks one on purpose. The checklist's auth-and-abuse line names it.

failures.title: A 403 terms_required showed as error text with no way to the Terms screen
failures.symptom: Since REQ-219 the server answers signed-in routes with 403 { code: terms_required } until the account accepts the current Terms and Privacy Policy. A build whose launch prompt never ran (the onboarding request failed or the state was stale) showed the server's sentence as error text on every screen and never opened the Terms screen, so the learner could not act on it.
failures.how_detected: Review of batch G4 (REQ-219); approved follow-up
failures.root_cause: Only the launch gate (GET /api/onboarding, read once per sign-in) opened the Terms screen. The API client had a hook for study_notice_required (FAIL-1061) that reloads that state, but nothing for terms_required, added server-side in REQ-219 without the matching client path.
failures.fix_summary: isTermsRequired and registerTermsRequiredHook: the client hands a 403 terms_required to the onboarding provider, which reloads the launch state (one reload at a time, and none when the state already says the Terms are waiting); the gate then opens /agree. Nothing is retried. JavaScript only.
failures.prevention_notes: A refusal code the server adds for a state the app's launch gate owns (terms_required, study_notice_required) gets a client hook in the same change; the checklist's legal-version line says so, and mobile/src/lib/termsRequired.test.ts checks the wiring.
